name: Transfer GB Residence Document to New Passport
description: Service to transfer a GB residence document (Aufenthaltsdokument-GB) from an expired passport to a new passport.
eligibility: Main residence in Berlin; personal appointment required. Transfers are conducted at citizen offices (Bürgerämter) or the State Office for Immigration (Landesamt für Einwanderung) only by appointment. For transfer at a citizen office, you must: possess the expired passport; have received the GB residence document from the State Office for Immigration Berlin; have no more than 12 months between the expiration date of the old passport and the issuance date of the new passport; and have not continuously left Germany for longer than 12 months. If any of these conditions are not met (e.g., old passport is missing, GB residence document was issued by a different authority), the State Office for Immigration is responsible for the transfer.
requiredDocuments: Your new passport
Your old passport (or police report if stolen)
Your GB residence document, if applicable with additional sheet

1 current biometric passport photo (as of 01.05.2025, biometric photos must be created digitally at authorities or photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic means; check the State Office for Immigration website for current requirements)

name: Transfer of residence permit to new passport
description: This service allows eligible residents to transfer their valid residence permit from an expired passport to a new passport.
eligibility: Personal appointment required. You must have your primary residence in Berlin. You can apply at any Berlin citizens' office (Bürgeramt) if: you possess the expired passport with a valid residence permit; the residence permit was issued by the immigration authority or last transferred by a Berlin citizens' office; your old passport is complete; no more than 6 months have passed between the expiration date of the old passport and the issuance date of the new passport; you have not continuously left Germany for longer than 6 months. If any of these conditions are not met (for example, if your old passport is no longer available or the residence permit was not issued by Berlin immigration authorities), the State Office for Immigration (Landesamt für Einwanderung) is responsible for the transfer.
requiredDocuments: Your new passport
Your old passport (or, if your passport was stolen and you filed a police report, bring the police report)
Your residence permit: Electronic residence permit (eAT) together with the supplementary sheet, or your old passport with the affixed residence permit

1 current biometric passport photo (new regulation as of 01.05.2025 — as of this date, biometric passport photos may only be created digitally by authorities or photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic means; check the State Office for Immigration website before your appointment for current details)

name: Extend Residence Permit on Humanitarian Grounds

This service does not apply if you hold a residence permit under § 24 AufenthG for refugees from Ukraine. You must have a main residence in Berlin (a secondary residence is not sufficient). The humanitarian ground must still be applicable. You must possess a valid passport or travel document of your country of origin, or demonstrate that obtaining one is not reasonably possible. You must have a current email address and consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal) for fees.

Electronic health card copy (front and back) or current health insurance confirmation (if insured with statutory health insurance)

name: Residence permit for persons with a right of return
description: A residence permit issued to foreign nationals who were previously lawfully resident in Germany for at least eight years and have since left, provided they meet specific eligibility criteria including age, residency history, and financial requirements.
eligibility: Applicant must be between 15 and 21 years old at time of application and apply within five years of departure. Must have been lawfully resident in Germany for at least eight years before departure, or have acquired a recognized school diploma there. Must have attended school in Germany for at least six years before departure. Livelihood must be secured through own employment or a support commitment from another person for at least five years. Special provisions apply for victims of forced marriage with relaxed requirements if application is made within three months of the forced situation ending, or within five years of departure. Primary residence must be in Berlin. In-person appointment required.
requiredDocuments: Application for issuance of a residence title (completed) available in German, English, French, Italian, Greek, Turkish, Vietnamese, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Serbian, and Bosnian
Valid passport or passport substitute
One current biometric photograph (as of 01.05.2025, biometric photos may only be created digitally by authorities or photo studios and submitted via secure electronic transmission)
All German school certificates and diplomas (original and copy)

Proof of livelihood (original and copy): If support commitment from third party, that person must provide employment contract and current employer confirmation of employment (not older than 14 days) and last six pay statements (for employees), or audit report from tax advisor/auditor with supporting documents such as trade register extract (for self-employed), rental agreement or proof of property ownership, and passport or ID card; if securing livelihood from own means, provide proof of intended employment with expected income, rental agreement or proof of property ownership, and health insurance
Proof of primary residence in Berlin: Registration confirmation (residence registration certificate) or rental agreement and landlord's move-in confirmation
fees: 100.00 EUR for issuance of residence permit; 93.00 EUR for extension of residence permit; 46.00 EUR maximum for Turkish nationals
processingTime: Approximately 4 weeks after the in-person appointment until the residence permit is issued as an electronic residence title and can be collected.

name: Apply for Residence Permit for a Foreign Parent's Child
description: This service allows eligible foreign parents to apply for a residence permit for their minor child to join them in Berlin under family reunification provisions.
eligibility: At least one parent must hold a valid residence title (Niederlassungserlaubnis, Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt-EU, Aufenthaltserlaubnis, Blaue Karte EU, ICT-Karte, or Mobiler ICT-Karte); family reunification is not possible if parents hold certain other residence permits based on subsidiary protection or specific legal grounds (§ 25 Abs. 2, § 25 Abs. 4, 4b, 5, § 25a Abs. 2, § 25b Abs. 4, § 104a-104c AufenthG). The child must already be in Germany with a valid residence title or residence authorization, or be eligible to enter visa-free and apply for a permit. The child must be a minor at time of application (with exceptions for asylum-eligible children based on parent's asylum application date). For children aged 16-17 not moving with parents, a positive integration prognosis may be required unless parents hold employment or humanitarian permits. The child's living costs must be covered without state benefits (SGB II, XII, or asylum benefits), unless exceptions apply. The child must have adequate health insurance in Germany. The family must have sufficient living space. No deportation interest must exist, and the child must not pose a security risk or be involved in violence for political/religious purposes. The family must have their main residence in Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Online application form for residence permit based on family reasons (online only); you will receive a PDF confirmation that your child's current residence title remains valid beyond its expiration date in Germany
Power of attorney with description of the matter (if applying through a representative)

Identity documents of parents with custody: copy of passport or ID of the sole custodial parent; if both parents have joint custody, also a signed declaration of consent and copy of passport or ID of the other parent
Copy of child's residence permit or other German residence title (if already held)
Passport copies in color: data pages (with photo and personal information); if first-time application after entry, also entry stamp and visa or other EU state residence title (if in passport)
Birth certificate
Proof of custody (especially if one parent does not live in Germany)
Current school certificate (if child is of school age)
Income documentation for employed parents: employment contract; net salary documentation for last 6 months (pay stubs, bank statements); current employer certification (not older than 14 days)

Income documentation for self-employed or freelance parents: most recent tax assessment; completed audit report form with supporting documents (completed by tax advisor, certified accountant, or tax agent); tax office certification; for self-employed: commercial register extract or business registration (if no register entry required); for freelancers: registration as freelancer with tax office and chamber registration (if required)

Income documentation for non-working parents: examples include unemployment benefit notification; pension or retirement notification; proof of assets; Bürgergeld, social assistance, or asylum benefit notification; BAföG or vocational training allowance; other benefits (parental allowance, child allowance, housing allowance, child tax allowance, orphan's pension/allowance, integration allowance, maintenance payment documentation)

Housing documentation: for rental: lease agreement (without house rules or annexes); proof of current monthly costs including utilities (warm rent), such as bank statements; for owned property: land register extract (Section 3); monthly building maintenance costs; any monthly mortgage costs

Health insurance documentation: for statutory health insurance: electronic health card (color copies of front and back) or current insurance confirmation; for private health insurance: insurer certification of coverage scope and costs per § 257 Abs. 2a SGB V (inform insurer it is needed for family reunification residence permit)
fees: €50.00 for initial residence permit issuance; €46.50 for residence permit extension; €27.60 for Turkish nationals (both initial and extension); free for those unable to support living costs without SGB II, XII, or asylum benefits (current jobcenter or welfare office confirmation required); €6.00 additional for digital photo creation at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: Minimum 4 weeks after in-person appointment until the residence permit is issued as an electronic residence document and ready for collection

name: Request residence permit for minor child of German citizen
description: This service allows you to apply for a residence permit for your minor child who has at least one German parent and does not hold German citizenship.
eligibility: The child must be a minor, unmarried, and not possess German citizenship. At least one parent must have German citizenship and maintain a family household with the child. There must be no deportation interests or pending criminal proceedings. The child must not pose a threat to Germany's democratic order or security, and must not be involved in violence or publicly advocate for violence for political or religious purposes. The primary residence must be in Berlin (a secondary residence is not sufficient). You must provide a current email address, and for online applications, consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal).
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit on family grounds (online only)
PDF confirmation document of application
Power of attorney with specification of matter (if application submitted by proxy)
Copy of passport or ID of sole-custody parent (if applicable)
Signed consent declaration and copy of passport or ID of other custody-holding parent (if parents jointly have custody)
Copy of existing residence permit or other German residence title (if child already possesses one)

Passport copies in color: data pages with photo and personal information (always required); entry stamp and entry visa or residence title from another EU state in passport (if child is entering for the first time and applying for first residence permit)
Birth certificate
Current school certificate (if child is of school age)
Most recent benefits approval notice (if receiving benefits under SGB II or XII or Asylum Seeker Benefits Act)
fees: €50.00 for initial issuance of residence permit; €46.50 for extension of residence permit; €27.60 for Turkish nationals (for both initial issuance and extension); no fees for foreigners unable to support themselves without benefits under SGB II or XII or Asylum Seeker Benefits Act (current job center or social welfare office confirmation required); €6.00 additional for digital passport photo creation at self-service terminal on-site.
processingTime: After an in-person appointment, it takes a minimum of 4 weeks before the residence permit is issued as a digital residence title and can be picked up.

name: Residence Permit for Foreign Spouse of a Foreigner
description: This service allows the foreign spouse or registered life partner of a foreigner with a valid residence permit to apply for their own residence permit in Germany.
eligibility: Your spouse or registered life partner must hold a valid residence permit under the Residence Act (AufenthG), such as a settlement permit, EU long-term residence permit, residence permit, Blue Card EU, ICT card, or mobile ICT card. Spousal reunification is not possible if your spouse holds a residence permit under specific legal grounds (§ 25 Abs. 2 Satz 1 Alt. 2, § 25 Abs. 4, 4b or 5, § 25a Abs. 2, § 25b Abs. 4, § 104a Abs. 1 Satz 1, § 104b or § 104c AufenthG). You must already reside in Germany with a valid residence permit or pending residence application, or enter visa-free and apply, or hold a toleration certificate (Duldung) and be married in Germany. Your marriage or registered partnership must be legally valid. Both spouses must be at least 18 years old. Basic German language skills (A1 level) are generally required. Your livelihood and that of dependents must be secured through your own income without relying on social welfare benefits (Bürgergeld, social assistance), with exceptions for spouses holding permits on humanitarian grounds. You must have adequate health insurance in Germany (statutory or comparable private insurance). Adequate housing for you and household members is required, with exceptions if your spouse holds employment or humanitarian permits. You must have no deportation interest: no criminal proceedings, no threat to democratic order or German security, and no participation in violence for political or religious purposes. Your primary residence must be in Berlin with your spouse (secondary residence is not sufficient).
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit on family grounds (online only); you will receive a PDF confirmation document certifying that your current residence permit remains valid beyond its expiration date (does not apply if you hold a Schengen visa C or your permit expired on the application date); save and print this document
Power of attorney with description of proceedings (if applying through an authorized representative)
Copy of your residence permit (if you already hold a German residence permit or other residence title for Germany)
Colored passport copies: data pages with photo and personal information (always required); entry stamp and visa or other EU state residence permit in passport (if applicable and first application)
Copy of spouse's or partner's passport, passport replacement document, or travel document
Marriage certificate or registered partnership certificate; if foreign, provide certified translation; may also require apostille or legalization depending on origin country

Proof of basic German language skills: language certificate at A1 level of CEFR or equivalent/higher diploma; or German test for immigrants (Deutschtest für Zuwanderer); or integration course final test

Employment income documentation (if employed): employment contract; proof of net salary for last 6 months (salary certificates, bank statements); current employer certification (not older than 14 days)

Self-employment/freelance income documentation (if applicable): latest tax assessment; completed audit report form with supporting documents (must be completed by tax advisor, auditor, or tax agent); tax office certification; for self-employed: trade register extract or business registration; for freelancers: registration as freelancer with tax office and chamber registration (if required)

Non-employment income documentation (if not employed): unemployment benefit I decision; pension or retirement decision; proof of assets; decision on Bürgergeld, social assistance, or asylum seeker benefits receipt; BAföG or vocational training allowance

Additional income documentation as applicable to your situation: parental allowance, child allowance, housing allowance, child tax credit, orphan pension or benefits, startup allowance, maintenance payment documentation

Proof of housing size and costs: for rental: lease agreement (without house rules); proof of current monthly costs (warm rent) such as bank statements; for owned property: land register extract (Section 3); monthly house management costs; possibly monthly mortgage costs

Health insurance documentation: statutory insurance: electronic health card (copies of front and back) or current insurance confirmation; private insurance: insurer's certification of coverage scope and costs under § 257 Abs. 2a SGB V (inform insurer this is needed for family reunion residence permit)
fees: €100.00 for initial issuance of residence permit; €93.00 for renewal; €27.60 for Turkish nationals up to age 24 (issuance/renewal); €46.00 for Turkish nationals age 24 and over (issuance/renewal); no fee for those unable to support themselves without SGB II/XII or asylum seeker benefits (current jobcenter or social office confirmation required); €6.00 additional for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: At least 4 weeks after your in-person appointment until the residence permit is issued as an electronic residence title and ready for collection

name: Apply for Residence Permit as Foreign Spouse of a German Citizen
description: This service allows foreign spouses or registered life partners of German citizens to apply for a residence permit in Berlin, provided they meet eligibility requirements including valid residency status, marriage validity, basic German language skills, and security clearance.
eligibility: Your spouse or registered life partner holds German nationality. Your current residence status entitles you to obtain a residence permit: you either already reside in Germany with a valid residence title or residence authorization, or you are entitled by your nationality to apply for a residence permit following visa-free entry, or you hold a suspension of deportation (Duldung) under § 60a AufenthG and were married in Germany. Your marriage or same-sex registered partnership was validly concluded. Both spouses or registered partners must generally be at least 18 years old. You typically possess basic German language skills (level A1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages). No deportation interests: no criminal fines or ongoing criminal investigations; you pose no threat to Germany's free democratic order or security; you are not involved in violence for political or religious purposes and do not publicly incite or threaten violence. You have your principal residence in Berlin together with your German spouse or registered partner (a secondary residence is insufficient). You provide a current email address, as the Immigration Office will contact you by email. For online application: you consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal).
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit on family grounds (online only); you will receive a PDF confirmation that your current residence title remains valid beyond its previous expiration date (does not apply if you hold a Schengen visa C for short-term stay or your current residence title has already expired); you must save and print this document
Power of attorney with specification of the matter if applying through a representative
Copy of your residence title if you already possess a German residence permit or other German residence title for Germany

Passport copies in colour: data pages (with your photo and personal information) always required; if you are entering for the first time and applying for a residence permit, additionally: entry stamp and visa for entry or residence title of another EU state in passport (if applicable)
Copy of the German passport or national ID card of your German spouse or registered partner

Marriage certificate or registered partnership certificate; for foreign documents, a certified translation must be provided; depending on country of origin, an apostille or legalization may also be required

Proof of basic German language skills: language certificate with overall result A1 of the GER or equivalent or higher language diploma, or Deutschtest für Zuwanderer (German test for immigrants), or integration course final test
Most recent benefit decision if receiving benefits under SGB II or XII or the Asylum Seekers' Benefits Act
fees: €100.00 for first issuance of residence permit; €93.00 for extension of residence permit; €27.60 for Turkish nationals up to age 24 for first issuance or extension; €46.00 for Turkish nationals age 24 and above for first issuance or extension; no fees for foreigners unable to support themselves without benefits under SGB II or XII or Asylum Seekers' Benefits Act (current decision from job centre or social office required); €6.00 additionally for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: After your scheduled appointment, it takes a minimum of 4 weeks until the residence permit is issued as an electronic residence title and can be collected.

name: Residence Permit for Au-pair Employment
description: This service allows individuals aged 18-26 to apply for a residence permit in Berlin to work as an au-pair with a host family that speaks German as a native language.
eligibility: You must be 18-26 years old at time of application; hold a valid residence title or national D-visa, or be eligible to apply visa-free; have basic German language skills (A1 level); not have previously worked as an au-pair in Germany for one year; the host family must live in Berlin and speak German as their native or family language; you must obtain approval from the Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit); have adequate health insurance; and present no security risks to public order or the constitutional democratic order of Germany or the security of the Federal Republic.

name: Apply for Residence Permit for Working Holiday or Youth Mobility Program
description: This service allows citizens of Australia, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, Canada, and South Korea to apply for a residence permit to participate in working holiday or youth mobility exchange programs in Germany.
eligibility: Applicants must be nationals of Australia, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, Canada, or South Korea with a valid working holiday or youth mobility agreement with Germany; be between 18-35 years old (age limits vary by country: 18-30 for Australia/Israel/Japan/New Zealand, 18-34 for South Korea, 18-35 for Canada); have main residence in Berlin; apply within 90 days of entry to Germany (except South Korea nationals who may apply in exceptional cases only); have no indicators of endangering public safety or order; provide a current email address; and consent to electronic payment methods for online applications.

name: Request Residence Permit for Voluntary Service Participation
description: This service allows eligible foreign nationals to apply for a residence permit in order to participate in an approved voluntary service program in Germany.
eligibility: You must have a valid residence permit or other residence title (such as a national D-visa) or be eligible to apply visa-free. Age requirements vary by program: Youth Voluntary Service (under 27 years), Federal Voluntary Service (no age limit), or European Voluntary Service (17-30 years). School attendance requirements from your home country must be met. For European Voluntary Service, you must be a national of an Erasmus+ partner country. You must have a written agreement with the voluntary service provider, secured means of subsistence during your stay, adequate health insurance, no grounds for endangering public security or order, and a main residence in Berlin during the service.

name: Apply for Residence Permit for Employment in Research
description: This service allows eligible foreign researchers already in Germany to apply for a residence permit that authorizes employment at a recognized research facility.
eligibility: You must already be lawfully resident in Germany with a valid residence permit or other residence title (such as a national D visa), or be eligible to apply following visa-free entry based on your nationality. Applications may be submitted no earlier than 4 months before expiration of your current national D visa or residence permit. You must be employed at a recognized research facility (including those recognized by the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees, companies or private institutions conducting research jointly with public institutions, or spin-offs from public research institutions). You must provide either a host agreement or employment contract and a cost assumption declaration (unless the research facility is publicly funded or has already provided a general declaration). You must have adequate health insurance in Germany (statutory or comparable private insurance). You must present no indicators of endangering public security or order, including no prior criminal convictions, no ongoing criminal proceedings at the time of application, and no involvement in violence for political or religious purposes. You must maintain your main residence in Berlin during the research employment period.
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for research employment (online only); you will receive a PDF confirmation document certifying that your current residence title remains valid in Germany beyond its previous expiration date (not applicable if you hold a Schengen visa or your current title has already expired)
Power of attorney with specification of the matter (if applying through an authorized representative)
Copy of your residence title (if you already possess a residence permit or other German residence title)

name: Residence Permit for School-Based Vocational Training
description: This service allows foreign nationals to apply for a residence permit in Berlin to pursue state-recognized vocational training at accredited educational institutions.
eligibility: You must pursue training leading to a state-recognized vocational qualification at an accredited institution (vocational school, technical academy, technical gymnasium, vocational or health sciences school, or private recognized supplementary school). name: Apply for Residence Permit for Skilled Workers with Academic Qualifications
description: This service allows skilled workers with university degrees to apply for a residence permit in Germany to work in their profession.
eligibility: You must have lawful residence in Germany with a valid residence permit or other residence title (such as a national D visa), or be eligible to apply for a residence permit after visa-free entry based on your nationality. Application can be made earliest 4 months before your national D visa or current employment residence permit expires. You must have an employment contract or concrete job offer already in place, at minimum a draft. Your employment must be in Germany and your employer must have a business location in Germany. The Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) must have approved your employment. If your profession requires a professional license (e.g., doctors, engineers), you must have or be promised this license before the residence permit is issued. You must hold a German university degree, a recognized foreign university degree, or a foreign university degree equivalent to a German one; you can check recognition in the Anabin database or request an individual evaluation from the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB) if needed. If you are over 45 years old, you must have adequate retirement provision, meaning your salary must be at least 55% of the annual assessment limit in general pension insurance (€4,647.50 gross per month for 2026), unless you already have adequate retirement provision from other public or private sources. You must have adequate health insurance in Germany, either statutory or private insurance comparable to German standards; foreign insurance is generally not sufficient. You must have no indicators of endangering public safety or order; even fines can prevent permit issuance, and you cannot be under investigation, must not endanger the free democratic basic order or security of Germany, and must not participate in violence or call for violence for political or religious purposes. You must have your main residence in Berlin (a secondary residence is insufficient). You must provide a current email address for the State Office for Immigration to contact you. For online applications, you must consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal).
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for employment as a skilled worker (online only); you will receive a PDF confirmation that your current residence title remains valid beyond its previous expiration date within Germany (not applicable if you hold a Schengen visa for short-term stay or your current residence title has already expired on the application date); please save and print this document
Power of attorney specifying the subject matter of the proceeding (if applying through an authorized representative)
Copy of your residence title (if you already have a residence permit or other German residence title for Germany)

Your employment contract or job offer

Proof of qualification as a skilled worker with academic education: German university degree and diploma, or recognized foreign university degree with Anabin database assessment, or foreign university degree comparable to a German university degree with individual paid ZAB assessment
Completed and signed Employment Relationship Declaration form (Formular Erklärung zum Beschäftigungsverhältnis) from your employer
Professional license if required (only if specified in eligibility requirements)

name: Apply for Residence Permit for Skilled Workers with Vocational Training
description: This service allows skilled workers with completed vocational training to apply for a residence permit in Germany for employment purposes.
eligibility: You must have lawful residence in Germany (with a national D-visa or other residence title, or be eligible to apply visa-free); you must already have a valid employment contract or concrete job offer; the employment must be in Germany with the employer's business location in Germany; you must have approval from the German Federal Employment Agency (Bundesagentur für Arbeit); you must hold a German vocational qualification after at least 2 years of training or a recognized equivalent foreign qualification; if you are 45 years or older, you must have adequate retirement provisions (minimum monthly gross income of €4,647.50 for 2026, equivalent to 55% of the annual assessment threshold in general pension insurance); you must have adequate health insurance (statutory or comparable private insurance in Germany); you must have no indicators of endangering public safety or order (criminal convictions or pending investigations can prevent issuance); you must have your main residence in Berlin (a secondary residence is not sufficient); you must provide a current email address; for online application, you must consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal); application is possible earliest 4 months before expiration of your national D-visa or current employment residence permit.
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for employment as skilled worker (online only)
PDF confirmation document of your application (demonstrating continued validity of current residence title)
Power of attorney with specification of subject matter (only if applying through a representative)
Copy of your residence title (if you already have a German residence permit or other residence title for federal territory)

fees: €56.00 for initial issuance as sticker; €49.00 for renewal as sticker; €100.00 for initial issuance as electronic residence permit; €93.00 for renewal as electronic residence permit; €27.60 for Turkish nationals up to age 24 for initial issuance or renewal; €46.00 for Turkish nationals age 24 and above for initial issuance or renewal; €6.00 additional for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on-site

name: Residence Permit for Well-Integrated Youth or Young Adults with Toleration Status or Opportunity Residence Permit
description: This service allows young people aged 14-26 with toleration or opportunity residence status to apply for a residence permit if they meet integration criteria including education, financial stability, and positive integration prospects.
eligibility: You must be at least 14 and not yet 27 years old (age limits do not apply to close family members). You must have continuously resided in Germany for at least 3 years with toleration, temporary residence, or residence permit status (does not apply to close family members). You must possess either a valid residence permit under § 104c of the Residence Act or have held toleration status for at least 12 months (does not apply to close family members). Your identity must be clarified and you must hold a valid passport or travel document. You must have successfully attended school in Germany for 3 years or acquired a recognized school or vocational qualification in Germany (exception granted for physical, mental, or psychological illness or disability; does not apply to close family members). Your livelihood must be secured or you must currently be in school, vocational training, or university studies (does not apply to minor children or siblings). You must have a positive integration prognosis (youth or adult criminal sentences generally preclude this; for close family members, sentences of up to 50 or 90 daily rates for immigration or asylum law violations exclude eligibility). You must affirm commitment to the free democratic basic order of Germany and possess basic knowledge of German law, social order, and living conditions. You must have your main residence in Berlin (a secondary residence is insufficient). You must provide a current email address. You must have submitted the online application for the residence permit for integrated toleration or opportunity residence permit holders.
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for well-integrated youth or young adults (online only; you will receive a PDF confirmation which you must save and print if possible)
Power of attorney with specification of the subject matter (if applying through a representative)

Documents regarding guardians (if parents apply for a minor child): If one parent has sole custody: Copy of sole custodian's passport; If both parents have joint custody: Signed consent declaration and copy of other parent's passport
Copies of passport or travel document in color (data pages with photo and personal information)
If employed: Employment contract, net salary statements for last 6 months (earnings statements), and current employer certification (not older than 14 days)

If self-employed or freelance: Latest tax assessment notice, completed audit report form with required documents (must be completed by tax advisor, auditor, or tax representative), tax office certification, and business registration excerpt or commercial registration (for self-employed) or professional registration with tax office and chamber membership (for freelancers)

If not employed: Proof of livelihood such as unemployment benefit I decision, pension or retirement decision, proof of assets, citizen's allowance or social welfare decision, asylum seeker benefits decision, BAföG or vocational training assistance
Additional benefit documents if applicable (parental allowance, child allowance, housing allowance, child supplement, orphan pension, startup allowance, or proof of maintenance payments)

For students, trainees, or university students: School grades, school certification, training certification and contract, or university enrollment certification; current participation certificate for state-subsidized vocational preparation measure (if applicable)
Other integration evidence (social engagement in associations or social institutions)
Lease agreement with proof of current rent amount

Health insurance proof: For statutory insurance: electronic health card copy (front and back) or current confirmation; For private insurance: insurer's certification of coverage scope and costs under § 257 Section 2a SGB V (inform insurer the certification is needed for humanitarian residence permit)
fees: 100.00 EUR for adults; 50.00 EUR for minors; Free if you receive benefits under SGB II or XII or the Asylum Seeker Benefits Act (current job center or welfare office decision must be provided as proof); 6.00 EUR additional for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on site
processingTime: Due to very high application volume, processing may take considerable time. After positive application review, you will receive an appointment for an in-person interview. After the interview appointment, it takes approximately 4-6 weeks for the residence permit to be issued as a digital residence title and available for pickup.

name: Request Residence Permit for Child Born in Germany
description: A residence permit service for children born in Germany whose parents hold valid residence titles issued in Berlin.
eligibility: The child must have been born in Germany and registered in Berlin together with parents or sole legal guardian. Both parents (or sole legal guardian) must hold a valid residence title (residence permit, Blue Card-EU, settlement permit, or EU permanent residence permit) at the time of the child's birth. The parents' residence titles must have been issued in Berlin and must remain valid for more than 6 months. A personal appointment with a legal guardian and the child is required. If these conditions are not met, the application must be submitted to the State Office for Immigration (LEA).
requiredDocuments: Child's passport (valid passport in child's own name or entry in valid passport of a parent)
One current biometric passport photograph (new regulation as of 01.05.2025 — photos must be created digitally at authorities or photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic means)
Birth certificate
Passports and residence titles of parents

name: Residence Permit for Long-term Residents from Other EU Member States
description: A residence permit for non-German EU citizens who hold long-term resident status (Daueraufenthalt-EG or Daueraufenthalt-EU) in another EU member state and wish to establish their main residence in Berlin.
eligibility: You must hold the legal status of a long-term resident in another EU member state with a residence title designated 'Daueraufenthalt-EG' or 'Daueraufenthalt-EU' issued under EU Directive 2003/109/EG from 25 November 2003. An unlimited residence title without this designation is generally insufficient. In exceptional cases, proof of long-term resident status may be provided through written confirmation from the authorities of another EU member state, but a residence permit may only be issued at the discretion of the German authorities. You must have your main residence in Berlin and must appear in person at a scheduled appointment.

Evidence of secured means of subsistence (e.g., employment contract, blocked account, or declaration of commitment for students, bank statements for the last 3 months)
Documentation of the intended purpose of residence (e.g., certificate of enrolment or employment offer and employment contract)

Declaration regarding employment relationship form (completed where applicable; residence permit for employment purposes can generally only be issued with consent from the German Federal Employment Agency)
Health insurance
Proof of main residence in Berlin (registration certificate or rental contract and landlord's confirmation of move-in)
fees: €100.00 for initial issuance of residence permit; €93.00 for each renewal of residence permit; €50.00 for initial issuance of residence permit for minors; €46.50 for each renewal of residence permit for minors; €27.60 for applicants up to age 24; €46.00 for applicants from age 24 onwards
processingTime: Approximately 4 weeks after your scheduled appointment until the residence permit is issued as an electronic residence title and ready for collection.

bookingInfo.office: This service can only be accessed at the State Office for Immigration (LEA) at the Keplerstraße location in Berlin.

name: Apply for Residence Permit for Sustainably Integrated Persons with Toleration or Opportunity Residence Permit
description: This service allows persons with toleration or an opportunity residence permit who meet integration requirements to apply for a residence permit in Germany.
eligibility: You must have been continuously tolerated, permitted, or holding a residence permit in Germany for several years. The required duration depends on your situation: 30 months if you have held toleration for employment under § 60d of the Residence Act for at least 30 months; 4 years if you live together with a minor unmarried child; 6 years in all other cases. You must possess either toleration or a valid residence permit under § 104c of the Residence Act. Your identity must be clarified. You must possess a valid passport or passport substitute. You must affirm your commitment to the free democratic constitutional order of the Federal Republic of Germany and possess basic knowledge of the legal and social order and living conditions in Germany. Your livelihood must be substantially secured or will be fully secured in the future (this requirement may be waived if you cannot meet it due to physical, mental, or psychological illness or disability, or due to age; temporary receipt of social benefits is generally not a problem if you are studying, in recognized vocational training, or in state-sponsored vocational preparation measures; or if you are a family with minor children temporarily dependent on supplementary social assistance; or if you are a single parent caring for a child under 3 years; or if you care for close family members in need of care). You must possess sufficient oral German language skills at level A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (this requirement is waived for children under 6 years old and adults over 65 years, or if you cannot meet it due to physical, mental, or psychological illness or disability). If you have a school-aged child, you must demonstrate their actual school attendance. There must be no indications that you pose a threat to public security or order (even criminal fines can prevent issuance of the residence permit). You must not pose a threat to the free democratic constitutional order or the security of the Federal Republic of Germany. You must not be involved in violence for the pursuit of political or religious goals, must not publicly call for violence, and must not threaten violence. You must have your main residence in Berlin (a secondary residence in Berlin is not sufficient). You must provide a current email address, as the State Office for Immigration will contact you via this address. You must have submitted an online application for the residence permit for integrated persons with toleration or an opportunity residence permit.
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for sustainably integrated persons with toleration or opportunity residence permit (online only); you will receive a PDF document as confirmation of your application — please save and print this document
Power of attorney with specification of the matter (if applying through a representative)
Documents regarding custody for minor children: copy of passport of sole custodial parent, or if parents have joint custody, signed consent declaration and copy of passport of other custodial parent
Copies of passport or passport substitute in color (photo pages and personal data pages)

Proof of oral German language skills at level A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference: Language certificate with overall result A2 of the Common European Framework or equivalent or higher language diploma, or language proficiency certificate level A2, or at least 3 years of successful attendance at a German general education school (promotion to next class and overall grade or average grade of at least 'satisfactory' on last school report), or successful completion of studies at a German-language university or technical college or German-language vocational training leading to recognized professional qualification, or promotion to tenth class of a general education German school, or acquisition of German vocational education maturity or equivalent educational standard or school-leaving certificate of a general education school

Proof of basic knowledge of the legal and social order: Certificate of successfully completed integration course or orientation course 'Test Leben in Deutschland' or citizenship test, or successful attendance at a German general education school for four years with promotion to next class and overall grade or average grade of at least 'satisfactory' on last school report, or promotion to tenth class of a general education German school, or acquisition of German vocational education maturity or equivalent educational standard or school-leaving certificate of a German general education school, or successful completion of German qualified vocational training or having been in corresponding training in Germany for at least one year, or successful completion of studies at a German university or technical college, or receipt of a doctoral degree from a German university, or receipt of state authorization for independent professional practice (Approbation)
If employed: Proof of livelihood — employment contract, proof of net salary for last 6 months (salary statements), current employer certificate (not older than 14 days)

If self-employed or freelance: Proof of livelihood — last tax assessment notice, completed examination report form with attached documents (must be completed by tax advisor, auditor, or tax representative), tax office certificate, trade register extract or business registration for self-employed persons, or registration as freelancer with tax office and chamber registration if required

If not employed: Proof of livelihood — for example, unemployment benefit I notice, pension decision, proof of assets, notice of receipt of Bürgergeld or social assistance or asylum seeker benefits, BAföG or vocational training assistance

Additional proof of benefits depending on your situation: parental allowance, child benefit, housing allowance, child supplement, orphan's pension or benefit, start-up allowance, proof of maintenance payments

For students, trainees, or apprentices: School report cards, school certificate, training certificate and training contract, or university enrollment certificate, or current participation certificate for state-sponsored vocational preparation measure
Rental contract with proof of current rent

Proof of health insurance in Germany: for statutory health insurance — copy of electronic health card (front and back) or current health insurance confirmation; for private health insurance — insurer's certificate of scope and costs of insurance under § 257 Abs. 2a SGB V
Medical certificate from a specialist doctor (if you have physical, mental, or psychological illness or disability)
fees: 100.00 Euro for adults; 50.00 Euro for minors; no fees if you receive benefits under SGB II or XII or the Asylum Seeker Benefits Act (current notice from job center or social office required as proof); 6.00 Euro additional for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: Due to the very high number of applications, processing may take some time. You will receive an appointment for an in-person interview after positive review of your application. After the in-person appointment, it takes approximately 4 to 6 weeks for the residence permit to be issued as a digital residence title and to be available for collection.

description: This service allows non-German residents in Berlin to apply for a residence permit specifically to attend an intensive German language course.

You must have health insurance in Germany (statutory, private, or travel insurance for the duration of the course). You must have your principal residence in Berlin (a secondary residence does not suffice). You must provide a current email address for contact by the Immigration Office (Landesamt für Einwanderung). name: Residence Permit for School Attendance or Student Exchange Participation
description: This service issues a residence permit for foreign students who wish to attend school in Berlin or participate in a student exchange program.
eligibility: For student exchange: The exchange must be organized by a student exchange organization, a youth welfare provider, a German school, or another public institution in cooperation with a school or public institution in the other country. Privately or commercially organized student exchanges are also possible. For school attendance: The school must be either a public or state-recognized school with an international focus, or a school that is not primarily funded by public funds and prepares students for international qualifications, qualifications from other countries, or state-recognized qualifications. All school types must have a mixed composition of students from different nationalities (exceptions may apply for embassy schools). Consent of guardians is required only if the foreign student is not yet of legal age. Main residence must be in Berlin. Personal appointment is required — contact the responsible departments B 1–4 via contact form. Submit appointment requests preferably 8 weeks before the current residence permit expires. For children under 18, the application must be submitted by a supervising adult (host parent) authorized by the parents.

name: Apply for Temporary Residence Permit for Refugees from Ukraine
description: This service allows eligible refugees from Ukraine and their family members to apply for temporary protective residence in Berlin.
eligibility: You must have had your ordinary residence in Ukraine before 24 February 2022 and belong to one of the following groups: Ukrainian nationals; stateless persons and nationals of countries outside the EU/EWR who enjoyed international or equivalent national protection in Ukraine; stateless persons and nationals of countries outside the EU/EWR who can prove they legally resided in Ukraine under an unlimited residence title issued under Ukrainian law; or family members of any of the above persons. You must not already hold a temporary protection residence permit in another EU member state. You must have received an assignment decision for distribution to Berlin from the State Office for Refugee Affairs (LAF) or another reception facility in Germany, for which you received a contact certificate. You must have submitted an online application for temporary protection and attend your scheduled in-person appointment.
requiredDocuments: Online application for temporary protection under § 24 of the Residence Act (only possible online); PDF confirmation document of your application (save and print if possible)
Completed application form for issuance of a residence title (bring to appointment)
Valid identity document (one of the following: valid passport or passport substitute, Ukrainian ID card, or certificate of identity clarification issued by the Ukrainian embassy)
One current biometric photograph per person
Ukrainian residence title (if you do not hold Ukrainian nationality)
Proof of assignment decision for distribution to Berlin (contact certificate from LAF or reception facility)
Marriage certificate or civil partnership certificate (if applicable)
Birth certificate (if applicable) for minor children
Confirmation of your online application for temporary protection (bring printed or digital copy on smartphone)
Appointment confirmation (bring invitation email as print or digital copy on smartphone)
fees: No fee for issuance of the residence permit. Registration fee by age: €60.00 from age 24 onwards; €38.00 until age 24; €14.00 for children until age 12.
processingTime: Due to the very high number of refugees, there may be a delay before you receive your appointment. Processing at in-person appointment: immediate. If an electronic residence title must be issued: 5-6 weeks.

description: This service grants a residence permit to foreign professionals with recognized qualification deficits who are undertaking approved qualifying measures to meet German professional standards.
eligibility: Your professional qualification is not yet recognized. The competent authority responsible for recognizing your professional qualification in Germany has issued a decision (deficit notice) identifying technical, professional practice, or language deficiencies and, in the case of a regulated profession (for example in healthcare), the necessity of adaptation measures or a language course. The qualifying measure must be suitable. For school-based qualifying measures: the education provider must be appropriately qualified — either state-run, state-recognized, or certified according to the Recognition and Approval Regulation for Labor Market Support (AZAV). For primarily workplace-based qualifying measures: approval from the Federal Employment Agency is required (a qualifying measure is primarily workplace-based when more than half the time is spent on workplace/practical activities). You must have secured living expenses of EUR 1,091.20 per month (2026 rate) covering general living costs, rent, and health insurance. You must have sufficient German language skills at level A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference. You must have your main residence in Berlin. You must attend a personal appointment by appointment — contact the responsible department B 6 via the contact form at least 8 weeks before your current residence permit expires.
requiredDocuments: Application form for issuing a residence permit (completed)
Valid passport

Current biometric passport photo (note: as of May 1, 2025, biometric passport photos may only be created digitally directly at government offices or photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic channels)
Deficit notice from the recognition authority
Evidence of sufficient German language skills at level A2
Documentation of the intended qualifying measure
For school-based qualification: evidence regarding the education provider

For workplace-based qualification: documents for Federal Employment Agency participation (employment contract or continuing education contract; completed form 'Declaration of employment relationship'; completed form 'Supplement sheet A' with the training plan mentioned there)

Evidence of living expenses (if living expenses are not secured through employment income: establishment of a blocked account at a German bank or submission of a declaration of commitment to the State Office for Immigration)

Health insurance documentation (for statutory health insurance: electronic health card with photo and current confirmation of health insurance; for private health insurance: proof of paid contributions, for example through bank statements, or insurer's certificate)
Evidence of residence (for example: registration confirmation or rental agreement and landlord's confirmation of move-in)
fees: EUR 100.00 for first-time issuance; EUR 96.00 for extension up to three months; EUR 93.00 for extension of more than three months; EUR 27.60 for those under 24 years old; EUR 46.00 for those 24 years and older
processingTime: Approximately 6 weeks after your scheduled appointment until the residence permit is issued as an electronic residence title and is ready for collection

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — contact department B 6 via the contact form for appointment scheduling

name: Residence Permit for Job Search Following Completion of Education or Work in Germany
description: Apply for a residence permit to search for employment in Germany after successfully completing education, professional qualification recognition, or research work.
eligibility: Valid residence permit; successful completion of education, professional qualification recognition, or research activities in Germany; secured means of livelihood; adequate health insurance (statutory or equivalent private insurance in Germany); no grounds for threat to public security or order (no criminal convictions, no ongoing investigations, no threat to constitutional order, no violence for political or religious purposes); principal residence in Berlin (not secondary residence); current email address; consent to electronic payment for online applications (credit card Visa/Mastercard or PayPal accepted)
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for job search (online only; you will receive a PDF confirmation that your current residence permit remains valid beyond its previous expiration date)
Power of attorney specifying the subject matter (if applying through a representative)
Copy of current residence permit
Passport copies in color (data pages with photo and personal information)
Study completion certificate, degree, or confirmation from university (if completed studies in Germany)
Documentation of completed research activity (if research activity in Germany is concluded)
Training certificate (if completed qualified vocational training in Germany)
Recognition decision from competent authority, professional practice permit, or permission to use professional title (if completed professional qualification recognition in Germany)
Training certificate or training certification (if completed health or care training in Germany)
Proof of Berlin residence: registration confirmation (Meldebestätigung) or rental contract with landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeber-Bestätigung)

Proof of living space size and costs: for rental apartment - rental contract and proof of current monthly costs (warm rent) such as bank statements; for owned property - land registry extract section 3, monthly housing costs, and any monthly loan costs
Proof of secured livelihood: bank statements, declaration of obligation from third party, scholarship

Health insurance proof: for statutory insurance - electronic health card copies (front and back) or current confirmation; for private insurance - certificate from insurer showing scope and costs per § 257 Abs. 2a SGB V
fees: €56.00 for residence permit as sticker; €100.00 for residence permit as electronic residence title; €27.60 for Turkish nationals under age 24; €46.00 for Turkish nationals age 24 and over; €6.00 additional for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on site
processingTime: If application is approved, you will receive an appointment. Residence permit as sticker can be issued immediately at the appointment. Electronic residence title (eAT) takes 4 to 6 weeks to be ready for collection.

bookingInfo.office: Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA) at Keplerstraße location only

name: Request Residence Permit for Employment of Certain Nationalities
description: This service allows citizens of specified countries to apply for a German residence permit for employment purposes, provided they meet eligibility requirements including legal residence status, a valid employment contract, and Federal Employment Agency approval.
eligibility: Lawful residence. For nationals of Australia, Israel, Japan, Canada, Republic of Korea, New Zealand, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, and United States of America: you entered Germany no more than 90 days ago or already hold a residence permit or other residence title in the federal territory. For nationals of Albania, Andorra, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Monaco, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, and San Marino: you entered with a national D-visa issued by a German foreign mission for employment purposes (pursuant to § 19c Residence Act in conjunction with § 26 Employment Ordinance). Application may be submitted no earlier than 4 months before expiration of your national D-visa or current employment residence permit. Employment: a work contract should already exist; for nationals of Australia, Israel, Japan, Canada, Republic of Korea, New Zealand, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, and United States of America, a draft employment contract also suffices. Employment in Germany: the employment relationship must exist in Germany; for nationals of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia, the employer's business location must also be in Germany. Federal Employment Agency approval: the residence permit can generally only be issued if the Federal Employment Agency (BA) has approved it; the State Immigration Office requests this in an internal procedure after the application is submitted; for nationals of Albania, Andorra, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Monaco, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, and San Marino, approval is obtained before entry by the German foreign mission. Adequate health insurance: you must be insured with a statutory or equivalent private health insurance in Germany; foreign health insurance generally does not suffice. No indicators of threat to public safety or order: even fines can prevent issuance; applications cannot be processed during ongoing investigations; you pose no threat to the free democratic basic order or security of the Federal Republic of Germany; you do not participate in violence, publicly call for violence, or threaten violence for political or religious purposes. Main residence in Berlin: you reside in Berlin (secondary residence is not sufficient). Current email address: the State Immigration Office will contact you via your current email; please regularly check your spam folder. For online application: consent to electronic payment method (credit card Visa/Mastercard or PayPal available).
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for employment (online only); you will receive a PDF document confirming your application certifying that your current residence title (national D-visa or residence permit) remains valid in the federal territory beyond its previous expiration date (not applicable if your current residence title already expired on the application date); please save and print this document
Power of attorney with specification of the procedure subject (if application submitted by authorized representative)
Copy of your residence title (if you already hold a German residence permit or other residence title for the federal territory)
Passport copies in color: data pages with your photo and personal information (always); entry stamp and entry visa (if you entered and are applying for residence permit for the first time)

Employment contract (draft contract also acceptable for nationals of Australia, Israel, Japan, Canada, Republic of Korea, New Zealand, United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, and United States of America)
Completed and signed Declaration on Employment Relationship form (from your employer)
Proof of main residence in Berlin: registration certificate (Meldebestätigung) or rental contract and landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung)

Proof of size and costs of living space: for rental apartment — rental contract (without house rules and attachments) and proof of current monthly costs (gross rent) such as bank statements; for own property — land register extract section three, monthly housing costs and possibly monthly loan costs for the property

Health insurance proof: for statutory health insurance — health insurance card copy (front and back) or current confirmation from health insurance; for private health insurance — certificate from insurer regarding scope and costs of insurance pursuant to § 257 para. 2a SGB V

For renewal of residence permit for employment: proof of current employment — employer certification of duration of uncanceled employment relationship (not older than 14 days) and salary statements from first two and last two months
fees: €56.00 for initial issuance of residence permit as sticker; €49.00 for renewal of residence permit as sticker; €100.00 for initial issuance as electronic residence permit (eAT); €93.00 for renewal as electronic residence permit (eAT); €6.00 additional for digital passport photo creation at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: After positive review of your application, you will receive an appointment. Residence permit as sticker can be issued directly on-site at your appointment. For issuance as electronic residence permit (eAT), it takes 4 to 6 weeks until pickup.

bookingInfo.office: This service can only be accessed at the State Immigration Office (LEA) at the Keplerstraße location.

name: Apply for Residence Permit for Freelance Activity
description: This service allows foreign nationals to apply for a German residence permit to engage in self-employed professional activities such as scientific, artistic, or educational work.
eligibility: You must have lawful residence in Germany with a valid residence title (such as a national D-visa or residence permit), or you must be a citizen of a country eligible to apply visa-free. You must engage in self-employed professional work as defined by German income tax law (§18 EStG), such as scientific, artistic, writing, teaching, or educational activity. If you are over 45 years old, you must demonstrate adequate retirement provision: either a monthly pension of €1,612.53 (for at least 12 years) or savings of €232,204.00 (exemptions apply for citizens of Dominican Republic, Indonesia, Japan, Philippines, and Sri Lanka). You must have adequate health insurance in Germany through statutory or comparable private insurance. You must not pose a security risk, have pending criminal investigations or fines, engage in violence for political or religious purposes, or incite violence. Your main residence must be in Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for freelance activity (online only); you will receive a PDF confirmation certifying your current residence title remains valid beyond its original expiration date (not applicable if you hold a Schengen C-visa or your current title has already expired—save and print this document)
Power of attorney with description of the matter (if applying through an authorized representative)
Copy of your residence title (if you already hold a residence permit or other German residence title)

Passport copies in color: data pages with photo and personal information (always required); entry stamp and visa for entry or residence title from another EU state in passport, if applicable (required if entering for the first time to apply for residence permit)
Curriculum vitae or resume with evidence of qualifications and professional background
References or letters of funding commitment
Earnings forecast (see forms section)
Fee agreements or contracts; alternatively, at least 2 letters of intent describing collaboration and scope of activity (if working on an honorarium basis)
Professional license or permit (if required for the freelance activity, e.g., medical license, legal license)
Evidence of other regular income such as personal assets, regular support from parents, or written commitment from a solvent third party (for artists and language teachers)

Proof of health insurance: for statutory insurance, current confirmation with contribution amount or registration with Artists' Social Insurance (Künstlersozialkasse); for private insurance, insurer's certificate covering scope and costs under § 257 Abs. 2a SGB V
Lease agreement or proof of property ownership
Monthly housing costs documentation (such as current bank statement) or property costs documentation (originals required)
fees: €56.00 for residence permit issued as a label sticker; €100.00 for residence permit issued as electronic residence title; €27.60 for Turkish nationals up to age 24; €46.00 for Turkish nationals age 24 and older; €6.00 additional for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: Residence permit as a label sticker can be issued on-site at your appointment. Residence permit as electronic title (eAT) takes 4-6 weeks to collect.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Residence Permit for Medical Treatment
description: A residence permit allowing foreign nationals to stay in Berlin for medical treatment, requiring a valid national visa and proof of secured living expenses and medical care.
eligibility: Valid national visa (Type D) issued by a German foreign mission or immigration authority. If you have a Schengen visa (Type C), you may extend it as a national visa (Type D) under certain conditions. You must be receiving medical treatment within Germany, have secured living expenses for the duration of treatment, and maintain your main residence in Berlin during medical treatment. For outpatient treatment, both the patient and accompanying person must appear in person. For inpatient treatment, the accompanying person must appear in person with power of attorney, and a hospital certificate of admission must be provided for the patient. To request an appointment, contact the responsible department at LEA via contact form at least 8 weeks before your current residence title expires.
requiredDocuments: Passport with valid national visa (patient must have valid national visa for medical treatment; accompanying person must have valid national visa for accompanying the patient); all passports must contain at least two blank pages without stamps or visas
1 current biometric passport photo (as of 1 May 2025, biometric photos must be created digitally directly at authorities or photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic means)
Completed form 'Application for Issuance of a Residence Title'
Passport or ID card of authorized representative (if applicable)
Cost coverage declaration confirmed by the embassy certifying payment for current and future treatment costs
Proof of living expenses for self-payers: bank statements showing personal financial resources and evidence of payment for previous treatment costs (if no cost coverage declaration can be provided)
Proof of medical treatment: confirmation from treating hospital, doctor, or institution regarding availability of treatment, appointment start date, and expected duration of treatment
Travel health insurance for the duration of outpatient treatment until departure
Documentation of care services provided by accompanying person (if applicable)
Written power of attorney and identification document of representative (passport or German ID card) if applicant cannot apply in person
fees: €100.00 for initial issuance (adults); €96.00 for extension (adults); €50.00 for initial issuance (minors); €48.00 for extension (minors)
processingTime: Approximately 4 weeks after your appointment until the residence permit is issued as an electronic residence title and ready for pickup.

bookingInfo.office: Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA) at Friedrich-Krause-Ufer location only.

name: Extend Residence Permit for Self-Employment or Freelance Work
description: A service to renew your residence permit that authorizes self-employment or freelance professional activities in Germany.
eligibility: You must hold a valid residence permit for self-employment or freelance work under § 21 AufenthG (application may be submitted earliest 4 months before expiration). Your livelihood must be permanently secured through your self-employed or freelance activities. You must have appropriate old-age provision if you are over 45 years old (as of 01.07.2025: you must be able to demonstrate either a monthly pension of €1,612.53 for at least 12 years or assets of €232,204.00 upon reaching age 67; exemptions apply for nationals of Dominican Republic, Indonesia, Japan, Philippines, and Sri Lanka). You must have adequate health insurance (statutory or comparable private insurance in Germany; foreign insurance generally insufficient). You must have no grounds for deportation (previous fines or ongoing investigations may prevent permit issuance; you pose no threat to the free democratic basic order or security of Germany; you are not engaged in violence for political or religious purposes and do not publicly call for or threaten violence). You must have your main residence in Berlin (secondary residence insufficient). You must have a current email address.
requiredDocuments: Application for renewal of residence permit for self-employment or freelance work (online only); you will receive a PDF confirmation document certifying your current residence permit remains valid beyond its previous expiration date (does not apply if permit already expired on application date); save and print this document
Power of attorney specifying the matter of the procedure (if applying through an authorized representative)
Copy of your current residence permit
Color copy of passport

For self-employed entrepreneurs (under § 21 Abs. 1, 2a, or 2b AufenthG): completed 'Examination Report' (Prüfungsbericht) form prepared by a tax advisor, auditor, or lawyer with relevant professional experience (e.g., tax law specialist); should bear an official stamp; together with documents mentioned in the report

For freelance professionals (under § 21 Abs. 5 AufenthG): evidence of livelihood from latest tax assessment and net profit statement from tax advisor; bank statements from last 6 months showing regular income from freelance work; invoices (e.g., from galleries and auction houses); evidence of future commissions; evidence of other regular income (e.g., personal assets or maintenance payments)
Business register excerpt or trade registration (if self-employed)
Chamber registration (if your freelance profession requires registration with a professional chamber)
Registration as freelancer with the competent tax office (if freelance professional)

Health insurance proof: for statutory health insurance — current confirmation from health insurance showing contribution amount or proof of registration with Artists' Social Insurance Fund; for private health insurance — certificate from insurer stating scope and costs of coverage under § 257 Abs. 2a SGB V (inform your insurer you need the certificate for a residence permit for employment)
Rental contract or proof of property ownership (original)
Proof of housing costs (original) — documentation of monthly rent (current bank statement) or costs of occupied property (original)
fees: €49.00 for residence permit issued as label; €93.00 for residence permit issued as electronic residence permit; €27.60 for Turkish nationals up to age 24; €46.00 for Turkish nationals age 24 and above; €6.00 additional for digital passport photo created at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: Residence permit as label can be issued directly on-site during scheduled appointment. Electronic residence permit (eAT) takes 4-6 weeks for collection.

bookingInfo.office: This service is only available at the Immigration Office (Landesamt für Einwanderung / LEA) at the Friedrich-Krause-Ufer location.

name: Apply for Residence Permit for Self-Employment
description: This service allows foreign nationals to apply for a German residence permit to conduct independent business activities in Berlin, subject to economic interest, qualifications, and financial security requirements.
eligibility: You must have lawful residence in Germany (national D-visa or residence permit; Schengen visa is insufficient) or be a national of a visa-exempt country. You must meet one of these conditions: (1) there is economic interest or regional need for your business, the activity has positive economic impact, and financing is secured through equity or credit commitment; (2) you completed a degree or work as a skilled researcher/scientist in Germany and your business relates to your studies or research; or (3) you hold a startup scholarship from a German economic organization or public authority. If over 45 years old, you must have adequate retirement provision (monthly pension of €1,612.53 for 12+ years or assets of €232,204.00, with exceptions for certain nationalities). You must have adequate health insurance in Germany (statutory or comparable private). You must have no deportation interest (no criminal convictions or ongoing investigations, no threat to democratic order or security, no involvement in violence). You must have your primary residence in Berlin. You must provide a current email address. For online application, you must consent to electronic payment (credit card or PayPal).
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit for self-employment (online only)
Power of attorney with specification of case subject (if applying through representative)
Copy of current residence permit or other German residence title (if applicable)
Passport copies in color: data pages with photo and personal information (always required); entry stamp and entry visa or other EU residence title in passport (if applicable and first-time applicant)
Curriculum vitae with qualifications and professional history
References or funding confirmations
University degree diploma (Bachelor, Master) (for university graduates)
University statement regarding knowledge acquired and connection to business idea (for university graduates)
Previous employer statement regarding connection between prior work and business idea (for research/science professionals)
Company profile and detailed business concept
Business plan
Financial plan
Trade register extract or notarized business registration
Business registration certificate (if trade register entry not required)
Proof of other income sources (only if you have additional regular income)
Current health insurance confirmation with premium information (for statutory insurance)
Health insurance certificate covering scope and costs per § 257 Abs. 2a SGB V (for private insurance)
Lease agreement or proof of property ownership
Proof of monthly rent or property costs (current bank statement)
