You can prove your primary residence in Berlin using your ID card or a residence certificate together with your national passport. The residence certificate can also be obtained on-site, so you do not need to visit the citizen's office. Personal appearance is required.
requiredDocuments: Your ID card or national passport
Documents from your embassy (if you have received a special fingerprint form from your embassy, please bring it with you)
fees: 15.00 euros; if a photo also needs to be certified, an additional 5.00 euros
processingTime: Immediately

bookingInfo.office: If this is not handled by your embassy directly, you can obtain this service exclusively at the State Office for Citizenship and Public Order, Central Resident Affairs, if you are registered in Berlin with your primary residence. If you reside elsewhere in Germany, contact your responsible city or municipal administration.

name: Certification of Copies
description: This service certifies that copies of official documents are true and accurate reproductions of the originals, for use with government agencies.
eligibility: The original document must come from a government agency, or the copy must be intended for a government agency. Certain documents can only be certified by the agency that issued the original, including: excerpts from the land register (District Court - Land Registry Office), excerpts from the commercial register (District Court - Registry Court), excerpts from the association register (District Court - Registry Court), birth certificates, marriage certificates, death certificates and other civil status certificates (Registry Office), and information from the real estate cadastre (District Office - Survey Office). For foreign public documents such as certificates or diplomas to be used domestically, legalization/apostille must be obtained from the country of origin. The original document must be unaltered (no gaps, strikethroughs, or correction fluid) and complete (all pages must be presented). Another person may be authorized to apply on your behalf without requiring a power of attorney.
requiredDocuments: Original document and copy of the document

German translation by a publicly sworn/certified interpreter (if the document is in another language) — generally required unless the certifying office has sufficient language skills to understand the content, with the decision made after the document is presented
fees: 5.00 euros per page. Fees may be higher if the original and copy are difficult to compare, for example with technical drawings or chemical formulas.
processingTime: Immediate

bookingInfo.office: This service is available at all citizen offices (Bürgerämter) in Berlin.

name: Certification of Notarial Documents, Certificates and Translations for Use Abroad (Apostille/Legalisation)
description: This service provides official certification (apostille or legalisation) of notarial documents, certificates, and translations for use in foreign countries.
eligibility: You need your notarial document or translation for use in a foreign country.
requiredDocuments: The original document to be certified (this may be a notarial deed, a certified copy, a certified photocopy, or a certificate from a Berlin notary)
fees: 25.00 Euro. Payment methods: Court cost stamp, bank transfer after notification of the case reference number by the Berlin Regional Court II, or in exceptional cases: cash payment.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Certification of Signatures
description: This service certifies that a signature on a document is genuine for submission to a government authority or as required by law.
eligibility: Your signature can be certified only if the document will be submitted to a German government authority or to another organization where you are required to submit it by law or regulation. You must appear in person. Certain documents cannot be certified, including: documents in foreign languages; contracts; documents where the signature has no accompanying text; documents requiring special forms of certification, such as those concerning real estate, commercial register entries, association register entries, family law, inheritance law, or advance powers of attorney.
requiredDocuments: The document on which the signature is to be certified
Identity document, for example your ID card (Personalausweis) or passport
processingTime: Approximately 15 minutes

bookingInfo.office: This service is available at all citizen offices (Bürgerzimmer) in Berlin.

name: Certification of Documents for Abroad (Apostille/Legalization)
description: This service provides official certification (apostille or legalization) of documents issued by Berlin authorities for use abroad.
eligibility: The document you need certified was issued by a Berlin authority. For postal requests: certified documents are normally sent only within Germany; if you request international shipping, longer delivery times and additional postage costs apply. International shipments are sent by registered mail with return receipt; postage fees (flat rate) are charged: Compact letter = €7.45 (100-235 mm long, 70-125 mm wide, up to 50 g); Large letter = €10.10 (100-353 mm long, 70-250 mm wide, up to 500 g). You will receive a tracking number to monitor shipping status online, though no binding delivery guarantees can be given for international mail.
requiredDocuments: Original document issued by Berlin authorities

For school certificates (except non-state-recognized private schools): first contact the Senate Department for Education, Youth and Family, then submit to the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters
For certificates from state universities: first contact your university's examination office, then submit to the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters

For certificates from state-recognized private universities in Berlin: first contact the Senate Department for Science, Health, Care and Equality, then submit to the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters
For Charité documents: first contact Charité, then submit to the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters
For German-language medical certificates: first contact the State Office for Health and Social Affairs, then submit to the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters
For tax office certificates: first contact the Senate Department for Finance, then submit to the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters

For certificates from evangelical/Catholic schools: first contact the Consistory of the Evangelical Church Berlin-Brandenburg-Silesian Upper Lusatia or the Archbishopric Ordinariat, then contact the Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion, then submit to the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters

For documents from chambers (e.g., Medical Chamber, Pharmacy Chamber, Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Bar Association, Architecture Chamber): first contact the respective chamber, then submit to the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters
fees: €19.00 per document for apostille; €19.00 per document for pre-certification for legalization; €5.00 per page for certification of German passports, ID cards and residence permits; additional postage costs apply for international shipping (€7.45 for compact letter, €10.10 for large letter)
processingTime: In-person appointment: immediate; By mail within Germany: approximately 2 weeks; By mail with international return shipping: no binding timeframe can be provided

bookingInfo.office: State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Matters (LABO). Maximum 3 documents per booked appointment; book multiple appointments if you need to certify more documents.

name: Authentication of Judgments, Resolutions, Inheritance Certificates, and Settlements for Foreign Use (Apostille/Legalization)
description: This service authenticates court documents from Berlin courts for use abroad through apostille or legalization certificates.
eligibility: You need a judgment, resolution, inheritance certificate, or settlement from a Berlin court for use abroad.
requiredDocuments: Certified copy or certified extract of the judgment, resolution, inheritance certificate, or settlement

If enforcement abroad is intended, a fully enforceable copy of the judgment, resolution, inheritance certificate, or settlement must be submitted; note that for enforcement outside the European Union, a fully enforceable copy with statement of facts and reasoning (long version) may be required
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The court that pronounced the judgment, issued the resolution or inheritance certificate, or recorded the settlement is responsible. If a translation is required for the recipient country, please commission an authorized translator after receipt of the authentication certificate. For authentication of translations by an authorized translator for Berlin courts, the Berlin Regional Court (Landgericht Berlin) is responsible.

name: Certification of Information in Tax Matters, Residency Certificates for Foreign Use (Apostille/Legalization)
description: This service certifies tax-related documents and residency certificates issued by Berlin tax offices for use abroad, with official apostille or legalization.
eligibility: The document you need certified is an original document issued by a Berlin tax office (Finanzamt) and is required for use outside Germany.
requiredDocuments: Original document
processingTime: Approximately 15 minutes if submitted in person; approximately 1 week if documents are sent by mail

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Subsidy for Medical Costs - Information Request
description: This service provides information and documentation assistance to Berlin civil servants and surviving pension recipients regarding subsidies for medical expenses.
eligibility: You must be in a direct civil service relationship with the Land Berlin or be a recipient of a survivor pension from the Land Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Invoices and/or receipts (copies or invoice copies are sufficient)
Any previously issued notices/decisions
Your personnel number or pension number

name: Information Service for Nursing Care Benefits (Beihilfe zu Pflegeleistungen)
description: This service provides information about nursing care benefits for Berlin state civil servants and pension recipients whose family members require nursing care.
eligibility: You must be in a direct civil service employment relationship with the State of Berlin or be a recipient of a survivor's pension from the State of Berlin. You or your privately insured family members must be in need of care (Pflegebedürftigkeit) as defined in sections 14 and 15 of the German Social Code Book Eleven (requiring determination of a care grade).
requiredDocuments: Nursing care fund notice (Pflegekassenbescheid) from the responsible private or statutory nursing care insurance confirming approval of a care grade and awarded nursing care benefits
Notification regarding approval of nursing care aids (Pflegehilfsmittel)
Additional documents from the nursing care fund concerning approved benefits
Receipts, invoices, or documentation of expenses (copies or invoice copies are sufficient)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Information on Allowances for Psychotherapy, Rehabilitation Measures, and Dental Treatments
description: This service provides information and processing for allowance applications related to psychotherapy, rehabilitation measures, and dental treatments for eligible Berlin state employees and survivors' pension recipients.
eligibility: You must be in a direct employment relationship with the State of Berlin or be a recipient of a survivors' pension from the State of Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Application form and cost estimates for dental treatment (including orthodontic treatments)
Medical documentation (treatment and cost plans) showing the necessity of the dental treatment measure
Application for approval of a rehabilitation measure
Medical documentation showing the necessity of the rehabilitation measure
Application for approval of psychotherapy
Medical documentation (consultation report, sealed medical opinion)
Any previously issued decisions
Your personnel number or pension number

name: Child Support Guardianship (Beistandschaft) through Youth Welfare Office
description: A service for separated or single parents to receive official support in establishing and enforcing child support payments through the youth welfare office.
eligibility: Your child is a minor. You can apply if you are separated from the other parent and have sole custody, or if you share joint custody with the other parent but the child lives with you. A written application is required.
requiredDocuments: Personal ID (Personalausweis)
Child's birth certificate (Geburtsurkunde des Kindes)
Enforceable copy of the maintenance/support order (vollstreckbare Ausfertigung des Unterhaltstitels) — if paternity has already been established
Proof of paternity establishment (Nachweis der Vaterschaftsfeststellung) — if paternity has already been established

name: Authorization to Use Berlin-Ticket S and Additional Discounts

eligibility: You are eligible if you have your primary residence in Berlin or have no fixed address and receive benefits from the state of Berlin. You are also eligible if you receive any of the following transfer benefits: Unemployment Benefit II or Social Money (Hartz IV, Citizen's Allowance); Social assistance; Basic security in old age; Basic security for full occupational disability; Benefits under the Asylum Seekers' Benefits Act; Housing allowance; or benefits under the SED Injustice Redress Laws. Family members in your household unit of the benefit recipient (for benefits 1-5) and household members of housing allowance recipients (if included in the housing allowance calculation) are also eligible. Some groups require a separate application: persons in Berlin correctional facilities participating in outside programs; persons living in Berlin facilities receiving social assistance in another state; persons without fixed address receiving Berlin state benefits; persons with Berlin residence receiving victim pensions or SED compensation from another state; and household members without their own claim but whose excess income covers others' needs.

name: Recognition of Professional Qualification from Abroad - Security Officer / Insurance Consultant / Insurance Agent / Financial Investment Agent / Independent Financial Investment Advisor / Mortgage Broker
description: This service allows you to have your foreign professional qualification recognized so you can work permanently in Germany in one of these regulated professions.
eligibility: You have a professional qualification as a security officer, insurance consultant, insurance agent, financial investment agent, independent financial investment advisor, or mortgage broker from abroad, and you intend to settle permanently in Germany and work in one of these professions. You can apply in Berlin if you intend to work in Berlin in one of these regulated professions.
requiredDocuments: Application for equivalence assessment - informal application in text form (competent offices may provide specific forms)
Identity document - copy of passport or ID card
Tabular curriculum vitae - list in table form showing your training and professional experience

Evidence of your professional qualification - documentation of completed training or evidence of relevant professional experience or other qualification certificates such as completed further education, if necessary to establish equivalence
Declaration of initial application - declaration that no application for establishment of equivalence has been submitted previously

If applicable, certificate from the authority of your country of training - only required if your profession is regulated in your country of training, certifying that you are permitted to practice the profession there
fees: Between €5.00 and €5,000.00 depending on effort and legal regulations; possibly additional costs for translations, certifications, or compensatory measures
processingTime: The competent office will confirm receipt of your documents within a maximum of one month. The office will notify you if documents are missing. If all necessary documents are provided, the procedure takes a maximum of 3 months. In individual cases, the procedure may be extended by a maximum of one additional month.

name: Certificate of Permanent Residence Right for EU/EEA Citizens
description: This service issues a certificate confirming the permanent residence right of EU, Icelandic, Liechtensteinian, or Norwegian citizens who have legally resided in Germany for a qualifying period.
eligibility: EU citizen or national of Iceland, Liechtenstein, or Norway with multi-year residence in Germany based on freedom of movement rights; permanent residence right generally acquired after 5 years of lawful residence (in exceptional cases may be shorter); must have continuously held freedom of movement rights during this period (e.g., as employee, self-employed person, or non-working person with sufficient means of subsistence); main residence in Berlin; in-person appointment required (contact Department E 6 via contact form to schedule).
requiredDocuments: Completed application form 'Antrag auf Ausstellung einer Daueraufenthaltsbescheinigung'
Valid passport or valid ID card

Current biometric passport photo (as of 01.05.2025, biometric photos must be created digitally only at government offices or certified photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic means; check the State Office for Immigration website for current details)
Residence registration certificate (Melderegisterauszug) to prove permanent residence in Germany, or alternative documents such as tax assessments

Proof of freedom of movement rights for the last 5 years: for employees, employer certification of employment type and duration; for self-employed, business registration and tax assessments; for non-working persons, health insurance and proof of sufficient means of subsistence (additional documents may be required on a case-by-case basis)
processingTime: The certificate is generally issued at the appointment.

name: Extension of Residence Certificate (Aufenthaltsgestattung)
description: This service allows you to extend your residence certificate (Aufenthaltsgestattung) if your asylum procedure in Germany is still ongoing and you meet the eligibility requirements.
eligibility: Your asylum procedure in Germany must still be ongoing. The residence certificate can only be extended if it has not expired by law, particularly not following an irrevocable decision from BAMF (Federal Office for Migration and Refugees). You must have your main residence in Berlin and be permitted to reside there for your asylum procedure with no territorial restrictions to another district's foreign office. Personal appearance in person is required for adults (aged 18 and over) by appointment; minors (under 18) do not need to appear in person, though school children should provide a current school certificate.
requiredDocuments: One current biometric photograph for each person with their own residence certificate (35mm x 45mm, frontal view with neutral facial expression and closed mouth, looking straight at the camera, light background)
Current residence certificate (the certificate should have at least more than 4 weeks of validity remaining at the time of your appointment)
processingTime: The residence certificate is typically extended during your in-person appointment.

bookingInfo.office: This service can only be accessed at the State Office for Immigration (LEA) at the Friedrich-Krause-Ufer location in Berlin.

name: Extend Certificate of Tolerated Stay (Duldung)
description: This service allows residents with a certificate of tolerated stay (Duldung) to extend their permission to remain in Germany when deportation remains impossible due to factual or legal reasons.
eligibility: Reasons for suspension of deportation must continue to exist; deportation must remain impossible due to factual or legal reasons. You must have your main residence in Berlin and cannot be obligated to live in another German state. Adults (18 and over) must appear in person with an appointment; minors under 18 do not need to appear in person, but a current school certificate is requested for school-age children. To schedule an appointment, contact the relevant department (A 2, A 3, or A 4) using the contact form in the Further Information section.
requiredDocuments: Current biometric photo for each person with a certificate of tolerated stay (35mm x 45mm, frontal view with neutral expression and closed mouth, looking straight at camera, light background)
Current certificate of tolerated stay (should be valid for at least 4 more weeks at the time of appointment)
Passport or passport substitute (if available)
If no passport or passport substitute is available: Proof of efforts to obtain a passport
If a child was born: Birth certificate, extract from birth register, or other proof of birth

If employment or vocational training is permitted: For employment—last three salary statements and employer certification; For vocational training—current certificate from training business or vocational school
Current proof of receiving benefits under the Asylum Seekers Benefits Act (if applicable)
School certificate (for school-age children)
fees: €37.00 for adults; €18.50 for children and young people; No fee if you provide current proof of receiving benefits under the Asylum Seekers Benefits Act
processingTime: The certificate of tolerated stay is typically extended during the appointment.

bookingInfo.office: This service can only be obtained at the State Office for Immigration (LEA) at the Friedrich-Krause-Ufer location.

name: Certificate of Unlimited Right of Residence
description: This service issues an official certificate confirming that you hold an unlimited right of residence in Germany, for eligible non-EU/EWR foreign nationals who meet specific requirements.
eligibility: You must hold an unlimited residence title (including settlement permit, permanent residence permit for EU citizens, or an unlimited residence permit or authorization issued before January 1, 2005). You cannot be an EU, EWR, or Swiss citizen. Your last usual place of residence must be or have been in Berlin. You must be able to support yourself without public benefits under SGB II or XII (unless married to a German citizen). You must have resided in Germany for at least 15 years (unless married to a German citizen). You must not have grounds for deportation according to Section 54 of the Residence Act.
requiredDocuments: Application for Certificate of Unlimited Right of Residence (can be submitted in person or by mail from abroad)
1 current biometric photograph on photo paper, 35mm x 45mm, front-facing with neutral expression and closed mouth looking directly at camera, light background
Valid passport or passport substitute (together with the unlimited residence title if requested before departure)
Power of attorney with passport or ID card (if personal attendance is not possible)
Proof of secured livelihood (if required): pension decision for retirees; or current health insurance certificate for persons aged 15-67 or those unable to work
Proof of minimum residence (if required): documentation of previous residence in another German federal state
fees: €18.00 for adults; €9.00 for minors; free for Turkish nationals
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

Tabular curriculum vitae (in German) showing all training, further education courses, and employment from start of relevant training

Evidence of relevant professional experience: employment certificates, employment records, reference letters (original language as certified copy and German translation as simple copy)
Other qualification certificates if available: training certificates and credentials (original language as certified copy and German translation as simple copy)
Previous recognition decisions on professional training equivalence (if available)

Completed and employer-signed form 'Declaration on Employment Relationship (Job Description)' (or after positive completion of recognition procedure if equivalence determination process used)

Marriage certificate for spouse joining: certified copy of international marriage certificate or certified copy of national marriage certificate with apostille (both with certified German translation)
German language certificate for spouse (if required)
Birth certificates of children: certified copy of international birth certificates or certified copy of national birth certificates with apostille (both with certified German translation)

Power of attorney issued to employer from skilled worker (sub-power of attorney required if employer engages external service providers); for family reunion: also powers of attorney from joining family members
Sub-power of attorney: authorization for employer staff member or external service provider engaged by employer
fees: 411.00 Euro for the accelerated skilled worker procedure, payable upon conclusion of the written agreement. Costs for certification, translation of documents, and recognition of vocational training and degrees are borne by the skilled worker or employer.

name: Administrative Burial (Ordnungsbehördliche Bestattung)
description: A municipal burial service arranged by the local health authority when a deceased person's burial cannot be organized by relatives or other responsible parties.
eligibility: The deceased must have died in Berlin. The responsible district office (Bezirksamt) is the one in whose area the deceased was registered at the time of death.
requiredDocuments: Police death notification (Form 1007) or notification containing the deceased's personal data, time and place of death, and authorization for burial of the body

Notification from the primary funeral home (Erstüberführer) containing the deceased's personal data, time and place of death, and identification of the party requesting the transfer (e.g., police or care facility)
Notification from a care facility (Heim) containing the deceased's personal data and a death certificate (Leichenschauschein)

name: Apply for Burial Cost Coverage
description: A service to request financial assistance from the city to cover burial costs when the deceased's estate or burial insurance is insufficient.
eligibility: You may be eligible if: (1) the deceased's estate or burial insurance does not cover costs; (2) you are legally responsible for burial costs, including: contractually obligated parties (e.g., under burial insurance agreements), heirs, the father of a child if the mother dies from pregnancy or childbirth complications, persons with maintenance obligations, or persons designated as burial-obligated under Section 16 of the Burial Act; and (3) you cannot afford the burial costs from your own income and assets. Note: You have no claim for cost coverage if you pay for burial without legal obligation (e.g., friends, neighbors, former carers, or estate managers acting out of moral duty rather than legal requirement).

Death certificate or autopsy report
Evidence of sources of the deceased's living expenses
Documentation of the estate, insurance benefits, and any damage claims against third parties

Valid identity documents

Income and asset documentation
Lease agreement
Proof of housing costs
Documentation of special financial burdens
Bank statements for all accounts
Certificate of inheritance or declaration of inheritance waiver (if applicable)

name: Taxation Procedure - Binding Information
description: A service that provides legally binding advance tax guidance on planned transactions and their tax implications before they are implemented.
eligibility: Written form; identification of applicant (name, address, tax number); comprehensive presentation of the facts — the applicant must provide a detailed and complete description of the seriously planned and not yet realized facts at the time of application; it is permissible if preparatory measures have already begun, as long as the facts underlying the request have not yet been substantially realized and other arrangements remain possible; demonstration of the applicant's special tax interest; detailed explanation of the legal issue with thorough justification of the applicant's own legal position; specification of the time period and type of tax; formulation of specific legal questions — general questions about potential tax issues upon implementation are insufficient; exclusivity declaration — statement that no binding information request regarding the submitted facts has been made with any other tax authority; affirmation by the applicant that all information necessary for issuing the advice and for assessment has been provided and is truthful.
requiredDocuments: Written application
fees: Application processing is generally subject to fees. The fee is calculated based on the subject matter value (tax effect), which must be specified by the applicant. Fees are collected under the Court Costs Act (Gerichtskostengesetz). The subject matter value is capped at a maximum of 30 million euros. If the subject matter value is below 10,000 euros, no fee is charged. If the subject matter value cannot be determined, a time-based fee of 50 euros per half hour of processing time is charged; if processing time is under two hours, no fee is charged. The fee must be paid within one month of its assessment. The decision on the application may be deferred until payment is received.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The tax authority competent to issue the binding information is the authority that would be responsible if the facts underlying the application were realized. For applicants for whom no tax authority is yet responsible at the time of application, and whose request concerns joint taxes (income tax, wage tax, sales tax, corporate tax), the Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern) is competent.

name: Appointment of a Legal Guardian
description: A service to appoint a legal guardian for adults who are unable to manage their affairs due to illness, disability, or need for support.
eligibility: Applicants must be adults (18 years or older). A legal guardianship can only be arranged if a mental illness or physical, intellectual, or emotional disability prevents the person from managing their affairs in whole or in part, granting power of attorney to a third party, or overseeing the activities of an authorized representative. The affected person may apply for guardianship themselves, or it may be requested by another person (such as relatives, neighbors, or authorities) or initiated by the court.
requiredDocuments: Application or petition for legal guardianship (can be submitted in writing, in person at the court's legal filing office, or using the provided template form)
Medical certificate or medical report (if available from a doctor such as a general practitioner)

Specification of areas of responsibility (such as: health matters; housing matters; representation before authorities; determination of residence; care facility matters; mail opening; financial matters; inheritance matters)
fees: If financial management is included in the guardianship, fees and costs apply only if the person's assets exceed €25,000 after deducting all liabilities. For each €5,000 of assets exceeding this threshold, an annual fee of €10 is charged, with a minimum fee of €200 per year. If financial management is not part of the guardianship, an annual fee of €300 applies unless the person's assets are documented to the court (in which case the calculation above applies). Additional costs may also apply for medical reports, compensation, or reimbursement of expenses for the guardian.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The District Court (Amtsgericht) responsible is the one in whose jurisdiction the affected person has their ordinary residence.

name: Recognition as a Guardianship Organization (Betreuungsverein)
description: This service allows established nonprofit associations in Berlin to apply for official recognition as a guardianship organization to provide legal guardianship and support services.
eligibility: Registered, legally capable association; headquarters and activities in Berlin; pursuit of charitable or nonprofit purposes; guarantee of sustained operational capacity and submission of annual activity reports; employment of professionally qualified full-time staff, ongoing training, and liability insurance coverage—minimum two staff members with a combined full-time position registered as professional guardians; planned efforts to recruit volunteer guardians; counseling and training for volunteer guardians and authorized representatives; planned information provision on advance directives, living wills, and guardianship directives; facilitation of experience exchange among staff; guardianship organization must be independent of residential or institutional facilities serving its clients.
requiredDocuments: Application for recognition as a guardianship organization (informal written application by mail)
Organizational concept (Konzeption)
Association bylaws (Vereinssatzung)
Extract from the association register (Auszug aus dem Vereinsregister)
Certificate from the tax office for charitable or nonprofit status (Bescheinigung vom Finanzamt)
Proof of liability insurance for staff (Nachweis über Haftpflichtversicherung)
Staffing plan for employed, professionally qualified, registered full-time professional guardians (Stellenplan)
processingTime: Approximately 3 months

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Guardianship - Counseling and Support by the Guardianship Authority
description: A service providing counseling and support through the guardianship authority for individuals requiring guardianship assistance.
eligibility: None
requiredDocuments: Valid identification documents
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The competent guardianship authority is determined by the ordinary place of residence of the person requiring guardianship.

name: Notarization of a Child's Maintenance Claim or Support Obligation
description: This service provides official notarization of child support obligations or claims, creating a legally binding document regarding maintenance payments.
eligibility: Valid identity document (e.g., passport, ID card, or driver's license) required; full legal capacity required (if capacity is limited, the legal guardian or custodian must appear in person); interpreter/language mediator required if German language skills are insufficient (the notarization is conducted in German, and any interpreter must not be related to the parties involved).
requiredDocuments: Valid identity document of the obligated party (e.g., ID card, passport, or driver's license)
Valid identity document of the interpreter/language mediator if applicable (e.g., ID card, passport, or driver's license)
Birth certificate of the child or acknowledgment of paternity document if available
Request letter for notarization of the support obligation from a lawyer, youth office, or the other parent if available
Evidence of agreement on the payment of a specific maintenance amount if available
Copy or extract of existing maintenance orders (document, court decision, judgment) if available
processingTime: 30 minutes (not including preparation time or waiting time)

bookingInfo.office: Youth office (Jugendamt) for the child's place of residence; if the child resides outside Berlin, the youth office for the residence of the obligated party.

name: Security Services License - Application
description: Apply for a permit to operate a security services business, which requires demonstrating personal reliability, financial stability, professional competency, and appropriate insurance coverage.
eligibility: Personal reliability (verified through criminal record checks, business registry checks, and police statement); financially sound condition (no significant debts or known insolvency proceedings); professional competency (proof of passed IHK examination or equivalent recognized qualification); sufficient professional liability insurance; for online application: BundID registration/login.
requiredDocuments: Application for permit under § 34a of the Trade Regulation Act (Gewerbeordnung) — can be submitted online or via form
Personal identification document — ID card or other official photo ID (not required for electronic submission); residence permit if applicant is not an EU citizen
Certificate of professional competency — IHK competency examination certificate or equivalent recognized professional qualification
Information from the Debtor Registry (Central Enforcement Portal) — request online via the Central Enforcement Portal of the states

Certificate regarding insolvency proceedings — for natural persons with residence in Berlin: two certificates required (one for consumer insolvency proceedings from local district court, one for standard insolvency proceedings from Amtsgericht Charlottenburg, Amtsgerichtsplatz 1, 14057 Berlin); for legal entities and partnerships with registered office in Berlin: Amtsgericht Charlottenburg; applicants with residence/registered office outside Berlin must check jurisdiction via central court directory
Tax clearance certificate — certificate of tax clearance (Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung) from the competent local tax office
Professional liability insurance — confirmation from an insurance company certifying professional liability insurance for security services business
Current commercial register extract — registered businesses must submit current extract; entities in formation must submit articles of association or bylaws
processingTime: Approximately 1 month

bookingInfo.office: The permit application must be submitted to the Ordnungsamt (regulatory office) responsible for the registered business location. If no business location is yet known, the application can be submitted to the Ordnungsamt responsible for the applicant's place of residence.

name: Security Company Registration - Security Personnel Registration
description: A service for registering security personnel with the Berlin authorities and maintaining them in the official security officer registry.
eligibility: Security personnel, operations managers, and branch managers must be reliable and trustworthy. Only persons with reliability credentials may be employed in security roles. For standard security activities: IHK instruction certificate required. For special security activities or management roles: IHK expert examination certificate or equivalent recognized professional qualification required.
requiredDocuments: Online registration in the security officer registry (online processing only)
IHK instruction certificate for employees or other recognized certificates for standard security activities

IHK expert examination certificate or equivalent recognized certificates required for: patrols in public traffic areas or on private premises with actual public access; retail theft prevention; door security at commercial nightclubs (bouncer); or in management positions: security at asylum/refugee accommodations or access-controlled major events
fees: €50.00 to €350.00 per registered security person (scale fee)
processingTime: 4 weeks, provided no further examination is required

bookingInfo.office: Ordnungsamt (Public Order Office)

name: Register for security industry examination
description: Register for the mandatory training and examination required to work in the security industry in Berlin.
eligibility: You must attend the training in person. Application deadline must be observed.
requiredDocuments: Online registration via the IHK Berlin registration portal (required)
Photo identification for exam verification
processingTime: The certificate will be issued immediately or sent to you within a few days.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Security Business - Register for Expert Knowledge Examination
description: Registration for the expert knowledge examination required to work in the security industry (Bewachungsgewerbe).
eligibility: You must appear in person for the examinations. You must observe the registration deadline.
requiredDocuments: Online registration through the IHK Berlin registration portal (registration for the expert knowledge examination is only possible online)
Photo identification for identification at the examination
Possibly additional documents as specified by your IHK
fees: 200.00 Euro for initial examination; 100.00 Euro for repetition of an examination part (written/oral)
processingTime: The certificate is normally available immediately or within a few days after passing the oral examination part.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Recognition of Educational Qualifications from Other German States
description: This service recognizes and evaluates educational qualifications and certificates obtained from other German states.
eligibility: The requirement is submission of verifiable school documentation. This regularly includes all forms of school completion certificates, annual certificates, individual examination records such as university entrance exams, university degrees with study performance certificates, academic certificates, internship records, employment records, and similar documents.
requiredDocuments: Documents as listed above in eligibility section
Curriculum vitae and copies of identification documents, if applicable with proof of residence title
fees: €50.00 for evaluation of foreign general educational qualifications; €50.00 for evaluation of foreign vocational qualifications; €40.00 for evaluation of domestic qualifications
processingTime: Several weeks to several months (in some cases up to years) depending on the complexity of the evaluation process

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Illegal Waste Disposal (Bio Waste) - Reporting and Removal
description: A service for reporting and arranging the disposal of illegally dumped biological waste in Berlin.
eligibility: Report of the illegal waste by telephone, in writing, or electronically.
requiredDocuments: Complaint containing the following information: location and time
volume of waste
perpetrator (if known)
personal details of the person reporting
fees: Free of charge (may be subject to fees for the perpetrator if applicable).
processingTime: Up to 7 days for public street land.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Request Blank Registration Certificate Part II for New Vehicles from EU Abroad
description: This service allows you to request a blank registration certificate part II for new vehicles purchased from elsewhere in the EU without going through the standard registration process.
eligibility: No prerequisites required.
requiredDocuments: Application for issuance of registration certificate part II outside the registration process for new vehicles (see Forms)
Identity card or passport with registration certificate
Informal power of attorney and personal documents of authorized party and authorized representative (unless a notarially executed power of attorney is used)
Trade register extract and business registration in original or certified copy (for companies)
Association register extract in original or certified copy (for associations)
COC document or data confirmation or expert report according to §13 EG-FGV or §21 StVZO (not older than 18 months) from a technical testing facility (for motorcycles and special vehicles)
Notification of intra-community acquisition (see Forms)
Purchase contract
fees: Fee is determined according to the current fee schedule for traffic law measures and is at minimum 14.90 EUR. Please note that this fee may be higher depending on the individual case and specific application.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Appointment required with the vehicle registration authority (KFZ-Zulassungsbehörde)

name: Request a blank registration certificate part II for new vehicles from non-EU countries
description: This service allows you to request a blank registration certificate part II (Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil II) for new vehicles imported from outside the EU.
eligibility: No prerequisites required.
requiredDocuments: Application for issuance of a registration certificate part II outside the registration procedure for new vehicles (see Forms)
ID card or passport with registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung)
Power of attorney and personal documents (if applicable): ID of the authorizing person (unless it is a notarized power of attorney) and ID of the authorized representative
Excerpt from the commercial register and business registration in original or certified copy (for companies)
Excerpt from the association register in original or certified copy (for associations)

COC paper or data confirmation or expert report according to § 13 EG-FGV or expert report according to § 21 StVZO (not older than 18 months) from a technical inspection facility (for motorcycles and special vehicles)
Customs clearance certificate according to § 6 paragraph 6 FZV
Purchase contract
fees: The fee is determined according to the current fee schedule for road traffic measures and is at minimum 14.90 EUR. Please note that this fee may be higher depending on the individual case and specific application.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Schedule an appointment with the vehicle registration authority (KFZ-Zulassungsbehörde)

name: Transfer Blue Card EU to a New Passport
description: This service allows you to transfer your valid Blue Card EU from an expired passport to a new passport in Berlin.
eligibility: You must have your main residence in Berlin and must book an appointment. You can transfer at any Berlin citizen office (Bürgeramt) if you have your expired passport with valid Blue Card EU, the Blue Card EU was issued by Berlin's immigration authority or previously transferred by a Berlin citizen office, your old passport is complete, no more than 12 months have passed between the old passport's expiration and new passport issuance dates, and you have not left Germany continuously for more than 12 months. If any of these conditions are not met, the State Office for Immigration (Landesamt für Einwanderung) is responsible for the transfer.
requiredDocuments: Your new passport
Your old passport (or police report if it was stolen)
Your Blue Card EU together with the supplementary sheet

1 current biometric passport photo (new regulations apply from 01.05.2025; as of this date, biometric passport photos must be created digitally only at government offices or photography studios and transmitted via secure electronic channels — check the State Office for Immigration website before your appointment)
fees: 67.00 euros; 27.60 euros for those under 24 years old; 46.00 euros for those 24 years and older
processingTime: Approximately 4 weeks after your appointment until the Blue Card EU is issued as an electronic residence permit and ready for collection

bookingInfo.office: Any Berlin citizen office (Bürgeramt) if eligibility conditions are met; otherwise the State Office for Immigration (Landesamt für Einwanderung)

name: Apply for Blue Card EU
description: This service allows qualified professionals with a job offer in Germany to apply for a Blue Card EU, which is a residence and work permit for highly skilled workers.
eligibility: You must have lawful residence in Germany (already holding a Blue Card EU, national D-visa, or residence permit) or be eligible to apply visa-free based on your nationality. You must apply at least 4 months before your current D-visa or Blue Card EU expires. You must hold a university degree from a German institution, a recognized foreign degree, or an equivalent tertiary education qualification lasting at least 3 years. Alternatively, you may be an experienced professional in information and communications technology (ICT) with at least 3 years of professional experience in the last 7 years in job categories 133 or 25 of ISCO-08. You must have a job contract or concrete job offer for at least 6 months in Germany with a German employer having a business location in Germany. Your gross monthly salary must meet minimum thresholds: €3,827.85 per month (€45,934.20 annually) for shortage occupations, or €4,225.00 per month (€50,700.00 annually) for other professions. If earning below €4,225.00 monthly, you need approval from the Federal Employment Agency. Depending on your profession, you may need a professional practice license. You must have adequate health insurance (statutory or comparable private insurance in Germany). You must have no indicators of endangering public security or order, and must not participate in violence for political or religious goals. You must have your main residence in Berlin. You must provide a current email address and consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal) for online application.
requiredDocuments: Application for Blue Card EU (online only); you will receive a PDF confirmation certifying your current residence title remains valid
Power of attorney with statement of matter if applying through an authorized representative
Copy of your residence title if you already hold a Blue Card EU or other German residence permit

Passport copies in color: data pages with photo and personal information (always required); entry stamp, entry visa, or other EU state residence permit in passport if entering Germany for the first time to apply for Blue Card EU
Your employment contract or job offer
University degree certificate
Proof of residence in Berlin: registration confirmation (Melde-Bestätigung) or rental contract with landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeber-Bestätigung)

Evidence of housing size and costs: for rental: rental contract (without house rules or annexes) and proof of current monthly costs (warm rent) such as bank statements; for owned property: land register excerpt (Section 3), monthly house management fees, and possibly monthly mortgage costs for the property

Proof of health insurance: for statutory insurance: electronic health card (copy of front and back) or current insurance confirmation; for private insurance: insurer's certificate of coverage and costs per § 257 section 2a SGB V
Completed and signed declaration of employment relationship form (from your employer)
Professional practice license if required for your profession
Certificate of degree evaluation (Zeugnisbewertung) from ZAB if your foreign degree is not rated in the anabin database
Resume and other training certificates if you do not hold a university degree
Recognition decision (Feststellungsbescheid) confirming equivalence of tertiary education program to university degree if applicable
For Blue Card EU renewal: employer's certification of continuous employment (not older than 14 days) and salary statements from first two and last two months
fees: €56.00 for first-time issuance as sticker; €49.00 for renewal as sticker; €100.00 for first-time issuance as electronic residence permit; €93.00 for renewal as electronic residence permit; €27.60 for Turkish nationals under age 24 for first issuance or renewal; €46.00 for Turkish nationals age 24 and over for first issuance or renewal; €6.00 additional for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: After your application is reviewed positively, you will receive an appointment. A Blue Card EU as sticker can be issued directly at your appointment. As electronic residence permit (eAT), it takes 4 to 6 weeks until collection.

bookingInfo.office: Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA) at the Keplerstraße location in Berlin only

name: Blind Assistance Benefit
description: Financial assistance provided to individuals who are blind or have severe visual impairment and low income in Berlin.
eligibility: Blindness (complete absence of vision) or permanent bilateral visual acuity of no more than 1/50; low income; low assets
requiredDocuments: Application for social assistance
Valid identity documents and residence confirmation
Income statements

Asset statements (e.g., for capital-building insurance such as life insurance, building savings insurance, Riester pension contracts, funeral insurance, funeral provisions, savings accounts, real estate, property, valuables, vehicles)
Bank statements
Rental contract and rent change notices
Proof of health and long-term care insurance
Evidence of severity of visual impairment (ophthalmological findings, severe disability determination notice, severe disability ID card with mark 'Bl')
Decisions about equivalent benefits (state long-term care allowance decision, nursing care level determination from nursing insurance fund, accident or occupational disease annuity decision)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Youth Office (Jugendamt): children and young people until age 18; Office for Social Affairs (Amt für Soziales): adults

name: Soil Contamination Register - Request Information
description: Property owners or their authorized representatives can request information about soil contamination from the soil contamination register for their property.
eligibility: You must be the property owner or an authorized representative. The information is valid only for the requested area(s) and does not apply to neighboring properties. Submit your request at least 4 weeks before you need the information. If representing another party, you must provide a power of attorney.
requiredDocuments: Application for information from the soil contamination register (preferably submitted online)
Property details: your name and address, the exact property designation with address and/or cadastral district, plot and parcel number, and optionally a location map
Power of attorney (if you are not the property owner)
Proof of fee exemption (if applicable)
fees: Free if grounds for fee exemption apply; €5.00 to €500.00 for transmission of environmental information and for copies, photocopies, and duplications.
processingTime: 4 weeks from submission of complete and assessable application documents. Processing may take longer in complex cases.

bookingInfo.office: Contact the Environmental and Nature Protection Office (Umwelt- und Naturschutzamt) in the district where the property is located. If the property falls under State administration upon review, your application will be forwarded immediately.

name: Bodenrichtwert - Auskunft
description: A service that provides information about standard land values (Bodenrichtwert) for properties in Berlin without any eligibility requirements.
eligibility: No requirements
requiredDocuments: Location designation of the property in question
fees: Free for online retrieval including PDF printout via BORIS Berlin
processingTime: Immediate when using the online Bodenrichtwert information service BORIS

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Berlin Stock Exchange Supervision - File a Complaint
description: Submit a complaint to the Berlin stock exchange supervisory authority regarding issues at the Tradegate Berlin Stock Exchange or concerning the authority itself.
eligibility: The complaint must relate to a matter at the Tradegate Berlin Stock Exchange or concern the Berlin stock exchange supervisory authority (e.g., alleged sender). The Berlin Stock Exchange Supervisory Authority only has legal supervision over trading at the Tradegate Berlin Stock Exchange. There is no jurisdiction for other federal German stock exchanges, off-exchange online trading platforms, or problems with foreign trading venues.
requiredDocuments: Complaint submitted online in text form with the disputed matter described as precisely as possible
If a transaction is being disputed: specific details must be named including stock exchange, time of transaction, and available identifiers (e.g., ISIN)
If a transaction is being disputed: evidence that the responsible trading surveillance office has not resolved your complaint, with any written correspondence included
If the sender is unclear: email as PDF
processingTime: Simple information requests can be provided within a few days. If investigations are required, the average processing time is approximately 2-3 weeks.

bookingInfo.office: Berlin Stock Exchange Supervisory Authority (Börsenaufsichtsbehörde Berlin). For other federal German stock exchanges, off-exchange online trading platforms, or issues with foreign trading venues, contact the respective local supervisory authority or the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin). Information about the responsible supervisory authority can usually be found in the imprint of the respective stock exchange or trading platform.

name: Report Broadband Internet Connection Need
description: A service allowing private users, businesses, and property owners in Berlin to register their need for improved broadband or fiber-optic internet connectivity.
eligibility: Private users dissatisfied with their broadband connection for everyday activities like email and streaming; business users and self-employed individuals in Berlin needing high-performance internet with fast download and upload speeds; property owners or their representatives who can securely register their interest in fiber-optic connections (property owner declaration) — only registered telecommunications companies on the Gigabit Portal Berlin have access to these registrations. An optional availability check is recommended to compare offerings from alternative telecommunications providers.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Request File Access in Administrative Fine Proceedings
description: This service allows affected parties or their authorized representatives to request access to files in administrative fine proceedings.
eligibility: Access to files is granted only to the affected party themselves or to an authorized representative.
requiredDocuments: Identity document (passport, travel document, or passport replacement document for foreign nationals)
Power of attorney signed by the affected party (required only if file access is requested by a third party)
fees: No charge for file access on-site; 12.00 Euro for file dispatch fee (only available for legal defense counsel); printing charges apply according to the current administrative fee schedule.
processingTime: 30 minutes

bookingInfo.office: The authority that issued the decision is responsible.

name: Penalty Procedure - Surrender Driver's License for Driving Ban
description: This service handles the surrender of your driver's license when a driving ban (Fahrverbot) is imposed as a result of a traffic violation penalty.
eligibility: For a first driving ban: surrender your license within 4 months of the ban becoming legally effective (14 days after receiving the penalty notice). If no driving ban was imposed against you in the two years before the traffic violation and up to the current penalty decision, you may choose when to surrender your license within this 4-month period, after which you cannot drive any motor vehicle. For a repeated driving ban (if a ban was imposed against you in the past two years): immediate surrender of your license as of legal effectiveness, meaning you must surrender your license no later than 14 days after receiving the penalty notice and must not drive any motor vehicle. Residents of Berlin may surrender the license at a police precinct (24 hours) or deposit it in the night mailbox at the penalty office; residents outside Berlin should inquire with their local police station whether they accept licenses in official custody, otherwise mail the license to the penalty office.
requiredDocuments: Driver's license for surrender
Identity document (Personalausweis, Reisepass, or Passersatzpapiere for foreign nationals) - required only when surrendering at a police precinct
Penalty notice (Bußgeldbescheid) - required only when surrendering at a police precinct
Case number (Aktenzeichen) - required only when depositing in the night mailbox of the penalty office
processingTime: 10 minutes for license surrender. The license will be returned to you by registered mail without any action required on your part.

bookingInfo.office: For traffic violations committed in the state of Berlin, the Penalty Office (Bußgeldstelle) of the state of Berlin is responsible. For traffic violations committed outside Berlin, the authority that issued the penalty notice is responsible.

name: Payment Plan or Deferment for Traffic Fines — Financial Hardship
description: This service allows residents facing financial hardship to request a payment plan or deferment for traffic-related fines that have become final and enforceable.
eligibility: Financial inability to pay. Payment plans or deferment are available for final, binding, and enforceable traffic violation orders if financial hardship is demonstrated. Payment arrangements cannot be granted for warning fines. If enforcement proceedings are already pending at the Tiergarten District Court, applications for payment arrangements must be directed there. Submitting a request for deferment or installment payments does not stop enforcement of final claims — enforcement measures are only suspended once the deferment or payment plan is approved.
requiredDocuments: Application for payment arrangements (informal written request, to be brought to your appointment or submitted by post, email, or fax — must include the case/file reference number)
Proof of identity (national ID card, passport, or travel documents for foreign nationals)
Proof of financial hardship (such as payroll statement, pension decision, or documentation of other payment obligations demonstrating your financial situation)
processingTime: 30 minutes

bookingInfo.office: The agency that issued the original order is responsible for processing your request.

name: Apply for Chance Card (Chancenkarte)
description: A residence permit for non-EU citizens to search for qualified employment or prepare to establish a business in Germany.
eligibility: You intend to seek employment in Germany and have legally entered with a national D-visa for job search purposes, or already hold a residence permit for employment under specific regulations, or possess a Blue Card EU. You must have secured means of subsistence through your own income, sufficient savings, or financial support from others. You must maintain adequate health insurance registered in Germany (statutory or private equivalent; foreign insurance is generally not sufficient). You must present no indicators of endangering public security or order, and must not have criminal convictions, active criminal investigations, or involvement in violence for political or religious purposes. You must have your main residence in Berlin (a secondary residence is insufficient). You must provide a current email address. For online applications, you must consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal).
requiredDocuments: Application for residence permit as Chancenkarte (online only)
Confirmation PDF document of your application (must be saved and printed)
Power of attorney if applying through an authorized representative
Passport copies in color (data pages with photo and personal information, and entry stamp page if entered on D-visa for job search)
Copy of current residence permit (visa, residence permit, or Blue Card EU)
Proof of residence: either registration certificate (Meldebestätigung) or landlord's move-in confirmation
Rental agreement (without house rules and attachments) and proof of current monthly housing costs (warm rent), such as bank statements
Proof of means of subsistence: for example, bank statements, employment certificates, or scholarship documentation

Health insurance documentation: for statutory health insurance, copy of electronic health card (front and back) or current confirmation; for private health insurance, certification from insurer regarding scope and costs of coverage
fees: 56,00 EUR (after entry with D-visa, issued as sticker); 100,00 EUR (after entry with D-visa, issued as electronic residence permit); 54,00 EUR (transfer from other employment residence permit, issued as sticker); 98,00 EUR (transfer from other employment residence permit, issued as electronic residence permit); 27,60 EUR (Turkish nationals under 24 years old); 46,00 EUR (Turkish nationals 24 years and older); additional 6,00 EUR for digital passport photo at self-service terminal on-site
processingTime: After your application is approved, you will receive an appointment. If issued as a sticker (Etikett), it can be issued immediately at your appointment. If issued as an electronic residence permit (eAT), it takes 4 to 6 weeks to collect.

bookingInfo.office: This service is only available at the State Office for Immigration (Landesamt für Einwanderung – LEA) at the Keplerstraße location in Berlin.

name: Submit Statistics Data as a Recognized Adult Education Institution
description: This service allows recognized adult education institutions to fulfill their mandatory obligation to report statistical data to the government.
eligibility: Recognition as an adult education institution according to the Adult Education Act. If your institution was recognized under § 3 paragraph 3 of the Adult Education Act, you are obligated to participate in the statistics by submitting your data. This obligation to participate applies for the first time after the completion of a full calendar year as a recognized provider and after a request from your authority in the following year.
processingTime: Immediate: confirmation of receipt of submitted data after electronic submission; 1 month: verification of submitted data for plausibility and, if necessary, request for missing data

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Permanent Residence Card for Family Members of EU and EEA Citizens
description: This service issues a permanent residence card to non-EU/EEA family members of EU or EEA citizens who have legally resided continuously in Germany for 5 years while exercising freedom of movement rights.
eligibility: You must be a family member of an EU or EEA citizen; you must not be a citizen of an EU member state or Iceland, Liechtenstein, or Norway; your family member must be from the EU or EEA; you must have legally and continuously resided together with the EU or EEA citizen in Germany for 5 years; during this entire period you must have continuously exercised freedom of movement rights (for example, as an employee, self-employed person, or with sufficient means of subsistence); and you must have your main place of residence in Berlin. A legal residence alone is not sufficient. Personal attendance at an appointment is required; please contact the responsible departments F1 and F2 via contact form to arrange an appointment.
requiredDocuments: Application for issuance of a permanent residence card (completed)
Valid passport

One current biometric passport photo (as of 1 May 2025, biometric photos must be created digitally only at government offices or certified photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic means; please check the Berlin Immigration Office website for current information before your appointment)
Current residence card or residence permit
Extended registration office statement if you have not lived continuously in Berlin for 5 years (to prove your permanent residence in Germany)

Proof of freedom of movement rights for the last 5 years: Employees must provide employer certification of type and duration of employment; Self-employed persons must provide business registration and tax assessments; Non-working persons must provide health insurance and proof of means of subsistence (additional documents may be required in individual cases)
fees: €46.00 for applicants aged 24 and over; €27.60 for applicants under 24 years of age; €6.00 additional fee for creating a digital passport photo at the self-service terminal on site
processingTime: Approximately 4 weeks after your appointment; the permanent residence card will be issued as an electronic residence title and can be collected.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for contact details.

name: Monument Tax Certificate Application (Income Tax Act)
description: A service for obtaining a tax certificate to claim tax deductions for expenses related to the preservation and maintenance of a property listed as a historical monument in Berlin.
eligibility: The property must be registered in Berlin's monument list; planned construction measures must be necessary for the preservation of the monument's substance and/or for its meaningful use; planned measures must be coordinated in advance with the State Monument Authority Berlin for tax recognition; for final certificates, a monument protection permit from the Lower Monument Protection Authority of the respective Berlin district must be obtained before construction begins; for preliminary certificates, the builder must provide exact specifications of the planned measures (e.g., by trade or building component); if represented by another person, written power of attorney must be provided; if submitting additional documents in response to a request, the specific documents listed in the request letter must be uploaded via the online application.
requiredDocuments: Online application for final or preliminary tax certificate for monument preservation
All required documents and evidence in PDF, JPG, or PNG format for upload
Monument protection permit (copy) — for final certificates only
Acceptance confirmation (copy) — for final certificates only
Invoices (copy) — for final certificates only
Photo documentation (depending on scope of construction measures at the property)
Power of attorney if represented by another person

name: Monument - Request Monument Protection Authorization
description: This service allows property owners and authorized representatives to request permission from Berlin authorities to perform construction work on, near, or affecting protected monuments.
eligibility: You need authorization if you plan to perform construction work on monuments or in their immediate surroundings, including: modernization, maintenance, renovation, or restoration measures; changes to a monument's appearance; removal (partial or complete) of a monument; or construction work in the immediate vicinity of a monument. Work can only begin after receiving approval from the responsible authority. This authorization does not replace other permits required under separate regulations (such as building permits or tree removal permits from the parks office). Violations constitute an administrative offense.

name: Landmark Grant - Apply for Heritage Conservation Additional Expenses
description: Apply for public funding to support additional costs incurred in heritage conservation work on registered landmarks in Berlin.
eligibility: You must coordinate the proposed conservation goal, funding eligibility, and requested funding amount in advance with the State Monument Office Berlin (Landesdenkmalamt Berlin). The landmark must be registered in the Berlin State Monument List. You must be the owner, a person with property rights, or responsible for building maintenance or conservation of the landmark (the federal government, state governments, and their subordinate institutions are not eligible). The work must be of substantial interest to monument protection and heritage conservation. You must obtain heritage rights permission (denkmalrechtliche Genehmigung) from the Lower Monument Protection Authority of the relevant Berlin district before beginning work. Work must not have started before you submit the application and receive a decision (as a rule, 'start' means concluding a contract for execution; the State Monument Office may make exceptions upon written request with justification). If you have already submitted an application and are asked to submit additional documents, upload them via the online application using the reference number in the request letter. If you have received a grant decision, you may begin work, request fund disbursement, and after completion submit a usage report. Submit an interim usage report when requesting partial fund disbursement or within 3 months of the calendar year end for which funding was approved. Submit a final usage report no later than 6 months after the funded work is completed.
requiredDocuments: Application for Heritage Conservation Additional Expenses Grant (online only; submit all documents in PDF, JPG, or PNG format, max 85 MB total file size, max 50 MB per file)
Copy of heritage rights permission OR copy of permission application

Project description (current condition of the monument, explanation of the conservation goal agreed with the State Monument Office, description of planned work, explanation of heritage-related additional expenses)

Cost estimate (cost estimate/cost calculation/cost assessment/cost quote)
Heritage-related additional expense analysis (presentation of heritage-related additional expense costs)
Financing plan (showing all income and expenses related to the heritage conservation work)

Fund disbursement, interim usage report, or usage report submission (online or by form; for online submission provide documents in PDF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, XLS, or XLSX format, max 50 MB per file, max 80 MB total)
Confirmation of due payments within next 3 months (if applicable to fund disbursement request)
Interim usage report with fund disbursement (if applicable, submit together with disbursement request)
Annexes 5 and 6 of your grant decision (for fund disbursement)
Activity report describing completed work (for usage or interim usage reports; include start date, duration, completion date, any deviations from approved plans and financing plan)

name: Interpreter Compensation in Criminal and Regulatory Offense Proceedings
description: This service provides payment compensation to interpreters for their work in criminal and regulatory offense proceedings.
eligibility: Compensation is only granted upon application. You may submit your written application to the accounting office of the Tiergarten District Court by post, in the mailbox of the accounting office (Old Building Room A 236), or at the business office or department of the proceeding in which you worked as an interpreter. The judge certifies your interpreter activity at the hearing and orders payment of compensation. Your right to compensation generally expires if you do not claim it within three months of the court or investigative authority that commissioned you. The deadline begins with the end of the hearing or examination for which you were engaged; in case of multiple engagements (e.g., continuation hearings), it begins with the end of the last hearing. If your engagement ends early, the deadline begins as soon as you are notified of the early termination.
requiredDocuments: Signed payment authorization form (HKR 174) in original and copy
Completed application for interpreter compensation (form available under 'Formulare')
Original receipts or documentation of incurred travel costs or other expenses

Certified extract from the registered partnership register of your last partnership with dissolution notation, if previously registered as partners in Germany; alternatively, registered partnership certificate with valid dissolution judgment (if applicable)

Registered partnership certificate and valid dissolution judgment if previously registered as partners abroad (if applicable)

name: Marriage Ceremony - Execution

Witnesses (optional): The marriage can be performed, if desired, with one or a maximum of two witnesses. The witnesses must be adults and be able to prove their identity with a valid ID card or passport. Sworn interpreter (if needed): If the parties entering marriage or the witnesses do not have sufficient command of the German language, a sworn interpreter must be commissioned by the parties entering marriage.

name: Request to Convert Registered Same-Sex Life Partnership to Marriage
description: This service allows same-sex partners in a registered life partnership established before October 1, 2017 to convert their partnership into a marriage.

All required documents must be submitted in German or officially translated by a German-certified interpreter. Some countries require apostille certification or legalization from the German embassy. For documents originally in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic, personal names must be transliterated according to ISO standards. If either partner is not sufficiently fluent in German, they must arrange and pay for an interpreter. Original documents are required and must not be altered, perforated, or laminated.
