eligibility: Personal appearance required (representation possible). You must collect your eID card in person. If you cannot collect it yourself, you may authorize another person in writing using a special declaration form (available under "Forms").
requiredDocuments: Valid identity document (passport, passport replacement, or national ID card/ID-Card of the authorized representative, if applicable)

Power of attorney (if someone else is collecting the card for you, provide the "Power of Attorney Declaration for Collection of ID Card" — other forms of authorization cannot be recognized; the authorized person must also identify themselves)
processingTime: Approximately 10 minutes

bookingInfo.office: The citizen service office (Bürgeramt) where you applied for the eID card.

name: Apply for an eID card for EU/EWR citizens
description: This service allows citizens of the European Union or European Economic Area to apply for a German eID card, provided they are at least 16 years old and not German nationals.
eligibility: You must be a citizen of the European Union (EU) or a member of the European Economic Area (EWR) and not simultaneously a German citizen as defined in Article 116(1) of the Basic Law. You must be at least 16 years old and apply in person. You must be registered in Berlin, unless you are not subject to registration and reside in Berlin or abroad (e.g., tourists).
requiredDocuments: Valid identity document issued by your home country (e.g., passport or national identity card/ID-Card)

Proof of residence or address if required (if you do not have a place of residence in Germany, proof of residence in your home country is required; contact the competent German foreign representation for details)
processingTime: Approximately 3 to 4 weeks. In individual cases, the production of the eID card may take considerably longer. Please inquire when submitting your application.

bookingInfo.office: The service can be obtained at all citizen offices (Bürgerbüro) in Berlin.

name: Naturalization - Apply for German Citizenship
description: Apply for German citizenship if you have lived in Germany for a sufficient period, meet language and integration requirements, and satisfy other eligibility criteria.
eligibility: You must have your main residence in Berlin and have lived in Germany for an uninterrupted legal stay of at least 5 years (or 3 years if married to a German citizen for at least 2 years). Your identity and citizenship must be clarified with a valid national passport or ID card. You must commit to the German constitution and reject extremism and terrorism. You must acknowledge Germany's special historical responsibility for Nazi injustice. You must hold a valid residence permit (such as Niederlassungserlaubnis, Aufenthaltserlaubnis, or Blaue Karte EU) or be an EU/EEA/Swiss citizen. You and your family must not receive basic social welfare (Bürgergeld) or social assistance, with exceptions for guest workers or those in full-time employment for at least 20 of the last 24 months. You must have no criminal convictions or ongoing investigations. You must speak German at B1 level (or conversational German if from the guest worker generation). You must demonstrate knowledge of German legal, social order and living conditions. You must not be polygamously married and must respect constitutional gender equality. Children under 16 require consent from both parents with joint custody.
requiredDocuments: Naturalization application (with Quick Check) - submit online and save/print the PDF confirmation
Valid passport or ID card
Vital records documents (marriage certificate, divorce decree, adoption decree with legal force notice if applicable)

For employed persons: Employment contract with salary statements for the last 6 months; Employer certification of continuous employment; Or bank statements showing the last 6 salary deposits if employer does not issue monthly statements

For self-employed or freelance workers: Latest tax assessment notice; Completed audit report form with supporting documents (prepared by tax advisor, auditor, or tax representative); Tax office certificate (tax clearance certificate); Trade register excerpt or business registration (for self-employed); Registration as freelancer with tax office and chamber registration if required (for freelance workers)

For non-employed persons: Unemployment benefit I decision; Pension or retirement benefit decision; Evidence of assets; Basic social welfare (Bürgergeld) or social assistance notice; BAföG or vocational training allowance notice

Evidence of additional benefits: Parental allowance, child allowance, housing allowance, child supplement, orphan pension, startup allowance, or child support payments (as applicable to your situation)
For students, apprentices, trainees: School certificate, apprenticeship certificate, or enrollment certificate; Apprenticeship contract; All school or vocational school report cards

Health and long-term care insurance proof: Electronic health card with photo and current health insurance confirmation (statutory insurance); Or proof of premium payments and current insurer certification (private insurance)
Rental contract with current rent amount or land register excerpt for homeowners

German language proficiency certificate: Deutschtest für Zuwanderer (Level B1); German language certificate at least Level B1 or equivalent/higher diploma; German school report card (9th grade or higher) with German grade of at least 'ausreichend'; Vocational education diploma (Berufsbildungsreife) or equivalent from German school; School-leaving certificate from German general education school; Completion of German-language vocational training in Germany; Completion of German-language university studies in Germany; German-language doctoral degree (Promotion) from German university; State professional license (Approbation)

Proof of knowledge of German legal and social order and living conditions: Certificate for passed 'Leben in Deutschland' test; Certificate for passed naturalization test; Four years of successful attendance at German general education school with at least 'ausreichend' overall grade; Advancement to 10th grade of German general education school (ISS, Realschule, Gymnasium, or Gesamtschule); Vocational education diploma (Berufsbildungsreife) or equivalent from German school; Completion of qualified vocational training in Germany; Completion of university studies at German university or university of applied sciences; German-language doctoral degree from German university; State professional license (Approbation)
Proof of registration (Meldebestätigung)
For children under 16 with joint custody: Consent declaration from the other custodial parent
Additional documents as required by your individual circumstances
fees: €255.00 per person; €51.00 for children under 16 applying together with a custodial parent; Additional costs may apply for release from previous citizenship (inquire at your home country's consulate).
processingTime: The LEA (State Office for Immigration) assumed approximately 40,000 open naturalization cases from Berlin districts as of 01.01.2024. Please expect longer processing times and refrain from requesting status updates.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Naturalization - Register for Citizenship Test
description: Registration service for individuals preparing to take the German citizenship test (Einbürgerungstest) as part of the naturalization process.
eligibility: No prerequisites required.
requiredDocuments: Registration form for citizenship test (completed on-site; the form is provided by the adult education center during consultation)
Valid identification document
processingTime: Test registrations can generally be processed and completed immediately.

bookingInfo.office: This service is available at all Berlin adult education centers (Volkshochschulen) regardless of place of residence.

name: Request Integration Assistance for Adults with Disabilities
description: This service allows adults with disabilities to apply for integration assistance (Eingliederungshilfe) if they have a participation need and a substantial, non-temporary disability.
eligibility: A participation need must exist. A substantial and not merely temporary disability must exist or be imminent. You must belong to the entitled circle of persons under § 99 SGB IX.
requiredDocuments: Application form for integration assistance benefits (can be submitted online or by post; documents can be submitted later if not currently available)
File size requirements for online submission: total maximum 30 MB, individual files maximum 5 MB each, accepted formats: JPG, JPEG, PNG, PDF
Valid identity documents such as national ID card, EU citizen card (eID card), electronic residence permit (eAT), or passport with registration confirmation or registration certificate
Proof of statutory health and long-term care insurance
Decisions from priority benefit providers such as the Employment Agency, Integration Office, pension providers, or health insurance companies
For severe disability: Decision from the Provision Office (Versorgungsamt) on determination of degree of disability and severe disability pass (Schwerbehindertenausweis)
Income documentation such as income tax assessment or pension adjustment notice from two years prior (if available)

Asset documentation such as for capital-building insurance (life insurance, savings contracts, Riester pension contracts, funeral insurance, burial provision, etc.), savings accounts, real estate, property, valuables, vehicles, etc.
The scope of required documents, particularly income and asset documentation, depends on the specific circumstances of the individual case
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: For persons who have previously lived in Berlin and continue to receive integration assistance benefits outside the city of Berlin; For persons receiving personal assistance services (so-called service complex 32 and employer model).

name: Integration assistance for children and adolescents with mental disabilities
description: This service provides integration assistance for children and adolescents whose mental health is significantly impaired and whose participation in society is affected, as determined by the youth welfare office.
eligibility: Determination that mental health is significantly impaired and likely to persist for a considerable duration; decision by the youth welfare office regarding the impact on the child's or adolescent's participation in society.
requiredDocuments: Application submission to the locally responsible youth welfare office
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The locally responsible youth welfare office is the one in the district where the child or adolescent lives with their parents or legal guardians.

name: Berlin Single Point of Contact (Einheitlicher Ansprechpartner Berlin)
description: A single point of contact service in Berlin for entrepreneurs, businesses, professionals, and those seeking professional qualification recognition from Germany, EU, or EWR countries.
eligibility: Service users include: service providers, businesses, founders, and persons seeking professional qualification recognition from the Federal Republic of Germany, a member state of the European Union (EU), or a member state of the European Economic Area (EEA), currently Iceland, Liechtenstein, or Norway. The Einheitlicher Ansprechpartner Berlin is only responsible if you intend to conduct business or professional activities in Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Documentation requirements depend on your specific project; detailed information can be found on the Service Portal Berlin on the respective internet pages of the offered services
fees: The Einheitlicher Ansprechpartner Berlin charges no fees. Information and inquiries are free of charge.
processingTime: Online portals: immediate response; email inquiries: typically up to 3 days

bookingInfo.office: The Einheitlicher Ansprechpartner Berlin accepts inquiries in German and English. Administrative procedures are typically conducted in German, though some online procedures are also available in English. The service accepts inquiries from third countries, though the responsible authorities may reject electronic application submissions via the EA.

name: Income Tax Return - Mandatory Filing
description: This service allows residents who are required to file an income tax return to submit their mandatory annual tax declaration to the Berlin tax office.
eligibility: If you are required to file, you must submit your income tax return by July 31 of the following year (for example, by July 31, 2025 for the 2024 tax year). The tax office can grant you an extension upon request, which you can apply for by mail, fax, email, or phone. When requesting an extension, provide your name, tax number or ID number, the relevant tax year, the desired deadline, and justification. If the tax office approves your extension, you will not receive confirmation unless you explicitly request it. If a tax advisor or tax relief organization prepares your return, the deadline extends to the last day of February of the year following the subsequent calendar year. Special extended deadlines apply due to COVID-19 pandemic impacts: until June 2, 2025 for the 2023 tax year and until April 30, 2026 for the 2024 tax year. You can submit your income tax return electronically, by mail, or in person. If you have income from freelance, business, or agricultural/forestry activities, you must submit your return electronically and authenticated via Mein ELSTER. Paper submissions will not be accepted except in cases of particular hardship.
requiredDocuments: Income tax return forms
Mein ELSTER registration with electronic authentication certificate (registration may take up to two weeks)
Authenticated submission via Mein ELSTER or commercial tax software

For paper forms: obtain free forms from Berlin tax offices or download, fill out, and print from the internet; postage reimbursement only possible if you send a pre-stamped, addressed return envelope (DIN C 5) with form request to your tax office
Supporting documents and receipts (not required to be submitted initially, but keep them available for the tax office to request if needed)
Proof when first claiming disability allowance or if circumstances change
Tax certificates for capital gains tax, if applicable
Certificates for foreign taxes paid (§ 68b EStDV)
processingTime: Approximately 7 to 9 weeks on average from submission. Processing cannot begin before mid-March of the following year, as tax offices receive necessary electronic data from employers, insurers, and other institutions by the end of February. Processing order is based on date of receipt. Individual cases may take longer depending on complexity and content.

bookingInfo.office: Generally, the tax office of your place of residence is responsible.

name: Income Tax Return - Voluntary Submission (Request for Assessment)
description: A service that allows you to voluntarily file an income tax return within a four-year deadline from the end of the tax year.
eligibility: You must submit your voluntary income tax return within a four-year deadline (standard statute of limitations period) from the end of the tax year in question. This deadline cannot be extended. For example, for the year 2022, the deadline is 31 December 2026.
requiredDocuments: Registration on Mein ELSTER to obtain an authentication certificate (registration may take up to 2 weeks)
Income tax return forms submitted via Mein ELSTER or commercial software, authenticated with your electronic certificate

Income tax return forms (available free of charge from Berlin tax offices, or downloadable from the Federal Ministry of Finance website under Frequently Used Forms > Taxes > Tax Forms > Income Tax) — if submitting in paper form, print and mail directly to your tax office; postal submission requires a pre-paid return envelope (DIN C 5) addressed to you with 1.60 Euro postage (Deutsche Post AG); email submission is not permitted

Supporting documents (receipts/certificates) — generally not required to be submitted with the return, but the tax office may request them later if needed for processing; exceptions include: disability allowance documentation (first-time claim or change to previous determination), original tax certificates for creditable capital gains tax (if no favorable review or withholding tax review is requested), and certificates for creditable foreign taxes (§ 68b EStDV)
processingTime: Average processing time is 7 to 9 weeks for income tax returns submitted to Berlin tax offices, regardless of whether submitted by paper or ELSTER. Processing time may vary depending on the scope and content of the individual return.

bookingInfo.office: In general, the tax office of your place of residence is responsible.

name: Request Lump-Sum Funding for Short-Term Care and Day/Night Care Facilities
description: This service allows operators of short-term care, day care, or night care facilities in Berlin to apply for lump-sum funding from the state.
eligibility: The facility must be a short-term care, day care, or night care facility operating in Berlin. A care provision agreement (Versorgungsvertrag) and fee agreement (Vergütungsvereinbarung) must be in place as of January 1st. The number of care places specified in the provision agreement must be available as of January 1st of the funding year and is used to calculate the annual lump sum. An agreement or notice confirming recognized necessary investment costs must be on file. A prior application for separately calculable expenses under § 82 Abs. 3 SGB XI must have already been submitted for the facility.
requiredDocuments: Application for lump-sum funding according to § 6 LPflegEG (to be submitted by email; contact vertrag-kupf@senwgp.berlin.de for short-term care facility operators or vertrag-tapf@senwgp.berlin.de for day/night care facility operators)
Care provision agreement (Versorgungsvertrag) with health insurance funds (may be omitted if already submitted in prior years with no changes)
Copy of current commercial register or association register extract
Power of attorney for any additional authorized representatives
processingTime: The funding decision is typically issued within 4 weeks of application submission. Lump-sum funding payments are made no earlier than June 30th of each year.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: School Entrance Examination
description: A medical examination for children before starting primary school to assess their health and developmental readiness.
eligibility: Minimum age 5 years. The examination takes place before the child starts primary school. Your child must be registered at the primary school.
requiredDocuments: Examination booklet (yellow booklet)
Vaccination record
Glasses or hearing aids if available
Completed parent questionnaire
processingTime: The examination takes approximately one hour.

bookingInfo.office: The service can only be used at the health office (Gesundheitsamt) of the district where the designated school is located.

name: Request Entry-Level Funding for Performing Arts/Dance
description: This service provides entry-level funding for emerging artists and career-changers in performing arts and dance who live and work in Berlin.
eligibility: Applications are accepted from 18 May 2026 to 30 June 2026, with the deadline at 23:59 on 30 June 2026. The project must begin and end in the coming calendar year. You must reside and work in Berlin with residency and employment focus there. You must belong to at least one of these groups: career starters (completed professional training in performing arts/dance of all genres but have not yet had productions in Berlin receive public and critical attention); career changers from other fields (demonstrable professional artistic quality in performing arts/dance but no professional training in this field); career switchers (previously worked as performers but now want to work as artistic leaders like directors or choreographers, and have not received project funding for this new role in the last five years); or re-entrants (completed professional training and are returning after a documented work break of at least five years, and did not receive project funding during the break). Premieres and performances must take place in Berlin. You cannot be enrolled at university or employed as a professor at a university at the time of funding (though you may still be enrolled when applying, you must provide proof of graduation and de-enrollment before funding is granted).
requiredDocuments: Entry-level funding application form for Performing Arts/Dance (submitted online, all documents in PDF format)
Relevant diplomas/certificates and documentation of student or non-independent projects (for career starters)
Evidence of professional artistic quality such as reference letters or links to work samples (for career changers)
Documentation of previous work through samples or project links and reference letters (for career switchers)
Documentation of final works before career break (for re-entrants)
Detailed project description (max. 4 MB, PDF file, max. 8 pages total) including artistic planning, goals, profile, and thematic/aesthetic focus
Artistic CV (max. 2 MB, PDF file)

Detailed financing plan (max. 5 MB, XLSX file) using the provided template, including GEMA fees, KSK contributions, foreign income tax, barrier removal costs, and ticket revenue; amounts must match the online application form
List of project participants/permanent group (max. 1 MB, PDF file)
Venue confirmation, if possible (max. 2 MB, PDF file)

Documentation and information material about previous artistic work, including student projects (max. 4 MB, PDF file), press releases, programmes, cast lists, video links, or website links to work samples

Identity document, proof of primary residence in Berlin, and proof of residence permit if applicable (max. 2 MB, JPEG/PNG/PDF file): for German/EU citizens, copy of both sides of ID card showing Berlin address or Berlin address page from passport plus registration certificate; for non-EU citizens, passport copy, registration confirmation, residence permit with Berlin address and work permission
For group applications: GbR contract or GbR declaration (max. 2 MB, PDF file), stating that at least half of members have primary residence in Berlin
processingTime: 6 months

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Individual Permit for Mopeds, Four-Wheeled Light Motor Vehicles, Motorized Wheelchairs, and Self-Propelled Work Machines and Forklifts with a Maximum Speed of 20 km/h
description: This service issues an individual permit for low-speed motorized vehicles and equipment with a maximum speed not exceeding 20 km/h, based on an expert assessment.
eligibility: Assessment by an officially recognized motor vehicle expert is required to obtain an individual permit.
requiredDocuments: Assessment report from an officially recognized motor vehicle expert for obtaining an individual permit
Purchase contract and, if applicable, proof of the status of the previous individual permit or operating permit
Identity card or passport with registration confirmation
fees: 10.20 euros (according to the current fee schedule for road traffic measures).
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: This service is available exclusively at the Berlin-Lichtenberg vehicle registration authority location. Please note that appointments are only possible by prior arrangement. Submit your appointment request to post.kfz-zulassung@labo.berlin.de.

name: Apply for Individual Project Funding for Performing Arts/Dance
description: This service provides funding support for individual performing arts and dance projects in Berlin that meet specific artistic and residency criteria.
eligibility: Applications are accepted from 18 May 2026 to 30 June 2026, with a deadline of 23:59 on 30 June 2026. Online applications must be submitted by this time; submissions after 23:59 are not possible and incomplete transfers will be automatically cancelled. The project must begin and end in the coming year. Entry-level funding is advertised in the current year for the following calendar year. You must have created and presented at least one production in Berlin that has received public and critical interest. You must reside and work in Berlin, with both your main residence and work focus there. Premieres and performances must take place in Berlin. This funding programme supports the Berlin theatre and dance landscape. You must not be enrolled at a university.
requiredDocuments: Application form for individual project funding for performing arts/dance (online submission required; all documents and evidence must be submitted in PDF format)

Detailed project description (maximum 4 MB, PDF file) — descriptions of which artistic project is planned and how it will be realized; for revivals, documentation of successful premiere in its reception by public and critics, plus justification for the necessity of a revival (e.g. production success). Maximum 8 pages total; applications exceeding 8 pages will be formally rejected.
Artist's CV (maximum 4 MB, PDF file)

Detailed financing plan (maximum 5 MB, XLSX file) — must use the provided template in Excel format XLSX; include mandatory items such as GEMA fees, KSK contributions, foreign tax, administrative fees, and barrier removal costs; include ticket income; yellow-marked rows must not be altered; adjust or supplement other positions as needed; ensure totals in the online application form match the financing plan totals (the application form takes precedence in case of discrepancies).
List of project participants/fixed ensemble (maximum 1 MB, PDF file)

Name/project title of your previous projects in Berlin (maximum 4 MB, PDF file) — upload documentation and supporting materials such as press articles, reviews, programme notes, cast lists, video links, etc.; the jury may view information, photos, and videos on your website if they cannot be uploaded electronically (provide your website link).
Venue certificate (maximum 2 MB, PDF file) — mandatory; applications without this will be formally rejected.

Identity proof, proof of main residence in Berlin, and proof of residence permit if applicable (maximum 2 MB JPEG, PNG, or PDF file) — for German/EU citizens: copy of both sides of ID card (if it shows your registration address) or copy of page with Berlin address from passport or passport replacement plus registration certificate; for non-EU citizens: copy of passport, copy of registration confirmation from the State Office for Civil and Regulatory Affairs, residence permit with Berlin address, and self-employment authorization/supplementary sheet (merged into one file; ensure employment status is visible).
For legal entities (association, GmbH, foundation, etc.): bylaws or partnership agreement plus extract from the association register or commercial register.

For group applications: GbR contract/GbR declaration (maximum 2 MB, PDF file) — either a written GbR contract or, for groups without a written contract, a GbR declaration must be submitted; for a GbR of two persons, one must have main residence in Berlin; for multiple persons, at least half must have main residence in Berlin; failure to submit all required attachments in compliance with these specifications will result in formal rejection.
processingTime: 6 months

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Request Electric License Plate (Elektrokennzeichen)
description: Service to register and obtain a special electric license plate for vehicles with alternative power sources such as battery electric, plug-in hybrid, or fuel cell vehicles that meet specific eligibility criteria.
eligibility: Vehicle must be in classes M1, N1, N2 (up to 4,250 kg), L3e, L4e, L5e, or L7e and powered by an alternative energy source such as: pure battery electric vehicle, externally chargeable plug-in hybrid electric vehicle, or fuel cell vehicle. For plug-in hybrids, the vehicle must emit no more than 50 grams of CO₂ per kilometer or have an electric-only range of at least 40 kilometers. Applicant must have residence in Germany; non-EU residents without German residence must provide a representative with Berlin address; EU citizens must provide foreign address and declare the vehicle's regular parking location in Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Application for vehicle registration (all documents in original)
Vehicle registration certificate Part II (Fahrzeugbrief/Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil II) with COC or certificate of conformity

Certificate of conformity with specific fields completed: Field 22 (for class L) or Field 23 (for M1, N1, N2) for pure electric drive; Field 23.1 for hybrid electric; Field 26 for fuel type; Fields 49.1 and 49.2 (NEFZ cycle) or Fields 49.4 and 49.5.2 (WLTP cycle) for emissions and electric range

Manufacturer's certificate or technical report per §21 StVZO for plug-in hybrid vehicles with fuel codes 0008, 0010, 0012, 0014, 0019, 0022, 0024, 0025, 0026, 0027, 0028, 0029, 0030, 0031, 0033 (if COC data incomplete)
Vehicle registration certificate Part I (Fahrzeugschein/Zulassungsbescheinigung Teil I)
Current license plate(s)
Electronic insurance confirmation (eVB) - only required for registration to new owner
Valid main inspection certificate per §29 StVZO
Identity card or passport with registration certificate (or official certified copy)
Power of attorney if applicable (informal or notarized with ID documents of both parties)
Commercial register extract and business registration in original or certified copy (for businesses)
Association register extract in original or certified copy (for associations)
SEPA direct debit mandate
fees: Starting at €31.80 if the service is not part of a vehicle registration and the vehicle is already registered. Final fee may be higher depending on individual circumstances. License plate production costs are separate and not provided by the vehicle registration authority.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Berlin Vehicle Registration Authority (Kfz-Zulassungsbehörde Berlin); additional appointment slots are released daily as capacity allows.

name: Electronic Institution Card (SMC-B) for Institutions with Healthcare Professionals
description: Apply for an electronic institution card (SMC-B) if your institution employs healthcare professionals who are not organized in professional chambers.
eligibility: You are an institution with employees from healthcare professions not organized in professional chambers. Currently, the following provider institutions can apply for SMC-B through the eGBR (as of 02.04.2025): Midwifery facilities; Health, nursing, and elderly care facilities; Physiotherapy facilities; Ergotherapy practices; Logopedic practices; Podology practices. You must hold authorization to provide services. You must be authorized to represent the institution externally. An employee of the institution must possess an eHBA (electronic health professional ID). For online application: Register/log in via BundID or Mein Unternehmenskonto (MUK). You need your electronic ID card, EU citizen ID card (eID), or electronic residence permit (eAT) and your PIN. Alternatively, have your username/password or ELSTER certificate ready.
requiredDocuments: Application for issuance of SMC-B as an institution with employees not organized in professional chambers (please submit the application online)
Proof of your institution as scan or photo (for example, power of attorney, bylaws)
IK (Institution identification number)
eHBA (electronic health professional ID) number of an employee of the institution
fees: 40.00 Euro administration fee charged by the eGBR. Costs for providing the SMC-B may vary depending on the trust service provider (VDA). The VDA charges an annual fee.
processingTime: 2-4 weeks

bookingInfo.office: As a joint body of the federal states, the eGBR is located at the Regierungsbezirk Münster in North Rhine-Westphalia. Medical professionals, psychotherapists, and pharmacists receive their SMC-B through their professional chambers.

name: Renew Electronic Institutional Card (SMC-B) as an Institution with Employees in Health Professions
description: This service allows institutions with employees in health professions not organized in professional chambers to renew their electronic institutional card (SMC-B) through the eGBR system.
eligibility: You are an institution with employees from health professions not organized in professional chambers. The eGBR system is currently under development. As of April 2, 2025, the following types of provider institutions can renew their SMC-B through eGBR: midwifery facilities; health, nursing and elderly care facilities; physiotherapy facilities; ergotherapy practices; speech therapy practices; podology practices. You must have authorization to provide services. You must be authorized to represent the institution externally. The employee must possess an eHBA (electronic healthcare professional card). For online application: registration/login via BundID or Mein Unternehmenskonto (MUK) using your electronic ID card, EU citizen card (eID card), or electronic residence permit (eAT) with your PIN, or alternatively your username/password or Elster certificate.
requiredDocuments: Application for renewal of SMC-B as an institution with employees not organized in professional chambers (to be submitted online)
Proof of your authorization to represent the institution (as scan or photo) — for example power of attorney or statutes
IK (institutional identification number)
Number of old SMC-B
eHBA (electronic healthcare professional card) number of an employee
fees: 40.00 euros administration fee charged by eGBR. Additional costs for SMC-B provision vary depending on the trust service provider (VDA); VDAs charge an annual fee.
processingTime: 2-4 weeks

bookingInfo.office: As a joint facility of the German federal states, the eGBR is located at the Münster Regional Government (Bezirksregierung Münster) in North Rhine-Westphalia. Medical professionals, psychotherapists, and pharmacists receive their SMC-B through their respective professional chambers.

name: Electronic Wage Tax Deduction Features - Amendment
description: Service to request changes to your electronic wage tax deduction features (ELStAM) within specified filing periods.
eligibility: Changes to ELStAM can be requested from October 1st for the following calendar year, or until November 30th for the current calendar year.
requiredDocuments: Completed application form (forms provided below)
Identity card or passport with residence confirmation (if submitting in person)
Power of attorney from spouse if applicable (required if one spouse is requesting entries on behalf of both spouses)
Application for wage tax reduction
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

requiredDocuments: Application for correction of ELStAM if the stored information is incorrect, the completed form is required
Written authorization from spouse if information for the spouse is also to be requested, their written authorization must be submitted
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The tax office (Finanzamt) responsible for your place of residence is in charge.

name: Apply for Electronic Health Professional Certificate (eHBA) as a Healthcare Professional
description: This service allows non-licensed healthcare professionals in certain regulated health professions to obtain an electronic health professional certificate (eHBA) for digital identification and authentication purposes.
eligibility: You must belong to the professional group of non-licensed persons in a healthcare profession. The eGBR (electronic professional register) is currently being established. As of April 2, 2025, the following professional groups can apply for their eHBA through the eGBR: nursing professionals, geriatric care nurses, health and hospital nurses, health and pediatric nurses, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, speech-language pathologists, podologists, midwives, and emergency medical technicians. For online application, you must register/log in via BundID using your electronic ID card, EU citizen card (eID), or electronic residence permit (eAT) with your PIN, or alternatively with your username and password.
requiredDocuments: Application for issuance of an electronic health professional certificate (eHBA) — please submit the application online
Professional authorization/professional license certificate (as a scan or photo)
If name changed: evidence of name change (for example, marriage certificate)
fees: 40.00 Euro administration fee charged by the eGBR. Additional costs for eHBA provision may vary depending on the trust service provider (VDA). Trust service providers charge an annual fee.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: As a joint facility of the federal states, the eGBR is located at the Bezirksregierung Münster in North Rhine-Westphalia. Medical professionals, psychotherapists, and pharmacists receive their eHBA through their respective professional chambers.

name: Electronic Residence Title (eAT) - Issuance
description: This service allows you to collect your electronic residence title (eAT) after your application for a residence permit has been approved and the card has been produced.

name: Apply for Parental Allowance (Elterngeld)
description: This service allows eligible parents and guardians in Berlin to apply for parental allowance (Elterngeld), a government benefit to support families after the birth or adoption of a child.
eligibility: You must be the mother or father of the child (biological, stepchild, adopted child, or intending to adopt); you must care for and raise the child yourself; you must work no more than 32 hours per week; you must live with the child in the same household; you must reside in Berlin and be registered there; your household's taxable income in the year before the child's birth must not exceed €300,000 (since 01.04.2024: €200,000; from 01.04.2025: €175,000). For online applications, you must register or log in with a BundID account using ELSTER certificate, online ID (eID), or username/password; for eID authentication, you will need an electronic ID card, EU citizen card (eID card), or electronic residence permit (eAT) with activated online ID function and a six-digit PIN, an external card reader or modern smartphone with Android or iOS, and the AusweisApp software.
requiredDocuments: Parental allowance application form (available online or by post; choose the variant based on whether your child was born before, on, or after 1 April 2025)
Identity documents: passports or travel documents including latest registration certificate for each parent
Child's birth certificate (original)
Declaration of previous income for each parent

Income documentation for the 12 months before the child's birth (for employees: salary statements; for self-employed persons and mixed income: latest income tax assessment or, if not yet available, income statement (EÜR) or equivalent proof of income)
Proof from health insurance company regarding maternity allowance (whether it was received and the amount)
Certification from employer regarding employer's supplement to maternity allowance (if applicable)
Agreement with employer regarding parental leave (for non-self-employed)

Confirmation of working hours and expected income during parental leave (for employees: employer's confirmation; for self-employed: your own declaration covering the entire period of parental allowance receipt)
Registration certificate and residence permit for foreign applicants
Berlin amendment application for parental allowance (if changes occur after initial application)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Compensation under Infection Protection Act for Work Ban/Quarantine - Self-Employed
description: Financial compensation for self-employed individuals who suffer loss of earnings due to a work ban or quarantine ordered by health authorities under the Infection Protection Act.
eligibility: You are eligible if: (1) You have received an order for a work ban or quarantine from a Berlin district health authority or a general order applies to you; (2) You have suffered verifiable loss of earnings from your self-employed activity due to the work ban or quarantine; (3) You did not avoid the ban or quarantine through available protective vaccination (for measles since March 1, 2020; for COVID-19 basic immunization since November 1, 2021; for COVID-19 booster since February 16, 2022); (4) You did not avoid the quarantine by not traveling to a risk area. Periods of illness, maternity protection, or times when your self-employed activity was not running for other reasons reduce the compensation period.

Official order (Bescheid) from a Berlin district health authority showing the work ban or quarantine, including address, reasoning, and information on legal remedies

name: Inheritance Law - Declining an Inheritance
description: A service for formally rejecting an inheritance within the required legal timeframe through notarial or court declaration.
eligibility: The deadline to decline an inheritance is six weeks from the date you learn that you have become an heir and the legal basis for this (testament or inheritance contract, statutory succession, or rejection by preceding heirs). The manner in which you receive notice is irrelevant; you do not need to have received a court letter. If you are called to inherit through testament or inheritance contract, the deadline does not begin before the court opens the testament or inheritance contract. If you become an heir through another person's rejection, the deadline begins when you learn of that rejection. A rejection declaration made to a notary must reach the competent probate court by the deadline. You must declare your rejection to the probate court record or to the district court responsible for your residence within the deadline. If booking online, your appointment must fall within the six-week period; if no appointments are available, contact a notary or write to the probate court. A longer six-month deadline applies if you are abroad at the start of the period or if the deceased had their last residence abroad. Special rule for minors: if you do not have sole parental custody, the co-custodian must also reject the inheritance within the deadline; rejection by only one parent is ineffective.
requiredDocuments: Rejection of inheritance declaration in written form with notarial authentication and sent to (or filed at) the probate court, or declared to the probate court record; plain written statements are not sufficient
If abroad, you may make the rejection with help from a German foreign office
Identity card (Personalausweis) or passport (Reisepass) with residence certificate (Meldebescheinigung), to be presented to the notary and court
Death certificate of the deceased (if available; not mandatory—if unavailable, provide the full name including maiden name, death date, and last residence of the deceased)
Names, addresses, and dates of birth of other heirs (children, parents, siblings of the deceased) and of your own children
Family court approval (if applicable) — must be obtained within the deadline if minor children are co-heirs
Guardianship court approval (if applicable) — required if a guardian is making the rejection, must be requested within the deadline
fees: 30.00 Euro minimum fee (depending on the value of the estate); additional costs for notary services (VAT and expenses)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Probate court (Nachlassgericht) in the district where the deceased had their last residence, or the district court (Amtsgericht) in the district of your residence. If the deceased had no residence in Germany at death, the competent court is in the district of their last German residence; if they never had a German residence, it is the court in your district.

The return of an inheritance contract can only be made to all contracting parties jointly.

For handwritten wills: you may choose your own storage location, or opt for official safekeeping at a probate court. For inheritance contracts: these can be deposited for official safekeeping or kept with a notary.

Identity card or passport

name: Application for EU Long-Term Residence Permit
description: This service allows eligible non-EU nationals who have lawfully resided in Germany for at least 5 years to apply for an EU long-term residence permit, provided they meet requirements for income security, health insurance, language skills, and integration.
eligibility: You must be at least 18 years old and currently hold a valid residence permit. Your current residence permit must not have been issued for international, humanitarian, or political reasons (with specific exceptions under German residence law), for education or training purposes, or for any temporary purpose. You must have lawfully resided in Germany continuously for at least 5 years with a valid residence permit (with specific calculations for asylum procedures, study/apprenticeship periods, and EU Blue Card holders). Your livelihood and that of your spouse/partner and children must be secured through your own income, with no reliance on social benefits. You must have adequate health and long-term care insurance (statutory or comparable private). You must have appropriate old-age provision (pension contributions or equivalent, with exceptions for those over 67 or with certified disabilities). You must have no criminal convictions or pending investigations that would endanger public security or democratic order. You must have adequate German language skills at B1 level of the Common European Framework (with exceptions for certified disabilities). You must have basic knowledge of German law and society (demonstrated through integration courses, education, or training in Germany). You must have adequate living space. You must have your main residence in Berlin. You must have a current email address and consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal) for online applications.

name: Reimbursement under the Infection Protection Act for Work Ban/Quarantine - Employers
description: Reimbursement for employers covering wage loss of employees subject to work bans or quarantine orders issued by health authorities.
eligibility: Work ban: An order concerning the individual's work ban or a legal regulation or general order imposing a work ban on the person; Quarantine: An order concerning the individual's isolation or a legal regulation or general order requiring the person to isolate; Lost earnings: Lost earnings are the net wages to which the affected person is entitled based on their regular working hours. The period of lost earnings caused by a work ban or quarantine does not always cover the entire period of the ordered measure. For example, periods during which the affected person has other compensation or wage continuation claims may reduce the measure-related lost earnings period, such as: periods of temporary incapacity, illness periods, training periods, vacation periods, maternity protection periods; Protective vaccination: No compensation is granted to anyone who could have avoided the work ban or quarantine by obtaining a protective vaccination that was legally required or publicly recommended in the area of their usual residence (for measles: generally from 1 March 2020; for COVID-19: for basic immunization by double vaccination generally from 1 November 2021; for COVID-19: for booster vaccination by third vaccination generally from 16 February 2022); Travel: No compensation is granted to anyone who could have avoided the work ban or quarantine by not undertaking an avoidable trip to a risk area already classified as such at the time of departure.
requiredDocuments: Application for reimbursement for work ban/quarantine - Employers (Note: documents must be in JPG, JPEG, PNG or PDF format, with total file size not exceeding 5 MB)
Decree from a health authority of a Berlin district
Notice or certificate from a Berlin health authority
Result of a PCR test
Result of a PoC test (antigen test)
Travel data (boarding card or ticket, exit card, notification to the responsible Berlin health authority, complete travel itinerary for the 10 or 14 days prior to entry into Berlin)
Compensation payments to employees (monthly wage statements for months when measures were ordered, plus wage statements from a comparable month without measures)
Employment contract (including any applicable collective bargaining agreements if contractual provisions were excluded)
Short-time work allowance (if applicable, documentation of daily calculation if employee received Kurzarbeitergeld during the lost earnings period)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: European Professional Card - Application for Issuance
description: This service allows qualified professionals in regulated occupations to apply for a European Professional Card to work temporarily or permanently in other EU/EWR countries.
eligibility: You can use the EPC procedure if you work in one of the eligible professions (general care nurse, pharmacist, physiotherapist, mountain guide, or real estate agent) and wish to practice your profession temporarily or permanently in another EU or EWR country. The eligible professions are: general care nurse (m/f/d), pharmacist (m/f/d), physiotherapist (m/f/d), mountain guide (m/f/d), and real estate agent (m/f/d). Other professionals must use the standard procedure for recognizing foreign professional qualifications.
requiredDocuments: Application for European Professional Card (online only, requires registration with the European Commission's authentication service ECAS)

Evidence documents for the host country (specific documents vary depending on profession, country of origin, host country, purpose of activity, and recognition procedure; consult the EU Commission quick query tool for details)
Identity card or passport (scanned and uploaded as file for electronic application)
Proof of nationality (scanned and uploaded as file for electronic application)
Training certificates and qualifications (scanned and uploaded as file for electronic application)
Certified copies of uploaded documents (may be requested by authorities)
fees: Both your home country authority and the host country authority may charge fees for reviewing your file. You will receive a separate invoice from each authority. Fee amounts vary by home country and host member state; some countries process applications free of charge. Consult the EU Commission quick query tool for specific fee information.
processingTime: Processing time varies based on whether automatic recognition applies. If no host country review is required: 3 weeks maximum. If host country review is required: home country has up to 1 month to review and forward; host country then has up to 3 months maximum to decide. For pharmacists and nurses with automatic recognition: host country decides within 2 months maximum. Without automatic recognition: host country decides within 3 months maximum. Additional aptitude tests or adaptation courses may be required if qualifications do not meet host country standards.

name: European Payment Order Procedure
description: This service allows you to request a European payment order (Zahlungsbefehl) from the competent European payment court for the collection of undisputed claims.
eligibility: To initiate a European payment order procedure, you must submit an application to the competent European Payment Court for the issuance of a payment order. The application is bound to a specific form and can be transmitted in various ways. Applications must be made against debtors with a place of residence or business registered in Germany. For consumer matters, the court where the consumer is resident is competent. Exceptions to this jurisdiction rule are possible (e.g., court agreement, place of performance).
requiredDocuments: European Payment Order Application - request for issuance of a payment order (available under 'Online Processing' or 'Forms')

Application printed and sent by post: You can complete and print the application at the eJustice Portal of the European Union and send it by post. This transmission method is no longer permitted for lawyers, registered debt collection service providers, and since 01.01.2022 also for authorities and legal entities under public law (§ 130 d Code of Civil Procedure)

Application sent electronically: You can complete the application at the eJustice Portal of the European Union and submit it using your ID card with activated online ID function (eID), via the special electronic law office mailbox (beA), the special electronic notary mailbox (beN), the electronic government mailbox (beBPo), the electronic citizen and organization mailbox (eBO), or via My Justice Mailbox (MJP)

No further documents required - as the European payment order procedure is a simplified procedure for undisputed claims, no supporting documents such as receipts, contract copies, etc. need to be attached to the application
fees: Half court fee according to the Court Costs Act (GKG) applies, minimum 38.00 Euro (cost register 1100 to § 34 GKG). Court costs depend on the amount of the claim being asserted. Payment of court costs can also be made by bank transfer if indicated accordingly in the application.
processingTime: 30 days

bookingInfo.office: European Payment Courts (specific court determined by the debtor's place of residence or business in Germany; for consumer matters, the court where the consumer resides is competent)
