name: Report Excessive Rent Increase
description: A service for reporting when rental prices in Berlin exceed the standard local comparison rent by more than 20 percent.
eligibility: Your report concerns a rental apartment in Berlin; your rent is more than 20 percent higher than the standard local comparison rent (check the Berlin Mietspiegel inquiry service). You can determine the standard local comparison rent for your rental apartment using the Berlin Mietspiegel inquiry service.
requiredDocuments: Report of excessive rent (submit via online service; upload documents in JPG, JPEG, PNG, or PDF format; maximum 5 MB per file; maximum 30 MB total)
Rental contract
Additional documents if available (e.g., energy certificate or rent increase letter)
processingTime: Processing time depends on the circumstances of the individual case.

bookingInfo.office: The service can only be accessed through the district office (Bezirksamt) of the district in which the rental apartment is located.

name: Declaration of Maternity (Mutterschaftsanerkennung)
description: A service for unmarried mothers, or mothers with non-German citizenship, to formally declare and register maternity before a registered official.
eligibility: The mother must be unmarried (single, divorced, or widowed), or the mother or father must hold non-German citizenship and the home country law must recognize maternity acknowledgment. The declaration must be made in person before an authorized official (registry office, youth welfare office, or notary). Unmarried mothers under 18 must bring a legal guardian. All documents must be in German or officially translated by a certified translator; some countries require apostille or legalization. Documents in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic script require transliteration of names according to ISO standards. All documents must be original and unaltered.
requiredDocuments: Valid and signed identity card or passport of the mother (original)
Birth certificate of the mother; if the name differs, proof of name change (e.g., marriage certificate)
Maternity record (Mutterpass) — only if acknowledging maternity before birth

Birth certificate of the child — only if acknowledging maternity after birth (required if registering at youth welfare office or with notary; only required at registry office if birth was registered elsewhere)
Any additional documents — may be required depending on citizenship of parents; consultation with the registry office is recommended
fees: €40 at registry office for maternity acknowledgment or consent declaration; free at youth welfare office; free at notary unless combined with custody declaration (then fees apply)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Any registry office regardless of residence; youth welfare office of residence; or the registry office that registered the child's birth (if parents had no or only temporary residence in Germany before the child's birth)

name: Name Change in Vehicle Registration Documents
description: A service to update your name in vehicle registration documents when your name has changed.
eligibility: No prerequisites required.
requiredDocuments: Application for name change in vehicle registration documents
Vehicle registration certificate Part II (Fahrzeugbrief)
Vehicle registration certificate Part I (Fahrzeugschein)
Personal ID or passport and registration certificate (or officially certified copy)
If applicable: power of attorney, including identity document of the grantor unless it is a notarially executed power of attorney, and identity document of the authorized representative
fees: The fee is determined according to the applicable fee schedule for measures in road traffic and is at minimum 12.00 Euro. Please note that this fee may be higher depending on the individual case and the specific application.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Within existing capacity, additional appointments are released daily. Regular checking of the appointment platform is therefore recommended.

name: Name Declaration - Gender-Adapted Form of Married Name According to Sorbian Tradition and Foreign Legal Systems
description: This service allows married persons or former married persons to declare a gender-adapted form of their married name if they have Sorbian heritage or if their country of origin recognizes gender-specific married names.
eligibility: An existing marriage is required; the name adaptation can be declared at or after the marriage ceremony, and remains possible after divorce as long as the married name is retained. Additionally, one of the following conditions must apply: one spouse belongs to the Sorbian people; the spouse has a migration background and their country of origin provides for gender-specific name forms; or the married name is traditionally carried in gender-specific form in a foreign legal system. The declaration must be publicly certified. If either person declaring is not sufficiently fluent in German, an interpreter must be arranged at that person's request and expense.
requiredDocuments: Declaration regarding the adaptation of the married name to gender-specific form (married name declaration) - may be submitted in person at the office
Identity card (Personalausweis) or passport of the declaring person
Marriage certificate (if required) - if the marriage took place abroad, an official translation is additionally required, unless it is an international (multilingual) document
fees: No fee for a married name declaration in connection with marriage registration; 25.00 Euro for a subsequent married name declaration; 12.00 Euro for a certification of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The registry office (Standesamt) that maintains the marriage register. The married name determination becomes effective at the German registry office where the marriage was registered and the marriage register is maintained. The declaration can also be submitted at the registry office of the place of residence. For marriages concluded abroad, the registry office of the place of residence is also responsible.

name: Declaration of Marital or Registered Partnership Name — New Determination / Revocation of Name
description: This service allows married couples or registered partners to establish, change, or revoke their marital or registered partnership name, subject to specific eligibility requirements and time restrictions.
eligibility: For new determinations: the marriage or registered partnership must exist at the time of declaration; such declarations made during marriage are irrevocable while the marriage exists. For existing determinations made before 01.05.2025: the marriage or registered partnership must still be in existence; redetermination as a double name is possible; revocation is only permitted if the original declaration was made before 01.05.2025. If either party does not have sufficient command of the German language, an interpreter must be provided at that party's expense.
requiredDocuments: Declaration of marital name (Ehenamenserklärung) — to be submitted in person at the registry office
Passports or national identity cards of both parties
Marriage certificate (if marriage was solemnized abroad and no international certificate exists, an official translation is required)
Birth certificates (if the marriage was solemnized abroad)
fees: Free for marital name declaration at the time of marriage; €25.00 for a subsequent marital name declaration; €12.00 for a certificate of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The declaration can be submitted at the registry office (Standesamt) of your place of residence. For marriages solemnized abroad, the registry office of your place of residence is also responsible.

name: Name Declaration - Certificate of Name Usage with Missing German Vital Records Entry
description: This service provides a certificate confirming how a person is using their name when there is no corresponding domestic vital records entry, issued by the Berlin Registry Office.
eligibility: A name declaration must have been validly received by the Berlin Registry Office I. Recipients entitled to receive the certificate are the person themselves, parents, grandparents, children, siblings, spouses, or registered life partners, as well as any person who can credibly demonstrate a legal or legitimate interest in obtaining the certificate. Certificates can be requested preferentially via web forms, or alternatively by mail, fax, or in person. Telephone requests are not possible.
requiredDocuments: Proof of relationship or other evidence of legal or legitimate interest
Identity card or passport for in-person application
fees: €12.00 for the certificate; €6.00 for each additional certificate issued at the same time
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Berlin Registry Office I

name: Declaration of Name Rights — Addition or Revocation of a Name to Marital or Registered Partnership Name
description: This service allows married individuals or registered partners to add or revoke an additional name to their existing marital or registered partnership name.
eligibility: A marital or registered partnership name must already be established. The person making the declaration must already use a marital or registered partnership name consisting of a single name. The declaration can only be made by the person whose name did not become the marital or registered partnership name. For revocation: a marital or registered partnership name with a supplementary name (double name) must have been previously established. All required documents must be in German or officially translated by a certified translator in Germany; some countries require additional authentication (Apostille or Legalization). Documents originally in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic must have personal names transliterated according to ISO standards (ISO 9-1995, ISO 843, DIN 31634, ELOT 734, etc.). All original documents must be provided to the registry office unaltered and not perforated or laminated.
requiredDocuments: Declaration form for adding or revoking a name to the marital or registered partnership name (can be submitted in person)
Valid and signed identity card (Personalausweis) or passport from the person making the declaration
Marriage certificate or registered partnership certificate showing the name currently in use
Certificate of name usage (if the name determination does not appear in the marriage or partnership certificate)
Birth certificate (if the marriage or partnership was concluded abroad)
Certified interpreter (if the person making the declaration does not have sufficient command of German language — to be arranged and paid for by that person)
fees: Free: for the declaration made at the time of marriage registration with simultaneous marital name determination; €25.00 for name declaration; €12.00 for a certificate of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Registry Office (Standesamt) that maintains the marriage or partnership register. The declaration becomes effective upon receipt by the German registry office where the marriage was registered or the partnership was established. Alternatively, the declaration can also be submitted to the registry office of the person's place of residence; for marriages concluded abroad, the registry office of the place of residence is responsible.

name: Declaration of Name Change — Name Usage After Dissolution of Marriage or Civil Partnership
description: This service allows individuals who had a marital or civil partnership name to declare a change back to their birth name or previous name, or to combine names after their marriage or civil partnership has been dissolved.
eligibility: A marital or civil partnership name must have been established, the marriage or civil partnership must have been dissolved (typically by divorce, court decree, or death of spouse/partner), and the applicant must be able to provide original documents in German or certified translations. If the applicant does not have sufficient command of German, an interpreter must be arranged at the applicant's expense.
requiredDocuments: Declaration of name change (to be submitted in person at the registry office)
Valid and signed identification card or passport of the declaring person
Marriage certificate or extract from the marriage register (with official translation if marriage was conducted abroad)

Proof of dissolution of marriage — a final divorce judgment or death certificate if dissolution does not appear on the marriage certificate (with recognition of dissolution and official translation if divorce was conducted abroad)
Civil partnership certificate or extract from the civil partnership register (with official translation if civil partnership was established abroad)

Proof of termination of civil partnership — a final court decree on termination or death certificate if termination does not appear on the civil partnership certificate (with recognition of termination and official translation if civil partnership was terminated abroad)
Certificate of name usage (if marital or civil partnership name usage does not appear in the respective certificate; with official translation if partnership was established abroad)
Birth certificate (if marriage or civil partnership was established abroad)

Original documents in German language (foreign language documents require certified German translation and, if necessary, Apostille or legalization); for documents originally issued in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic, personal names must be transliterated according to ISO standards
Interpreter (if required, to be arranged at applicant's expense)
fees: 25.00 Euro for name declaration; 12.00 Euro for certificate of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The declaration can be submitted at the registry office (Standesamt) of your place of residence. If the marriage or civil partnership was established abroad, the registry office of your place of residence is also responsible.

name: Declaration of Name Order - Change the Sequence of Given Names
description: A service allowing individuals with multiple given names to change the order in which those names are registered.
eligibility: You must have multiple given names. If you are under 18 but at least 14 years old, you can submit the declaration yourself, but it requires the consent of your legal guardian(s).
requiredDocuments: Passport or national ID card of the declaring person
Birth certificate showing the person has multiple given names (if born abroad, an official translation is required)
Marriage certificate or registered partnership certificate, if applicable (if the marriage or partnership was registered abroad, an official translation is also required)
Interpreter, if needed at the applicant's expense (required if the declaring person does not have sufficient command of the German language)
fees: €12.00 for the name declaration; €12.00 for a certificate of name registration
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The declaration can be submitted at the registry office (Standesamt) of your place of residence. The name declaration becomes effective at the German registry office where the declaring person's birth was registered and which maintains the birth register. If the birth was not registered in a German register, the registry office responsible for maintaining the person's marriage or registered partnership register is competent. If neither exists, the registry office of the place of residence is competent.

name: Name Adjustment Declaration - Aligning First/Last Name to German Law
description: A service to officially align a name acquired under foreign law to conform with German legal requirements for naturalized citizens, expellees, late resettlers, or those marrying under German law.
eligibility: You must have acquired your name under foreign law and it contains name components or characters unfamiliar to German law. You must be in one of these groups: naturalized citizen, expellee, or late resettler. If you do not belong to these groups, a name adjustment is only possible if your name is to be determined as a marital name under German law. If you are under 18, consent from your legal guardian is required; if you are 14 or older, you must submit the declaration yourself but it still requires guardian consent. If the name being adjusted is a marital name, both spouses must consent. Prior consultation about adjustment options in your specific case is required. Any required documents not in German must be translated by a court-certified interpreter in Germany, and some countries require apostille or legalization. All required documents must be presented in original form to the responsible registry office. If you do not speak German sufficiently, you must arrange and pay for an interpreter.
requiredDocuments: Name adjustment declaration (declaration form to be completed on-site)
Valid identity card (Personalausweis) or passport
Birth certificate, if applicable with official translation
Marriage certificate, if applicable with official translation
Naturalization certificate, citizenship certificate, or document confirming acquisition of German citizenship, if applicable
Registration slip, late resettler certificate, or expellee ID, if applicable
Additional documents as needed (the list above is not necessarily exhaustive; further documents may be required)
fees: No fee for expellees and late resettlers, their spouses, and descendants; €25.00 for naturalized citizens; €12.00 for a certificate of name change
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The registry office (Standesamt) responsible in the location where you were born, or where you were married or entered into a registered partnership, or where you registered the birth or marriage/partnership.

name: Name Declaration - Child's Affiliation Statement to Parental Married Name
description: A service for parents or children to declare the child's affiliation to the parents' chosen married name, available when the child is over 5 years old.
eligibility: The parents have established a married name and the child wishes to adopt this married name. The child must be at least 5 years old. Children aged 5-14 may submit the declaration themselves with parental consent, or parents may submit it as legal representatives. Children over 14 must submit the declaration themselves but still require parental consent.
requiredDocuments: Name declaration form (to be submitted in person at the responsible registry office)
Identity cards or passports (child's if already issued; in all cases, parents' identification documents)
Child's birth certificate (if born abroad, an official translation is required)
Proof of parents' married name (marriage certificate or name certificate)
Interpreter (if any declaring person does not have sufficient command of German, an interpreter must be engaged at the person's request and expense)
fees: 25.00 Euro for name declaration; 12.00 Euro for certificate of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The declaration becomes effective at the German registry office that recorded the child's birth. The declaration may also be submitted at the registry office of the residence. If the child was born abroad, the registry office of the residence is responsible.

name: Name Change Declarations - Adding and Removing Surnames for Children and Adults
description: A service for registering surname changes for minors and adults through an official name change declaration, including adding a spouse's surname or reverting to a previous name.
eligibility: For adding a surname: A spouse's surname must have been chosen by the parents; the child must be a minor with one parent having sole or joint custody and living with that parent and their spouse in the same household, or the child must be an adult with parental consent. The other parent with custody rights or whose name the child bears must consent; children over 5 years old must also consent. For reverting to a previous surname: The marriage of the parent and spouse must have been dissolved, or the child no longer lives in the same household as the parent and spouse.
requiredDocuments: Declaration of surname addition or removal for children and adults (can be submitted on-site)
Identity cards or passports (parents, spouse, child if already available)
Birth certificate of the child (with official translation if born abroad)
Marriage certificate (proof that the custodial parent married a non-parent spouse and a surname was chosen; with official translation if married abroad)
Household registration certificate or residence registration certificate (to prove the custodial parent, spouse, and child live in the same household)
Current negative certificate from the youth office if applicable (if the custodial parent has sole custody)
Declaration of consent if applicable (from the other custodial parent or the child if over 5 years old)
fees: 25.00 Euro for name declaration; 12.00 Euro for certificate of surname usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The registry office (Standesamt) that maintains the birth register where the child's birth was recorded, or alternatively the registry office of the current place of residence

name: Name Declaration - Consent Statement for a Child
description: A service for parents to submit a consent declaration for giving, changing, or adding a name to a child.
eligibility: Name assignment or renaming of the child is desired. Both parents with custody rights, or the sole custodial parent, must submit the declaration. If the child is 14 years or older, the child's personal attendance and own declaration are required, subject to the legal representative's consent. Documents must be in German or officially translated by a court-sworn translator in Germany; for some countries an apostille or legalization is required. For documents originally in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic script, personal names must be transliterated according to ISO standards (ISO 9-1995, ISO 843, DIN 31634, ELOT 734, etc.). All original documents must be presented unaltered and not perforated or laminated. If a declaring person does not speak German, an interpreter must be provided at that person's expense and cost. Declarations may be submitted in advance or at the same time as other required filings. Prior consultation with the registry office is recommended.
requiredDocuments: Valid and signed identity card or passport of the declaring person (original)
Birth certificate of the child
Marriage certificate of the parents or paternity acknowledgment, if applicable, with custody declaration
Negative certificate from the Youth Welfare Office if one parent has sole custody rights
Further documents may be required depending on individual circumstances; consultation with the registry office is recommended if either parent holds a nationality other than German
fees: 25.00 Euro for name declaration; 30.00 Euro for statutory declaration (if applicable); 12.00 Euro for certificate of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Registry office (Standesamt) where the birth was registered if birth was registered in Berlin; residential registry office (Wohnsitzstandesamt) in all other cases; Registry Office I in Berlin if birth and residence are abroad

name: Marital Name Declaration - Declaration - Upon Marriage and Without Domestic Residence
description: This service allows individuals without a domestic residence in Germany to make a declaration regarding their marital name upon marriage or after marriage has taken place.
eligibility: No domestic residence in Germany; existing marriage. A marital name declaration must be submitted by both spouses. It can be made during the marriage ceremony or at a later time. Consultation regarding legal options and requirements is recommended.
requiredDocuments: Marriage certificate (issued by the state registration authority)
Documents proving citizenship, in particular passports/identity cards
Birth certificates of children affected by the name declaration
If applicable, documents proving dissolution of all previous marriages (legally binding divorce judgment) when resuming a former name
If applicable, recognition decision for a foreign divorce when resuming a former name
If applicable, documents regarding deviating name usage
fees: Marital name declaration at the time of marriage is free of charge. Subsequent marital name declaration: €25.00. If applicable, statutory declaration: €30.00. Certificate of name usage: €12.00.
processingTime: Registry Office I in Berlin endeavors to process your application as quickly as possible. In individual cases, processing time of several weeks to several months cannot be avoided, as postal transit times to and from abroad and potential processing times of other authorities (e.g., recognition of foreign divorce judgments) must be taken into account.

bookingInfo.office: This service can only be obtained from Registry Office I in Berlin if you do not have a domestic residence. If you previously had a domestic residence, please contact the registry office responsible for that last domestic residence within Germany.

name: Determining Family Name for a Newborn Child
description: This service allows parents to declare and determine the family name for their newborn child if they do not share a common married name.
eligibility: Both parents must have joint custody and must make a joint decision. If the parents do not have a common married name, they must actively determine the family name within one month of the child's birth. The choice can be the father's name, the mother's name, or a combined name from both (with or without hyphen). The chosen name automatically applies to any further children born to the parents. All required documents must be original documents in German or officially translated by a certified German translator; some countries may require apostille or legalization. Documents originally in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic must have personal names translated according to transliteration standards (ISO 9-1995, ISO 843, DIN 31634, ELOT 734, etc.). If either or both parents are not German citizens, consultation with the local civil registry office is recommended.
requiredDocuments: Declaration on family name for a newborn child (can be submitted on site)
Valid and signed passport or national ID card of both parents
Birth certificates of both parents
Marriage certificate of the parents or paternity recognition with custody declaration
Additional documents as determined by the civil registry office (documentation is not exhaustive; further documents may be required depending on parents' nationality)
fees: No fee for initial registration (Erstbeurkundung); 25.00 EUR for subsequent name declaration (nachträgliche Namenserklärung); 30.00 EUR for statutory declaration if applicable (ggf. Eidesstattliche Versicherung)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Civil Registry Office (Standesamt) of the child's place of birth

name: Name Law Declarations - Determining Registered Partnership Names
description: This service allows partners in an existing registered partnership to retroactively establish a joint partnership name if one was not determined when the partnership was registered.
eligibility: An existing registered partnership must be in place. If no joint registered partnership name was previously determined, this can be done retroactively at any time as long as the partnership is still active. After a registered partnership has been dissolved, determining a partnership name is no longer possible. If one of the declaring persons does not have sufficient command of the German language, a translator must be provided at that person's request and expense.
requiredDocuments: Declaration regarding the registered partnership name (can be completed on-site)
Identity cards or passports of both partners
Registered partnership certificate (if the partnership was established abroad, an official translation is additionally required)
Birth certificates (only if the registered partnership was established abroad)
fees: 25.00 Euro for a retroactive declaration of a registered partnership name; 12.00 Euro for a certificate confirming name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The declaration can also be submitted at the registry office of your place of residence. For registered partnerships established abroad, the registry office of your place of residence is also responsible.

name: Name Declaration - Change Child's Surname by Sole Custodial Parent
description: A service for a parent with sole custody to change their child's surname through a formal name declaration submitted to the registry office.
eligibility: One parent must have sole custody. A name change is only possible if only one parent has custody rights. The consent of the non-custodial parent is required, unless they are deceased. A name change can only occur while the child is a minor; if the child is over 5 years old, the child must consent. All required documents must be in German or officially translated by a court-certified translator in Germany; for some countries, additional authentication (Apostille or legalization) is required. For documents originally issued in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic, personal names must be transliterated according to ISO standards (ISO 9-1995, ISO 843, DIN 31634, ELOT 734, etc.). All required documents must be submitted to the registry office in original form; documents must not be altered, perforated, or laminated. If there is insufficient command of German, a court-certified interpreter is required. Legal consultation is recommended.
requiredDocuments: Name declaration form (submitted in person at the responsible registry office)
Identification documents: passports or ID cards of both parents, and child's ID card if one exists
Child's birth certificate (if born abroad, an official translation is required)
Current negative certification from the Youth Welfare Office (to prove sole custody)
Birth certificate of the non-custodial parent
Death certificate of the non-custodial parent (if deceased)

Additional documents as required (further documents may be needed depending on circumstances; consultation with the registry office is recommended, especially if either parent holds non-German citizenship)
fees: 25.00 Euro for name declaration; 12.00 Euro for certification of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The name change becomes effective at the German registry office (Standesamt) that recorded the child's birth. The declaration may also be submitted at the registry office of the current residence. If the child was born abroad, the registry office of the current residence is responsible.

name: Name Declaration - Establishing a New Birth Name for a Child
description: This service allows parents to declare a new birth name for their child through the civil registry office.
eligibility: Both parents must have joint custody or have successfully contested paternity. Both custodial parents must participate in the declaration. If the child is 14 years or older, the child must be present to make their own declaration, which requires parental consent. If the child has completed their fifth year of life, the name determination is only effective if the child agrees to it. Documents must be in German; non-German documents require translation by a certified translator in Germany and may require apostille or legalization depending on the country of origin. For documents originally in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic, personal names must be transliterated according to ISO standards (ISO 9-1995, ISO 843, DIN 31634, ELOT 734, etc.). All original documents must be unaltered and not perforated or laminated. If declarants do not speak German sufficiently, a certified interpreter must be engaged at their expense. Additional documents may be required depending on the parents' citizenship.
requiredDocuments: Valid and signed identification cards or passports
Child's birth certificate
Parents' marriage certificate or paternity recognition with custody declaration
Court order on contested paternity (if applicable)
fees: 25.00 Euro for name declaration; 30.00 Euro for statutory declaration (if applicable); 12.00 Euro for certificate confirming name
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Civil registry office (Standesamt) where the birth was registered for births registered in Berlin; Residential civil registry office (Wohnsitzstandesamt) in all other cases; Civil Registry Office I in Berlin for births and residence abroad

name: Name Rights Declaration - Parental Election of Surname for a Child
description: A service for parents where at least one parent is a foreign national to make a legal declaration choosing the surname their child will use.
eligibility: At least one parent is a foreign national. Both parents with custody rights, or the sole custodial parent, must appear. If the child is 14 years or older, the child's personal presence is required to make their own declaration, which requires the legal guardian's consent. If documents are not in German, they must be translated by a court-certified translator in Germany. For some countries, documents also require certification (Apostille or Legalisation). For documents originally in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic, personal names must be transliterated according to ISO standards (ISO 9-1995, ISO 843, DIN 31634, ELOT 734, etc.). All required documents must be provided in original form and may not be altered, perforated, or laminated. If the declaring parent(s) do not have sufficient German language skills, a court-certified translator must be engaged at the parent's expense. Consultation with the responsible registry office is recommended if either parent is a non-German national, as additional documents may be required depending on the countries involved.
requiredDocuments: Valid and signed identity cards or passports (original)
Birth certificate of the child
Birth certificates of both parents
Marriage certificate of the parents or paternity acknowledgement, possibly with parental custody declaration
Negative certification from the Youth Welfare Office if one parent has sole custody rights
fees: 25.00 Euro for name declaration; 30.00 Euro for statutory declaration (if applicable); 12.00 Euro for certificate of surname usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Registry office (Standesamt) where the birth was registered: for registration of births in Berlin; Registry office of residence (Wohnsitzstandesamt): in all other cases; Registry Office I in Berlin: for births and residence abroad

name: Declaration of Rights - Spousal Choice of Law Declaration for Marriage
description: This service allows you to file a declaration regarding which law will govern personal and property rights in a marriage when one or both spouses are foreign nationals.
eligibility: At least one spouse is a foreign national. All required documents must be in German or officially translated by a certified translator in Germany. For some countries, additional certification (Apostille or Legalization) is required. For documents originally in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic, personal names must be transliterated according to ISO standards (ISO 9-1995, ISO 843, DIN 31634, ELOT 734, etc.). Original documents are required and must not be altered, perforated, or laminated. If either spouse does not speak sufficient German, a certified interpreter must be present. The declaration can only be filed once; consultation with the registry office is recommended.
requiredDocuments: Valid and signed identification card or passport
Marriage certificate
Birth certificates if marriage took place abroad
fees: 25.00 EUR for name declaration; 30.00 EUR for statutory declaration if required; 12.00 EUR for certificate of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Registry office (Standesamt) where the marriage was registered for marriages registered in Berlin; Registry office of residence for all other cases; Registry Office I in Berlin for marriages registered and residence abroad

name: Name Declaration for Civil Partnership - Election of Law Statement
description: A service for registered civil partners where at least one partner holds foreign nationality to make a formal declaration regarding which law governs their partnership and name rights.
eligibility: One or both civil partners holds a foreign nationality; documents must be in German or officially translated by a sworn translator in Germany; for some countries, additional authentication (apostille or legalization) is required; documents in Arabic, Greek, Hebrew, or Cyrillic script require name transliteration according to ISO standards; all original documents must be unaltered and not perforated or laminated; a sworn translator must be present if the declaring parties lack sufficient German language skills; the declaration can only be made once and legal consultation is recommended.
requiredDocuments: Valid and signed identity cards or passports (original)
Civil partnership certificate
Birth certificates (if civil partnership established abroad)
Possibly additional documents depending on individual circumstances
fees: 25.00 Euro for name declaration; 30.00 Euro for statutory declaration (if applicable); 12.00 Euro for certificate of name usage
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Registry office (Standesamt) where the civil partnership was registered for civil partnerships registered in Berlin; residence registry office for all other cases; Registry Office I in Berlin if the civil partnership was established abroad and the residence is outside Germany

name: Certificate of Non-Existence of Register Entries
description: A certificate confirming that no register entries exist for a specified person, available to eligible family members and those with legal interest.
eligibility: Eligible recipients are the person themselves, their parents, grandparents, children, siblings, spouses, or registered life partners; additionally, any person who can credibly demonstrate a legal or legitimate interest in obtaining the certificate. Applications can be submitted preferably via web forms, or alternatively by post, fax, or in person. Telephone requests are not possible.
requiredDocuments: Proof of kinship or other evidence of legal or legitimate interest
Identity card or passport for in-person submission
fees: 30.00 Euro for registry and document collection review

name: Non-consideration of a Maintenance Obligation of the Debtor in Determining the Exempt Part of the Debtor's Income
description: A request to exclude a dependent person from the debtor's income calculation for wage garnishment purposes if that dependent has sufficient income of their own.
eligibility: The debtor's income is being garnished or is to be garnished. You can submit this request at the same time as the garnishment order or after it has been issued. The dependent person has their own income, and that income is sufficient to cover all or part of their necessary living expenses. Income can include: earnings from self-employment or employment, income from former employment (pension), investment income (such as rental income, interest), or maintenance payments from third parties.

name: Settlement Permission (General) Application
description: Application for a permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) for foreign nationals who meet specific residence, employment, income, health insurance, and integration requirements.
eligibility: You must be at least 18 years old. You must have held a residence permit for at least 5 years (or 3 years if married to or in a registered same-sex partnership with a settlement permit holder for skilled workers, with specific conditions). Your current residence permit must have been issued for family reunion with a foreign family member, employment, self-employment or freelance activity, or humanitarian reasons for non-temporary residence. Certain periods count toward the 5-year requirement: national visas, Blue Card EU, fictitious certificates, and study/training periods (at half rate). For humanitarian permits, asylum procedure periods (up to 2 years) may count; toleration periods do not. You cannot obtain this permit if your residence permit is for study or training purposes, or for temporary humanitarian residence. You must have secured livelihood through your own income (you and your dependents cannot receive unemployment benefits II, XII, or equivalent social assistance). You must have adequate health insurance in Germany (statutory or comparable private insurance). You must have paid contributions to statutory pension insurance for at least 60 months, or equivalent private pension arrangements (exceptions: age 67+, severe disability, or specific training situations). You must have no indicators of endangering public security or order (even fines can prevent issuance). You must have sufficient German language skills at B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference. You must have basic knowledge of German legal order, society, and living conditions. You must have adequate living space for yourself and family members living with you. Your main residence must be in Berlin. You must provide a current email address. For online applications, you must consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal).
requiredDocuments: Settlement permit application (with Quick-Check) — online only; you receive a PDF confirmation that your current residence title remains valid in Germany beyond its expiration date (does not apply to Schengen C visas for short-term stays); save and print this document

Income evidence if not employed: unemployment benefit I decision, pension/retirement benefit decision, asset proof, unemployment benefit II or social assistance decision, or BAföG/training assistance documents

Health insurance proof: electronic health card copy (front and back) or current insurance confirmation (for statutory insurance) or insurer certification of coverage and costs per SGB V § 257 Abs. 2a (for private insurance)

Education certificates: transcripts and diplomas from German training or studies

Knowledge of German legal/social order and living conditions: integration course completion, orientation course completion, 'Living in Germany' test certificate, citizenship test certificate, 4+ years of successful German schooling, promotion to 10th grade, German vocational qualification or 1+ year vocational training in Germany, German university degree, German doctoral degree, or state professional licensing (Approbation)
Medical certificate from specialist doctor (if claiming exemption due to physical, mental, or psychological illness or disability)

name: Apply for a Settlement Permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) as an Asylum Beneficiary or Recognized Refugee
description: This service allows asylum beneficiaries and recognized refugees in Berlin to apply for a permanent settlement permit if they meet specific eligibility criteria regarding residence duration, language proficiency, income, health insurance, and conduct.
eligibility: You must hold a residence permit as an asylum beneficiary, recognized refugee, or resettlement refugee granted under § 25 Abs. 1 or 2 (GFK) or § 23 Abs. 4 Aufenthaltsgesetz for at least 3 years (requirements are easier if held for 5+ years). Time spent in asylum procedures or other permitted stays counts. Grounds for asylum or refugee status must still exist and not be subject to withdrawal. You must have secured livelihood through your own income (public benefits should not exceed 25% of total income, or 50% if you've held the permit for 5+ years; exemptions apply for those 67+ or with medical conditions). You must have adequate health insurance in Germany (statutory or comparable private insurance). German language proficiency is required at C1 level (if permit held 3+ years) or A2 level (if held 5+ years); exemptions apply for medical reasons. You must have no indicators of endangering public security or order, and must not engage in violence for political or religious purposes. You must have basic knowledge of German legal and social order (demonstrated by integration course completion, German educational qualification, or 1+ year of vocational training in Germany). You must have adequate living space for yourself and family members. Your primary residence must be in Berlin. You must provide a current email address.

name: Apply for Settlement Permit for Skilled Workers
description: A settlement permit for qualified skilled workers with professional or academic qualifications who have worked in Germany for a specified period and meet various integration and financial requirements.
eligibility: You must have been employed as a skilled worker with a vocational or academic qualification, or in research, for at least 3 years (or 2 years if you completed vocational training or university studies in Germany). You must hold a residence permit that allows skilled worker employment (such as permits under § 18a, § 18b, or § 18d of the Residence Act) for at least 3 years; time holding a national D visa counts toward this period. You must continue to be employed as a skilled worker. You must have made pension insurance contributions for at least 36 months (or 24 months if you completed vocational training or studies in Germany) to statutory pension insurance or a comparable private pension provider. You must demonstrate German language skills at level B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). Your livelihood and that of your close family members (spouse/registered partner and children) must be secured through your own income, and you must not receive or be entitled to receive benefits under the German Social Code (such as Bürgergeld or social assistance). You must have health insurance in Germany, either statutory or private comparable coverage. You must have no criminal convictions or pending criminal investigations. You must have basic knowledge of the legal and social order and living conditions in Germany (demonstrated by completing an integration course, orientation course, or German schooling/training). You must have sufficient living space for yourself and family members living with you. You must have your main residence in Berlin (a secondary residence is not sufficient). You must provide a current email address.

Knowledge of legal and social order: certificate of successfully completed integration course; certificate of successfully completed orientation course; certificate of successfully completed 'Living in Germany' test; certificate of successfully completed citizenship test; at least 4 years of successful attendance at German general education school (promotion to next grade) with final school report grade of at least 'satisfactory'; promotion to tenth grade of a German general education school; acquisition of German basic vocational qualification or equivalent educational standard or school leaving certificate; successful completion of German qualified vocational training or completion of equivalent training in Germany for at least one year; successful completion of studies at German university or technical college; German-language doctoral degree from a German university; or state authorization for independent professional practice (Approbation)

name: Application for Settlement Permit for Family Members of German Citizens
description: This service allows family members of German citizens to apply for a settlement permit (permanent residence) in Germany if they meet specific eligibility requirements including continuous legal residency, family relationship, financial self-sufficiency, health insurance, and German language skills.
eligibility: You must have lawfully resided in Germany continuously for at least 3 years with a valid residence permit (national visa, residence permit, or Blue Card EU); maintain a family relationship with a German citizen (spouse, same-sex registered partner, minor child, or parent) that has existed continuously for at least 3 years in Germany; ensure your livelihood and that of your family members is secured through your own income without requiring benefits from jobcenters or social welfare offices (exceptions apply for permanent disability with medical certification); maintain adequate health insurance (statutory or comparable private insurance in Germany); have no deportation interests (no criminal convictions, ongoing investigations, or threats to public order or security); possess adequate German language skills at level B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (GER), or A1 if you held a residence permit before September 6, 2013 (exceptions apply for permanent disability with medical certification); have your primary residence in Berlin (secondary residence is insufficient); and provide a current email address for contact.

description: This service allows Blue Card EU holders who have worked for a specified period in Germany and meet certain conditions to apply for an unlimited settlement permit.

For online applications, you must consent to electronic payment methods.

name: Apply for Settlement Permit for Children (Age 16+)
description: A permanent residence permit application for foreign-born children aged 16 and older who meet specified eligibility requirements including length of residence, education or income status, and integration criteria.
eligibility: Applicant must be at least 16 years old. Applicant must have held a residence permit continuously for 5 years by the time they turn 16. Applicant must either be currently enrolled in education leading to a recognized qualification (school, vocational, or academic) or, if not in education, must have secured livelihood through own income without relying on jobcenter benefits, social welfare, or youth welfare services (exceptions apply for documented illness or disability). Applicants aged 18+ must demonstrate German language proficiency at CEFR level B1 (exceptions apply for documented illness or disability). Applicant must have valid health insurance in Germany (statutory or comparable private insurance). Applicant must have no indications of endangering public security or order, no criminal convictions, no ongoing investigations, and must not participate in violence for political or religious purposes. Applicant must have primary residence in Berlin (secondary residence is insufficient). Applicant must provide current email address. If under 18, a legal guardian (typically parent) must submit the application on applicant's behalf. For online application, applicant must consent to electronic payment methods (credit card or PayPal).

name: Settlement Permit for Self-Employed Entrepreneurs
description: A permanent settlement permit for non-EU nationals who have been operating an independent business in Berlin for at least 3 years and meet income, insurance, and other requirements.
eligibility: Applicants must have held a residence permit for independent business activity under § 21 Section 1 or 2a of the Residence Act for at least 3 years (or 5 years if self-employed under § 21 Section 5). Income from the business must cover living expenses for the applicant and any dependents. Adequate health insurance is required for the applicant and dependents. As of July 1, 2025, applicants must demonstrate either a monthly pension of €1,612.53 (for at least 12 years) or assets of €232,204.00 upon reaching age 67. No criminal convictions (even fines can prevent approval). Primary residence must be in Berlin.

description: Application for a permanent settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) for individuals holding subsidiary protection status or federal sponsorship residence permits who meet specific eligibility criteria.
eligibility: You must be at least 18 years old; have held a residence permit for at least 5 years (either under § 23 Abs. 2 or § 25 Abs. 2 AufenthG for subsidiary protection; asylum procedure periods count toward this requirement for up to 2 years, but periods with only a toleration notice do not); have secured living expenses for yourself and close family members (spouse/partner and children) through your own income without receiving social benefits (Bürgergeld, Sozialhilfe) or having a claim to them (exceptions apply for those unable to work due to permanent physical, mental, or psychological illness with medical certification); have adequate health insurance in Germany (statutory or comparable private insurance); have paid contributions to statutory pension insurance for at least 60 months or equivalent private pension provisions (or be age 67 or older, or have a documented permanent disability); show no indicators of endangering public security or constitutional order (criminal convictions, even fines, can prevent approval; ongoing criminal investigations bar processing); demonstrate sufficient German language skills at B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference (verified through integration course completion or language certificate, with exemptions for those unable to learn due to permanent illness); possess basic knowledge of the legal and social order and living conditions in Germany (verified through integration course, school/vocational qualification in Germany, or at least one year of school/vocational training in Germany); have adequate living space for yourself and family members; have your main residence in Berlin; and provide a current email address for contact.
