Training contract (for students, trainees, or university students)
All school or vocational school certificates (for students, trainees, or university students)
Electronic health card copy (front and back) or current health insurance confirmation (for statutory health insurance)
Insurance company certification regarding scope and costs of coverage under § 257 Abs. 2a SGB V (for private health insurance)
Rental contract without house rules and supplementary documents (for rental housing)
Documentation of current monthly costs (warm rent), such as bank statements (for rental housing)
Land register extract, Section 3 (for owned property)
Monthly housing association fees (for owned property)
Monthly credit costs for the property if applicable (for owned property)
Pension information or pension statement from German Pension Insurance or documentation of comparable benefits from other insurance or pension providers
Documentation of income from personal or business assets
Certificates or diplomas of educational achievement (if vocational training or university degree completed in Germany)
Deutschtest für Zuwanderer language certification (if German language skills B1 level not obtained through German education)
Zertifikat Deutsch or other language diploma (if German language skills B1 level not obtained through German education)
Integration course final test (if German language skills B1 level not obtained through German education)
Integration course final test (for knowledge of legal and social order, if no school or vocational training completed in Germany)
Orientation course "Living in Germany" final test (for knowledge of legal and social order, if no school or vocational training completed in Germany)
Successfully completed citizenship test (for knowledge of legal and social order, if no school or vocational training completed in Germany)
Medical certificate from a specialist physician (if claiming exemption due to physical, mental, or psychological illness or disability)
processingTime: If your application is approved, you will receive an appointment for an in-person interview. At the interview, you will receive written confirmation of lawful residence until the settlement permit is issued. After the appointment, it takes a minimum of 4 weeks for the settlement permit to be issued as an electronic residence document and made available for collection.

bookingInfo.office: This service can only be obtained at the State Immigration Office (Landesamt für Einwanderung — LEA) at the Friedrich-Krause-Ufer location.

name: Reissue of Settlement Permit or EU Long-Term Residence Permit
description: This service allows you to obtain a reissued settlement permit or EU long-term residence permit if your existing permit needs to be updated due to a new passport or expired electronic residence card.
eligibility: You must possess an unlimited residence title (settlement permit or EU long-term residence permit); AND one of the following applies: you received a new passport and your unlimited residence title was still affixed as a sticker in your old passport; OR you received a new passport and your electronic residence permit (eAT) still references your old passport; OR your electronic residence permit (eAT) card has expired (eAT cards are valid for a maximum of 10 years, but your unlimited residence title remains valid); AND you have your main place of residence in Berlin; AND you must attend in person with an appointment. For reissuance at a Citizens' Office, your unlimited residence title must have been issued by the Foreign Office/State Office for Immigration Berlin or last reissued by a Berlin Citizens' Office, and if reissuance is due to a new passport: you must possess the expired passport, no more than 6 months have passed between the expiration of your old passport and the issuance of your new passport (or 12 months for EU long-term residence permits), and you have not been continuously abroad for more than 6 months (or outside the EU for more than 12 months for EU long-term residence permits).
requiredDocuments: Your current passport
Your old passport (if reissuance is due to a new passport)
Police report of passport theft (if your passport was stolen and you reported it to the police)
Your unlimited residence title: either an electronic residence permit (eAT) together with the supplementary sheet, or your old passport with the affixed residence permit

1 current biometric passport photo (as of 01.05.2025, biometric passport photos may only be created digitally directly at the authorities or at photo studios/drugstores that can transmit them to the authorities via a secure electronic method)
fees: €67.00 for adults; €33.50 for minors; €27.60 for Turkish nationals up to age 24; €46.00 for Turkish nationals from age 24; no fee if you provide current proof of receiving benefits under SGB II (Hartz IV) or XII (social assistance/basic security) or the Asylum Seeker Benefits Act, for resettlement refugees (under § 23 paragraph 4 sentence 1 of the Residence Act), for asylum beneficiaries, or for foreigners with refugee or subsidiary protection status in Germany. Additional costs: €6.00 for creating a digital passport photo at a self-service terminal on-site; €15.00 for direct mail delivery of the residence permit to your home.
processingTime: Approximately 3-4 weeks after your appointment until the settlement permit or EU long-term residence permit is issued as an electronic residence permit.

bookingInfo.office: Citizens' Office (Bürgeramt): The service can generally be obtained at any Berlin Citizens' Office if the conditions stated in the eligibility section are met. State Office for Immigration (Landesamt für Einwanderung): The LEA is responsible for all other cases.

name: Appoint a Notary Representative
description: This service allows a notary to appoint a representative to act on their behalf during a period of complete inability to perform their duties.
eligibility: Appointment of a representative is only permitted if and as long as the notary is completely prevented from performing their duties. A representative appointment cannot be made if the notary is only prevented from performing individual official activities. The appointment of a notary representative must not result in compromising the principle of personal performance of duties or doubling the work capacity of the notary. The notary who wishes to be represented must submit the application.
requiredDocuments: Application for appointment of a notary representative (may be submitted by mail or fax)
Self-disclosure form (Questions 1-12) from proposed representatives, only if they are not themselves notaries
fees: €51.13 for the first appointment in the current calendar year; no fee for each subsequent appointment in the calendar year
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Public Contract - Price Review
description: A service for public contracting authorities in Berlin to request a price review of public contracts awarded to Berlin-based companies.
eligibility: You are a public contracting authority and have awarded a public contract to a Berlin-based company.
requiredDocuments: Application for price review
Contract and, if available, contract amendments
Contract documents
Service description
Final invoice
processingTime: Average processing time cannot be specified as it is determined primarily by the individual review effort required.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Online ID Function (eID) - Change or Set PIN
description: This service allows you to change or newly set your PIN for the online identification function on your German ID card, EU/EEA citizen card, or electronic residence permit.
eligibility: The online ID function chip must already be activated on your valid German personal ID card, EU/EEA citizen card (Unionsbürgerkarte), or electronic residence permit (eAT). You must either not have your PIN letter or no longer know your current PIN. Personal appearance is required — you must appear in person with your ID card to set or change your PIN on-site.
requiredDocuments: Application form for resetting the PIN for online ID function (eID) — only available in person on-site
Personal ID card, eID card, or eAT with activated online ID function
processingTime: Immediate

bookingInfo.office: Bürgeramt (Citizens' Office) — Subsequent activation (except for eAT) is possible at all Berlin Bürgerämter of your choice, regardless of your main residence in Berlin, and without prior appointment booking. Some locations optionally also offer appointment booking. Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA) (State Immigration Office) — For holders of an electronic residence permit (eAT), the LEA is responsible. Please contact your responsible department via the contact form.

name: Retroactively Activate Online ID Function (eID)
description: This service allows eligible residents to retroactively activate the online identification function on their valid German ID card, EU/EEA citizen card, or electronic residence permit.
eligibility: You must be at least 16 years old and have a valid German Personalausweis, eID card for EU/EEA citizens (Unionsbürgerkarte), or electronic residence permit (eAT) with the online ID function not yet activated. The chip must not be activated. If you were under 16 when your ID was issued, the chip is deactivated by default and can be activated after your 16th birthday. You must apply in person at an office.
requiredDocuments: Application for retroactive activation of the chip for the online ID function (eID)
Valid Personalausweis, eID card, or eAT with inactive online ID function
processingTime: Immediate

bookingInfo.office: Bürgeramt (Citizen's Office) — Retroactive activation (except for eAT) is available at all Berlin Bürgerämter of your choice, regardless of main residence in Berlin, without prior appointment booking. Some locations optionally offer appointment booking. Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA) — For electronic residence permit (eAT) holders, LEA is responsible. Please contact your responsible department via contact form.

name: Victim of Violence - Counseling and Support
description: This service provides counseling and support for individuals who have experienced violence, witnessed a violent act, or are relatives of violence victims.
eligibility: You have experienced violence; You are a witness to a violent act; You are a relative of a violence victim. Appointments must be arranged via email: kundencenter-beratung@lageso.berlin.de
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: This service is only available at LAGeSo - Versorgungsamt - Kundencenter. Please arrange an appointment via email: kundencenter-beratung@lageso.berlin.de

name: Request Assistance for Victims of Violence Under Social Compensation Law
description: This service provides financial and medical support to victims of violent crimes, witnesses who suffered psychological harm, and relatives of victims who experienced shock-related injuries.
eligibility: You are a victim of a violent crime and have suffered health damage as a result; OR you are a witness to a violent crime and have suffered psychological injury (shock damage); OR you are a close relative of a victim of a violent crime and have suffered psychological injury (shock damage).
requiredDocuments: Application for compensation for victims of violence (can be submitted in writing by post)
processingTime: Approximately 295 days

bookingInfo.office: This service can only be accessed at the Local Welfare Office (Versorgungsamt)

name: Change Resident Parking Permit
description: This service allows resident parking permit holders to modify their existing permit due to changes such as a new vehicle registration number, change of vehicle owner, or relocation to a different parking zone.
eligibility: You are the holder of a resident parking permit and there is a change: new vehicle registration number; change of vehicle owner (vehicle change); change of residence/relocation to a different parking zone (not yet possible online); or return of your previously valid resident parking permit (upon request). You must remain a resident at the same address in a parking management zone. You must be the registered owner of the new vehicle or demonstrably use it permanently, or if changing the registration number, the previous conditions remain unchanged (this also applies to rental vehicles). For online application: consent to electronic payment method — you will pay electronically directly in the online process by credit card (Visa, Mastercard).
requiredDocuments: Application for change of a resident parking permit (can be submitted online, by post, or in exceptional cases in person at the district citizens' offices of the parking zone)
Parking permit number

Vehicle registration certificate Part 1 (copy) — a copy of the complete unfolded front page of the vehicle registration certificate is necessary, showing the name and address of the registered owner, vehicle type, technically permissible gross weight, and official registration number

Identity document (copy) — for written application or in-person application: copies of both sides of identity card as proof of registered address; if using a passport or if actual residence is not entered in the identity card (e.g., secondary residence), additionally submit consent for official access to the registration register or alternatively a current registration certificate
Written power of attorney (only required if someone is authorized to change and receive the parking permit on your behalf)
Return of your previously valid resident parking permit (return your old permit; if the old sticker is damaged during removal, return the remains)
fees: 10.20 euros for modification of an existing resident parking permit. For written application, you will receive the resident parking permit and a fee notice with payment request. At some locations, payment on-site only is possible.
processingTime: Up to 4 weeks. Processing time may be delayed if required documents are submitted incompletely.

bookingInfo.office: Submit the application in the district where the parking management zone is located. Exception: For the entire Flottwellstraße, the Mitte district office is responsible.

name: Apply for Resident Parking Permit
description: A service that allows residents registered in a controlled parking zone to obtain a parking permit for their vehicles.
eligibility: You must be registered and actually reside within a controlled parking zone (in Berlin, a registered secondary residence is sufficient). You must be the registered owner of an approved vehicle or have documented permanent use rights (including rental cars). For online application, you must consent to electronic payment via credit card (Visa, Mastercard).
requiredDocuments: Application form for resident parking permit (can be submitted online, by post, or in person at district offices)
Vehicle registration certificate Part 1 (copy of complete front side)
Identity document copy (both sides of ID card, or passport with additional registration confirmation or consent for registry access)
Proof of permanent vehicle use rights if you are not the registered owner (e.g., written declaration from owner, or for rental cars: confirmation from rental company)
Carsharing contract (copy) if you are a carsharing member
Written power of attorney if applying on behalf of another person
fees: €20.40 for issuance of resident parking permit. For written applications, you will receive a fee notice with payment request. Payment may only be possible on-site at some locations.
processingTime: Up to 4 weeks. Incomplete submission of required documents will delay processing.

bookingInfo.office: Apply at the district office (Bezirksamt) of the district where the controlled parking zone is located. Exception: Flottwellstraße is under the jurisdiction of Mitte district office.

name: Resident Parking Permit Replacement
description: This service allows residents to replace a lost or damaged resident parking permit for a vehicle registered in their name in a parking management zone.
eligibility: You have lost or damaged your valid resident parking permit; you remain a resident of a parking management zone; you remain the registered owner of a licensed vehicle or have permanent use authorization (including rental vehicles); for online applications, you must consent to electronic payment via credit card (Visa, Mastercard).
requiredDocuments: Application for replacement resident parking permit (can be submitted online, by post, or in exceptional cases in person at district citizen offices)
Resident parking permit number

Vehicle registration certificate Part 1 (copy) — a copy of the complete front page of the registration certificate showing the owner's name and address, vehicle type, maximum permitted mass, and official license plate

Identity document (copy) — for postal or in-person applications: copy of both sides of ID card serving as proof of registered address; if using a passport or if actual residence is not listed on the ID card, submit consent for authority access to the resident registry or alternatively a current residence certificate
Proof of loss or damage — must be substantiated by receipts and/or written confirmation, such as police loss report or other loss declaration
Written power of attorney (only if someone else is applying for and receiving the permit on your behalf)
fees: 10.20 Euro for replacement issuance; for postal applications you receive a fee notice with payment request; payment may be required on-site at some locations.
processingTime: Up to 4 weeks; processing time may be delayed if required documents are incomplete.

bookingInfo.office: Apply in the district where the parking management zone is located; exception: Flottwellstraße is handled by the Mitte district office.

name: Renew Resident Parking Permit
description: This service allows residents of a parking management zone in Berlin to renew their resident parking permit before it expires.
eligibility: You must be the holder of a parking permit expiring within a maximum of 1 month; You must be a resident of a parking management zone (registered with the registration authority and actually living there; in Berlin, a registered secondary residence is sufficient); You must be the registered owner of a licensed vehicle or have documented permanent use of it (this also applies to rental cars); For online applications: you must consent to electronic payment via credit card (Visa, Mastercard).
requiredDocuments: Application for reissuance (renewal) of a resident parking permit
Parking permit number
Vehicle registration certificate Part 1 (copy of both sides)
Identity proof (copy) — for postal or in-person applications
Proof that you have permanent use of the vehicle if you are not the registered owner (e.g., written declaration from the vehicle owner, or for rental cars: confirmation from the rental company)
Carsharing contract (copy) if applicable
Written power of attorney if someone else is submitting the application on your behalf
fees: 20.40 Euro for reissuance (renewal) of a resident parking permit. For postal applications, you will receive the permit and a fee notice with payment request. At some locations, payment on-site only is possible.
processingTime: Up to 4 weeks. Processing time may be delayed if required documents are submitted incompletely.

bookingInfo.office: Apply for the resident parking permit at the district office (Bezirksamt) of the district where the parking management zone is located. Exception: For the entire Flottwellstraße, the responsible office is Bezirksamt Mitte.

name: Request Guest Parking Permit (Gästevignette)
description: A parking permit service that allows guests of residents in parking management zones in Berlin to park for up to 4 weeks, with eligibility based on special circumstances such as disability or residency outside Berlin's postal code ranges.
eligibility: You must have special grounds for exemption, such as health restrictions (e.g., guests with severe disabilities or equivalent status); be a guest of a resident in a parking management zone (permit issued for maximum 4 weeks); be the registered owner or authorized permanent user of the vehicle (including rental cars); have your residence outside postal code ranges 10000-16999 (permit also valid for vehicles with Berlin or Brandenburg license plates and rental cars); or be applying for a replacement due to loss or damage of an existing permit.
requiredDocuments: Completed and signed application for guest parking permit (Antrag auf Ausstellung einer Gästevignette)
Proof of special urgency, such as: EU parking permit, special parking permit for severely disabled persons (Gleichgestellte), severe disability ID with "G" designation, or medical certificate
Vehicle registration certificate Part 1 (copy) — if vehicle has Berlin/Brandenburg license plate registered outside postal code range 10000-16999
Proof that vehicle is available for your permanent use (if you are not the registered owner) — written declaration from owner or rental car company confirmation

ID document (copy of both sides) — for address verification and identity of host and guest; if using passport or actual residence differs from ID address, also provide consent for authority access to resident registry or current registration certificate
Proof of loss or damage (if applicable) — documented evidence or written confirmation supporting the claim
fees: €10.20 for up to 3 days; €13.00 for up to 1 week; €15.00 for up to 2 weeks; €20.00 for up to 3 weeks; €25.00 for up to 4 weeks
processingTime: Approximately 14 days

bookingInfo.office: Apply at the district office (Bezirksamt) where the parking management zone is located and where the host is registered. Exception: For Flottwellstraße, apply to the Mitte district office (Bezirksamt Mitte).

name: Apply for a Tradesperson Parking Permit
description: This service allows tradespeople from specified trades and sectors to apply for a parking permit that authorizes them to keep vehicles at their work sites in Berlin.
eligibility: Applicants must belong to a specific trade or economic sector listed in the official reference (or a comparable area with documented justification). There must be an absolute necessity to keep vehicles at the work site.
requiredDocuments: Application form for tradesperson parking permit (online or paper submission)
Proof of membership in a specified trade or economic sector (tradesperson card, commercial register extract, or chamber of commerce certificate)
Copy of vehicle registration certificate (Part 1)
Proof of permanent use authorization if vehicle is not registered to the applicant (e.g., for leased vehicles)
Photographs of all vehicles listed in the application showing the vehicle and license plate clearly
Written declaration: 'I declare that I depend on my vehicle(s) for transporting bulky materials and urgently need them at my work site to carry out my profession'
Work site verification form (not part of the permit application but required for permit validity)
fees: €130 for up to 6 months; €200 for up to 12 months; €350 for up to 24 months. Additional vehicle registration: €25 (6 months), €40 (12 months), or €70 (24 months) per vehicle, maximum 3 additional vehicles per permit.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Responsibility lies with the individual districts (Bezirke). Tradesperson parking permits can be applied for in all districts. Districts without parking management forward applications to districts that manage parking and issue permits.

name: Parking Permit for Severely Disabled Persons
description: This service issues a special parking permit for severely disabled persons with specific mobility or vision impairments who reside in Berlin.
eligibility: Requires a certificate of severe disability (Schwerbehindertenausweis) with the designation aG (exceptionally mobility impaired) or Bl (blind). If the aG designation was not granted, a certificate of equivalence (Gleichstellungsbescheinigung) from the social welfare office must be presented in addition to the disability certificate. Main place of residence must be in Berlin. The application is submitted to the district traffic authority (Straßenverkehrsbehörde) where your main residence is located.
requiredDocuments: Application form from the responsible authority
Copy of disability certificate (Schwerbehindertenausweis)
Copy of decision from the social welfare office (Versorgungsamt)
Copy of ID card (Personalausweis)
Passport-sized photograph (required only for EU parking permit)
Certificate of equivalence from the social welfare office (if applicable)
processingTime: 4 weeks

bookingInfo.office: The service is available at the district traffic authority (Straßenverkehrsbehörde) in the district where your main place of residence is located. An in-person visit is not required.

name: Parking facilities for severely disabled people - person-specific designation - person-bound
description: This service provides designated parking permits for severely disabled people who hold an EU disability parking pass and do not have suitable private parking available.
eligibility: EU disability parking pass required; no suitable parking available on private property (e.g., own property, tenant parking space, employer parking spaces); as a rule, the permit holder must themselves participate in road traffic
requiredDocuments: Written application to the responsible authority
Copy of vehicle registration document part I (vehicle registration certificate)
processingTime: 4 weeks

bookingInfo.office: The traffic authority (Straßenverkehrsbehörde) at the local government office (Ordnungsamt) responsible for your main residence or workplace. Personal attendance is not required.

name: Identity Card - Exemption from ID Requirement
description: A service for German citizens with limited public participation or without valid travel documents to request an exemption from the requirement to carry an identity card.
keywords: unable to participate in public life
eligibility: You must be a German citizen with main residence in Berlin. You qualify if at least one of the following applies: you are permanently accommodated in a hospital, nursing home, or similar facility; a legal guardian or caregiver is permanently appointed for you; you cannot move alone in public due to a disability; or you no longer have a valid identity card or passport (due to expiration, theft, or similar reasons).
requiredDocuments: Written application using the form 'Antrag auf Befreiung von der Ausweispflicht' (can be submitted by post)
Proof that you cannot participate independently in public life, such as a certificate from your general practitioner, hospital, nursing home, or care service
Your old identity card or old passport, if available
If applying through a representative: proof of authorization, such as a power of attorney or guardian certificate
If applying through a representative: identity document of the representative, such as an identity card or passport
processingTime: 2-3 weeks

bookingInfo.office: All citizen service offices (Bürgerämter) in Berlin

name: ID Card - Report Loss
description: A service to report the loss of your German ID card (Personalausweis) in person at a Berlin citizen office.
eligibility: You must appear in person to report the loss — only you can do this yourself. You must have your primary residence registered in Berlin, or at minimum a secondary residence in Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Application for a new ID card
processingTime: A few minutes

bookingInfo.office: This service is available at all citizen offices (Bürgersprechstelle) in Berlin.

name: Identity Card - Report of Finding Your Own Identity Card
description: A service for reporting the recovery of your lost or provisional German identity card (Personalausweis) to Berlin authorities.
eligibility: You must have found your previously lost identity card or provisional identity card. You must appear in person — the report can only be made on-site and only by you personally. You must be a resident of Berlin and registered there, though a second residence in Berlin is sufficient.
requiredDocuments: Report form for finding of identity card (must be completed in person on-site)
The recovered identity card
processingTime: A few minutes

bookingInfo.office: This service can be used at all citizen offices (Bürgerämter) in Berlin.

name: Pick up ID card (Personalausweis)
description: This service allows you to collect your newly issued German ID card (Personalausweis) in person from a Berlin citizen's office.
eligibility: You must pick up your ID card in person, though you may authorize another person in writing to collect it on your behalf (a power of attorney is only required if collecting a child's card and the child is 16 years or older). You can optionally check the processing status online by providing your date of birth and the serial number if you were given one. You may register your email address to receive a pickup notification.
requiredDocuments: Old ID card (if available) — please bring your previous ID card if you still have it; if it has been lost in the meantime, you must file a loss report in person to receive the new card
PIN letter for activating the online ID function (eID) (optional)

Power of attorney declaration for ID card pickup (if someone else is collecting on your behalf — only official power of attorney forms are accepted, and the representative must also provide identification)
processingTime: Approximately 10 minutes

bookingInfo.office: Pick up your ID card from the office where you applied for it. Pickup is available at all Berlin citizen's offices (Bürgerämter) without requiring a prior appointment booking, though some locations optionally offer appointment scheduling. Newly naturalized persons who applied for their ID card at Sellerstraße can pick it up at the 'Bürgeramt Klosterstraße - Document Pickup' location.

name: Request a National ID Card (Personalausweis)
description: This service allows German citizens and certain other residents to apply for a national identity card (Personalausweis) at Berlin citizen offices.
eligibility: German citizenship required. Personal attendance is mandatory for the applicant and any minors at the time of application. For minors under 16 years old, legal guardians must submit the application and the child must be present. Residence in Berlin with registration is required; a secondary residence (Nebenwohnsitz) in Berlin may be accepted if there is an important reason, but costs more. Exceptions apply for homeless persons, those temporarily in Berlin, tourists, and Germans with residence abroad — these applicants must apply at the State Office for Civic and Administrative Affairs (Landesamt für Bürger- und Ordnungsangelegenheiten).
requiredDocuments: One current, digital biometric passport photo (new regulation as of 01.05.2025); biometric photos must be created digitally at citizen offices (Bürgerämter) or certified photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic means
Religious head covering documentation if applicable to your religious community
Your old document, if available (even if expired or invalidated)
Your valid identity document, if available (for example, your Personalausweis or old passport)

Vital records document (Personenstandsurkunde) such as birth certificate, marriage certificate, or registered partnership certificate if you have never had an identity document before or if your personal information differs from the registration office records

Consent declaration and ID document of an absent legal guardian if applying for a minor's ID card (required if both parents have custody, are not separated, and one parent is absent; not required if you have sole custody or both parents are present)

Foreign passport or ID card from your previous nationality, or identity certificate from the State Office for Immigration (LEA), if you were naturalized and are applying for German documents for the first time
Naturalization certificate, if you were naturalized and are applying for German documents for the first time
fees: €27.60 for applicants under 24 years old; €46.00 for applicants 24 years or older; €13.00 additional if Berlin is your secondary residence; €6.00 additional for biometric photo creation on-site; €15.00 additional for direct mail delivery
processingTime: Approximately 3 to 4 weeks on average. Processing may take significantly longer in individual cases — please inquire when submitting your application. For urgent cases, you can additionally apply for a temporary national ID card (see further information).

bookingInfo.office: This service is available at all citizen offices (Bürgerämter) in Berlin. For applicants not registered in Berlin, applications must be submitted at the State Office for Civic and Administrative Affairs (Landesamt für Bürger- und Ordnungsangelegenheiten).

name: ID Card for Persons Not Registered in Berlin, Tourists, and Germans Living Abroad
description: This service issues a German national ID card (Personalausweis) to German citizens who are not registered in Berlin, are tourists, or reside outside Germany.
eligibility: You must possess German citizenship. Personal appearance at the office is required in all cases. For applicants under 16 years of age, the application must be submitted by the legal guardian (typically both parents).
requiredDocuments: 1 current digital biometric passport photo (new regulation effective 01.05.2025) — Biometric passport photos for travel and ID documents may only be created digitally directly at the authority (LABO) or at certified photo studios and transmitted via a secure electronic channel

Declaration of consent from an absent legal guardian — If a custodian does not appear in person, their written consent with signature and the original ID card/passport document are required. If no document is available, the signature on the declaration must be notarized. Contact your responsible city administration or German diplomatic mission beforehand
Your current ID card, or if unavailable, your passport (even if already expired)
Information sheet for Germans living abroad

Civil registry document (birth certificate or marriage certificate) — Required only if there are discrepancies from previous entries, such as a name change through marriage. If you are a member of a religious community required by its rules to wear head coverings in public, you must provide credible evidence of this at the first application

Proof of residence abroad (if applicable) — Not all countries have a registration requirement. Depending on your place of residence, different options may apply. Check the websites of German diplomatic missions beforehand to avoid unnecessary delays
fees: €27.60 for applicants up to 24 years old; €46.00 for applicants over 24 years old; €57.60 (€27.60 ID card + €30.00 jurisdiction fee) for applicants up to 24 years old; €76.00 (€46.00 ID card + €30.00 jurisdiction fee) for applicants over 24 years old; €40.60 (€27.60 ID card + €13.00 jurisdiction fee) for applicants up to 24 years old; €59.00 (€46.00 ID card + €13.00 jurisdiction fee) for applicants over 24 years old
processingTime: Collection possible after approximately 4 weeks

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details

name: Apply for Temporary ID Card (Personalausweis)
description: A service to apply for a temporary German ID card for residents with German citizenship who are registered or temporarily residing in Berlin.
eligibility: German citizenship required. Personal appearance is mandatory for the applicant (including minors). For minors under 16 years old, legal guardians must submit the application and the child must be present. Residency in Berlin is required (registered address). A secondary residence in Berlin may suffice if there is an important reason, though this incurs additional fees. The service is also available for people without fixed housing in Berlin, those temporarily staying in Berlin but registered elsewhere, and tourists. Non-Berlin residents and those applying for special circumstances should apply exclusively at the State Office for Citizens' and Regulatory Affairs.
requiredDocuments: One current, digital biometric passport photo (new regulation from 01.05.2025)
Documentation of religious headwear exemption (if applicable)
Old document (if available)
Valid document if applicable (such as old passport or existing ID card)
Birth certificate, marriage certificate, or registered partnership certificate (if you have never had an ID document or if your personal details differ from the registration office records)
Passport or ID card of previous nationality or identity certification from the State Office for Immigration (LEA) if you were naturalized
Naturalization certificate (if applicable)
fees: €10.00 for the temporary ID card; €13.00 additional if Berlin is your secondary residence; €6.00 additional for biometric photo creation on-site.
processingTime: Issuance is generally possible immediately once the applicant's identity is established.

bookingInfo.office: The service can be used at all citizen offices (Bürgerämter) in Berlin if you are registered with a residence address in Berlin.

name: Temporary Passport (ID Card), for Berlin Residents Without Fixed Residence or Persons Registered Outside Berlin
description: A temporary identity document for German citizens without a fixed address in Berlin or those registered outside Berlin who require personal identification.
eligibility: You must be a German citizen; personal appearance is required in all cases; for minors under 16 years old, the application must be submitted by the legal guardian, typically both parents.
requiredDocuments: 1 current biometric passport photo (new rules apply as of May 1, 2025); biometric photos may only be created digitally directly at the authority (LABO) or at certified photo studios

Declaration of consent from a guardian if they cannot attend in person; if the guardian is not present, written consent signed by them and the original ID/passport document is required; if no document is available, the signature on the declaration must be certified
Your current passport (ID card) if available, otherwise your travel document (even if expired)
Birth certificate or marriage certificate only if there have been changes from previous entries (for example, name change due to marriage)
If the passport holder belongs to a religious community that requires its members to wear head coverings, a certificate may be additionally required upon first application
fees: €10.00 for homeless persons; €23.00 (€10.00 ID + €13.00 processing fee for non-responsibility) for persons residing in the Federal Republic of Germany but outside Berlin
processingTime: Immediate, if all documents are provided

bookingInfo.office: Applications can only be submitted at the State Office for Citizenship and Regulatory Affairs (Landesamt für Bürger- und Ordnungsangelegenheiten).

name: Pawnbroking License – Application
description: A service to apply for a permit to operate a pawnbroking business, requiring proof of personal reliability, sound financial circumstances, and sufficient capital or collateral.
eligibility: Personal reliability verified through federal criminal record clearance (Führungszeugnis) and commercial register certificate; sound financial circumstances with no outstanding debts or known insolvency proceedings; proof of required capital or collateral for the first six months of operation; BundID account registration required for online applications.
requiredDocuments: Application for pawnbroking license permit (either online or paper form via post)
Identity document: valid passport, national ID card, or other official photo ID (not required for electronic applications); residency permit if applicant is not an EU citizen
Federal criminal record clearance (Bundeszentralregister – Führungszeugnis) for submission to authority (document type O), not older than three months
Commercial register certificate (Gewerbezentralregisterauszug) for submission to authority (document type 9), not older than three months
Information from the debtor registry (Zentrales Vollstreckungsportal) – request online

Bankruptcy register information: for natural persons resident in Berlin, two certificates required (one from local court for consumer insolvency, one from Charlottenburg District Court for standard insolvency); for legal entities and partnerships based in Berlin, contact Charlottenburg District Court, Amtsgerichtsplatz 1, 14057 Berlin; applicants with residence/business address outside Berlin should check competent insolvency court via central registry directory

Proof of required capital and collateral for at least the first six months of operation (bank guarantee or bank financing confirmation); must account for personnel, rent, equipment, furnishing, and insurance costs against expected income
Floor plan drawing of business premises (preferably at 1:100 scale)
Current commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) if company is registered; articles of association or bylaws if company is under formation
fees: €84.00 to €2,075.00 depending on extent of work required
processingTime: Approximately 1 month

bookingInfo.office: The competent district office (Ordnungsamt) responsible for the business location must receive the application. If the business location is not yet known, the application may be submitted to the district office responsible for the applicant's residence address.

name: Seizure for Ordinary Monetary Claims or Maintenance Claims with a Seizure and Transfer Order
description: A service for creditors to obtain a court order seizing funds from a third party (such as an employer or bank) to satisfy monetary or maintenance claims against a debtor.
eligibility: You must have a valid enforcement title (such as a court judgment, enforcement order from a dunning procedure, cost assessment decision, court settlement, or notarial deed) with an enforcement clause. The enforcement title must have been served on the debtor before enforcement begins. You must submit your application in writing to the competent enforcement court using the prescribed forms. You must specify the third debtor (the person, company, authority, or financial institution owing money to the debtor) with exact name, address, and file reference. You must clearly describe the debtor's claim against the third debtor. For maintenance claims, you must state the debtor's marital status and, if applicable, the number of dependent children. You must also specify how the seizure and transfer order should be served on the debtor.
requiredDocuments: Written application using the prescribed forms according to the Enforcement Forms Regulation (ZVFV)
Original enforcement title with enforcement clause and proof of service
Proof of service of the enforcement title on the debtor (for non-judicial enforcement titles)
List of your monetary or maintenance claims and enforcement costs with supporting documents
Personal identification document (passport or ID card with registration certificate) if submitting application in person at the court's legal application office
fees: €24.00 for the court decision on your application; plus additional costs charged by the court bailiff for serving the seizure and transfer order
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The competent enforcement court is determined by the debtor's place of residence or, for businesses, by their place of business.

name: Plant Protection Certification Certificate Application
description: Apply for a plant protection certification certificate demonstrating competence in safe pesticide handling and application.
eligibility: You must meet one of the following: (1) Passed a plant protection competence examination with a certificate; (2) Completed a recognized vocational qualification such as gardener, florist, farmer, or forester; (3) Hold a vocational training or university degree with a certificate from your institution confirming plant protection knowledge and skills were taught and examined; (4) Hold a plant protection certification from another EU member state or recognized foreign country (contact the plant protection office for special conditions); (5) Possess sufficient German language skills to understand and correctly apply pesticide instructions; (6) Complete mandatory continuing education every 3 years if actively engaged in plant protection work, or within 3 years before resuming such work if inactive for more than 3 years.
requiredDocuments: Application for plant protection certification (online or using the form; documents in PDF, JPG, PNG or ZIP format required for online submission)
Certificate or diploma of your professional, vocational, or university qualification demonstrating plant protection competence
Certificate confirming required knowledge and skills (only if required skills were taught in a training program not on the list of recognized qualifications)
Proof of continuing education participation (current attendance certificate less than 3 years old, if more than 3 years have passed since your original qualification)
Cost coverage declaration (informal statement with full billing address, if employer or third party covers fees)
Certified translation of foreign documents (if professional or academic qualifications were obtained abroad and documents are in a foreign language)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Submit your application to the plant protection office responsible for your primary residence.

name: Plant Protection Products — Notification Consultation and Application
description: A registration and notification service for individuals with valid plant protection product expertise to report their consulting and application activities.
eligibility: Valid Plant Protection Product Expertise Certificate required. Only persons who possess a valid expertise certificate for the application of plant protection products and for providing plant protection advice are permitted to apply plant protection products or provide plant protection consulting. The registration number of the expertise certificate must be entered on the form. NOTE: If you have not yet applied for an expertise certificate, you must do so at the plant protection service responsible for your primary residence. Further information can be found in the service description Plant Protection Product Expertise Certificate.
requiredDocuments: Application form (completed and signed) — Please fill out the form on a computer if possible and submit it signed to the Plant Protection Office.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Responsible office is the Plant Protection Office, located within the Senate Department for the Environment, Transport and Climate Protection. Email: pflanzenschutzamt@senuvk.berlin.de

name: Pesticide Product - Sales Registration Notification
description: This service allows individuals with valid pest control expertise certification to register for the commercial sale of pesticide products in Berlin.
eligibility: Valid pest control expertise certification (Sachkundenachweis) is required. Only persons holding a valid Sachkundenachweis for the dispensing of pesticide products may trade in them. The registration number of the Sachkundenachweis must be entered on the form. If you have not yet applied for a Sachkundenachweis, you must do so with the plant protection service responsible for your primary residence. Persons who distribute pesticide products via the Internet outside of a commercial activity must be qualified, but do not need to complete this registration procedure.
requiredDocuments: Completed application form (to be filled out on computer if possible and signed before submission to the Plant Protection Office Berlin)
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Plant Protection Office (Pflanzenschutzamt), located within the Senate Administration for Urban Development and the Environment. Email: pflanzenschutzamt@senuvk.berlin.de

name: Care Residential Communities — Annual Report Submission
description: An annual reporting requirement for operators and residents responsible for self-managed or provider-managed care residential communities to submit updates on January 31st of the following year.
eligibility: You must submit a report if you live in a self-managed care residential community and hold responsibility for it, or if you are the primary service provider in a provider-managed or intensive care residential community and hold responsibility for it. The deadline is February 15th of the following year. Submissions are only required if changes have occurred compared to the initial report or previous year snapshot report. Former 'bestandswohngemeinschaften' (existing communities) must now self-classify their category. Self-managed care communities require structural independence of residents from service providers, free choice and switching of providers, and full resident determination of communal living and daily activities. Provider-managed care communities require a nursing service as responsible provider and no more than two such communities of the same provider in immediate proximity. Intensive care communities serve at least two individuals requiring extra-clinical intensive care or provide care to at least two such individuals, and are always considered provider-managed.
requiredDocuments: Annual report for care residential communities (reporting date December 31st); documents must be in PDF, JPG/JPEG, or PNG format with individual files not exceeding 5 MB and total submission size not exceeding 30 MB

Personnel deployment plan (for provider-managed and intensive care communities only), showing the number of personnel to be deployed, particularly care and support staff, and how services will be staffed
User list (optional); you may submit a list of residents and their legal representatives living in the community on the reporting date

Documentation of legal relationships of the founder, service provider, and/or room provider if changes have occurred; examples include commercial register excerpts, association register excerpts, and cooperation agreements

Room inventory (if changes occurred); the form must document room types, location, number and size of rooms, planned occupancy of user rooms (planned capacity) broken down by target group; for self-managed communities: only if room usage, location, quantity, size, or planned occupancy changed from previous year; for provider-managed and intensive care communities: only if changes occurred in room usage, location, quantity, size, planned occupancy, or allocation by target groups (people with dementia, people with severe neurological damage (persistent vegetative state) phase F, long-term ventilated persons)
Concept of service provision (for provider-managed and intensive care communities only; required if changes occurred)

Qualification documentation of the lead contact person (for provider-managed and intensive care communities only; required if the lead contact changed); must show at least three-year professional training or university degree, business management qualification or nursing/social care/social pedagogy qualification, and professional history (without curriculum vitae for data protection reasons) documenting at least two years of management experience in a stationary facility, ambulatory service, or comparable facility

Qualification documentation of the responsible nursing specialist (for provider-managed and intensive care communities only; required if the responsible nursing specialist changed); must show at least three-year professional training, professional history (without curriculum vitae for data protection reasons) documenting two years of practical professional experience in the trained profession within the last eight years before further training, and further training for management functions with minimum 460 hours plus any additional specialized training certifications (e.g. in geriatric psychiatry/psychiatry)

Sample rental contract (for provider-managed and intensive care communities only; required if rental contracts for the community changed in content or landlord address details since the last annual report submission)

Sample care and support contracts (for provider-managed and intensive care communities only; required if care and support contracts or other service contracts or agreements between the responsible service provider and residents changed since the last annual report submission, such as changes to the primary service provider or contract content)

Community agreements (for provider-managed and intensive care communities only; required if changes occurred); if applicable, must include community house rules, community agreements, or other agreements between residents that have changed
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Guardianship for Unknown Parties - Appointment
description: This service allows you to request the court appointment of a guardian to handle a legal matter when the parties involved are unknown.
eligibility: The involved party in the legal matter to be regulated is unknown. The regulation of the matter must be necessary (demonstrated care need).
requiredDocuments: Written application
Justification describing the matter and the care need

Documentation of your own investigative efforts - you must have attempted to identify the unknown parties yourself, for example through the State Resident Registration Office (Landeseinwohneramt) or the Registry Office (Standesamt)
fees: The court charges fees for conducting the guardianship. Additionally, there is compensation for the guardian's activities.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The District Court (Guardianship Court) with jurisdiction in the district where the matter is to be regulated is responsible.

name: Sampler - Request Public Appointment and Oath
description: This service allows qualified professionals to apply for official appointment and oath as a sampler (Probenehmer/in) in Berlin, subject to demonstration of expertise, professional experience, and reliability.
eligibility: You must have acquired significantly above-average expertise through training and professional experience; you must have performed expert services in your field for several years; you must be psychologically and physically capable of fulfilling the requirements for experts in your field; there must be no doubt about your independence and objectivity, you must live in orderly economic circumstances, and be impartial and independent; additional requirements apply according to the expert regulations of the relevant chamber and the appointment prerequisites for your field of expertise.
requiredDocuments: Application for consultation meeting according to § 38 GewO and contact form for interested parties for public appointment and oath according to § 36 GewO with the Berlin Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IHK Berlin)
Curriculum vitae with biometric passport photo and detailed information about how you acquired above-average knowledge in the field of expertise for which public appointment is requested
Complete documentation of professional activity to date
List of all expert reports from the last three years (work samples)

Certified copies or photocopies of all relevant diplomas, certificates, credentials (e.g., professional designations), employment documentation, etc. (originals may be presented simultaneously or certified on-site by IHK staff)
Certificate of Conduct (Führungszeugnis) for submission to a government agency, not older than three months
Certificate of tax clearance (Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung) from the responsible tax office
Statement from insolvency register (may require up to two certificates for Berlin residents depending on employment status)
Employer release declaration (Freistellungserklärung) if employed, in civil service, or in military service
Reference list with at least five persons who can provide information about your personal suitability and specialist expertise
Attendance certificates from continuing education courses in the last three years
Proof of attendance at least three seminars on necessary knowledge for drafting expert reports, court procedure, dealing with private clients, and liability and insurance matters
List of own publications (if applicable)
fees: 1,000.00 to 3,000.00 euros; approximately 2,500.00 euros plus additional costs for expert committees
processingTime: The required reviews are comprehensive and typically take approximately six to twelve months.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Disposal of Illegal Waste (Problemstoffe)
description: A service for reporting and arranging disposal of illegally dumped waste in Berlin.
eligibility: Report of illegal waste by telephone, in writing, or electronically.
requiredDocuments: Complaint containing: location and time of dumping; volume of waste; person responsible (if known); personal data of the person reporting
fees: Free of charge; fees may apply to the person responsible for the illegal dumping.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Apply for Project and Reading Series Literature Funding
description: This service provides financial support for literature projects and reading series organized by Berlin-based individuals, groups, or small publishers.
eligibility: Applicants must have their primary residence or main office in Berlin, with the majority of project participants living and working in Berlin. Eligible publishers (publication projects) must have annual revenue not exceeding €100,000 and no more than three permanent employees. Literature journals are eligible. The maximum funding amount is €25,000 per year. Anniversary celebrations and primarily internal association events are excluded. Only one application per institution, group, or individual per funding cycle is allowed; if multiple applications are submitted by the same applicant, only the most recent is considered. Multiple participations in different projects are possible. For umbrella institutions with multiple locations or departments, one application per location/department is permitted. Applications including all required attachments must be submitted in German. Students and projects involving students are not eligible. Only projects that have not yet begun may be funded; this applies only to the project currently requested for the funding year, which is formally treated as a new project.
requiredDocuments: Project description (detailed description including information about project participants and curriculum vitae, and if applicable project specification)
Financing plan
Proof of Berlin residency
Confirmation of presentation/event venue
If applicable: Declaration of group association
processingTime: 6 months

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Apply for Project Funding from the Capital Culture Fund
description: This service allows cultural organizations, groups, and individuals to apply for project funding from Berlin's Capital Culture Fund (Hauptstadtkulturfonds) for projects of national and international relevance.
eligibility: Applications are accepted until 15 April 2026 at 14:00 (submissions after this deadline will not be accepted). Only one application per institution/group/individual is permitted per call. Projects must have national and international relevance, be developed and premiered/opened in Berlin, and be relevant to audiences or professionals beyond Berlin. At least four performances or events in Berlin are required. Projects must not have started yet. Appropriate fee levels for artists must be reflected in the budget plan. Applicants must ensure accessible offerings for people with disabilities and consider ecological sustainability. Prior public funding is expected for applicants in theatre, dance, and music. Applicants must be exmatriculated at the time funds are awarded (though they may still be enrolled at application).
requiredDocuments: Application for funding through the Capital Culture Fund (HKF) — submitted online only
Detailed project description
Detailed budget plan
Confirmation of presentation venue/performance space and accessibility status
Artistic background/CV
Project specification
Optional: Description of maximum 2 selected previous projects and project involvements
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Apply for Project Funding in Jazz
description: This service allows jazz musicians and ensembles based in Berlin to apply for project-based funding from the Berlin Senate.
eligibility: Applications are open from 03.08.2026 to 14.09.2026, with the deadline at 14:00 on 14.09.2026. Only one application per applicant is permitted. The project must not have started yet and must take place in Berlin. Applicants must be registered with their primary residence in Berlin (for legal entities/institutions, the headquarters must be in Berlin; for groups, more than 50% of members must be registered in Berlin; for duos, both members must have their primary residence in Berlin). Non-EU citizens can apply if their valid residence permit or residence rights certificate includes a work authorization note. The funded project cannot receive simultaneous funding from other Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion programs, including programs from the Initiative Neue Musik e.V. and Musicboard Berlin GmbH. Applicants must not be enrolled in regular study programs or pursuing doctorates at the time of application, during the selection process, or during the funding period. If studies ended recently, proof of completion must be provided.
requiredDocuments: Application for Jazz Project Funding (submitted online only; attachments accepted in XLSX, PDF, JPG, PNG, MP3 formats only)
Identity proof (mandatory attachment; max. 5 MB; PDF, JPG, PNG)
Proof of primary residence in Berlin (mandatory attachment; max. 5 MB; PDF, JPG, PNG)
Residence permit or residence rights certificate for non-EU citizens (mandatory if applicable; max. 5 MB; PDF, JPG, PNG)
Detailed project description (mandatory attachment; max. 8 DIN A4 pages including cover sheets and/or images; max. 5 MB; PDF)
Confirmation from at least one venue (mandatory attachment; use the template venue confirmation form; max. 5 MB; PDF)
Detailed financing plan (mandatory attachment; use the template financing plan; max. 5 MB; XLSX)
Artistic CV of artistic director and information about project-involved musicians (mandatory attachment; max. 5 MB; PDF)
Portfolio of previous artistic work (optional attachment; max. 5 MB; PDF)
Audio sample (mandatory attachment; max. 6 MB; MP3)
GbR contract for group applications (mandatory if applicable; upload signed contract copy or completed artist collaboration declaration; max. 5 MB; PDF)
Extract from association or commercial register for legal entities (mandatory if applicable; max. 5 MB; PDF)
processingTime: 7–8 months

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Apply for Project Funding in Interfaith and Secular Cooperation
description: This service provides grants for organizations and networks engaged in interfaith and secular dialogue and cooperation projects in Berlin.
eligibility: Applications accepted until 30 September 2026. Eligible applicants include religious or secular worldview organizations, interfaith dialogue and understanding networks, and civil society organizations in combination with these. Your organization's bylaws or rules of procedure must contain a clear religious or worldview commitment, or demonstrate the interfaith dialogue and understanding network. Projects must take place primarily in Berlin, have clear relevance to Berlin, be visible in Berlin, and have sustainable impact on city society. Results must be publicly accessible. Projects must be non-profit and serve the common good, complying with principles of the free democratic basic order. Minimum funding is €30,000 and maximum €100,000 per project per fiscal year. You must provide at least 10% of total costs as your own funds. Projects cannot replace existing publicly implemented or funded services. The project must not have started yet. Organizations must be registered in Berlin's Transparency Database.
requiredDocuments: Application for funding in interfaith and secular cooperation (submit online with all attachments)
Current bylaws or community regulations as applicable
Current register extracts
Tax treatment documentation or tax exemption certificate from the financial authority
Proof of authorization of signatory, or power of attorney if applicable
Financial plan with attachments
Third-party funding confirmation if applicable
processingTime: 4–5 months

bookingInfo.office: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

name: Prostitution Vehicle - Reporting Setup
description: A service for registering the placement of a licensed prostitution vehicle at a specific location with the appropriate local authority.
eligibility: You must hold a valid license to operate a prostitution business; the setup location and operating hours must meet legal requirements for the protection of all involved; you and any representative must be at least 18 years old.
requiredDocuments: Notice of prostitution vehicle setup (can be submitted online or by post) containing: vehicle owner's full name and operator's full name, vehicle or ship registration number, exact setup location, duration of setup, and operating hours

Copy of prostitution business license with operational concept demonstrating adequate interior space, appropriate furnishings, doors that can be opened from inside at all times, technical provisions for emergency assistance, appropriate sanitary facilities, valid operational approval, and vehicle in technically operational condition; copy of deputy authorization if applicable
Copy of registration certificates/alias certificates for all sex workers expected to work in the vehicle
Copy of agreements/contracts with sex workers regarding vehicle use
Current photos of the prostitution vehicle (exterior and interior views)
Proof of valid operational approval and technical operational readiness (such as copy of latest vehicle inspection, copy of registration certificate part I, service booklet, or similar)
processingTime: Approximately 2 weeks

bookingInfo.office: Submit the notice to the responsible local authority office (Ordnungsamt) in the district where the vehicle will be stationed.

name: Permit for Operating a Sex Work Business
description: A permit application for individuals or organizations seeking authorization to operate a sex work establishment or vehicle in Berlin, subject to personal reliability checks and minimum facility standards.
eligibility: Applicants must be at least 18 years old. Personal reliability is assessed through background checks, including a certificate of conduct from the Federal Criminal Register, a commercial register extract, and a statement from the relevant police authority. Sex work establishments must meet minimum requirements including: rooms used for sexual services must not be visible from outside, must have an appropriate emergency call system, doors must be openable from inside at all times, and must not be used as living or sleeping quarters. Facilities must have adequate sanitary equipment, appropriate rest and break areas, and individually lockable storage for personal items. Sex work vehicles must have sufficient interior space, appropriate interior fittings, doors openable from inside at all times, technical provisions to reach help at any time, adequate sanitary equipment, valid vehicle registration, and be in proper technical condition. Rooms used for sex work events must meet the same minimum requirements as establishments.
requiredDocuments: Application for permit under § 12 of the Prostitute Protection Act (ProstSchG) (see Forms section)
Personal identification document: passport or other official photo ID; residence permit if applicant is not an EU citizen
Certificate of conduct from the Federal Criminal Register (document type O) not older than three months

Commercial register extract for natural persons (document type 9) not older than three months, to be requested from the resident's municipality or any Berlin citizen office and sent directly to the competent administrative office
Commercial register extract for legal entities (document type 9) to be requested from the competent administrative office for the business location
Debtor register information from the Central Enforcement Portal

Operating concept detailing essential business features and measures to comply with the Prostitute Protection Act, including: typical organizational procedures and operating conditions for sexual services; measures ensuring no persons under 18 or trafficking victims under 21 work in the business; measures to reduce transmission risk of sexually transmitted infections; measures protecting health interests of sex workers and third parties; measures ensuring sex worker safety; and measures preventing presence of persons under 18
Floor plan drawing of buildings, rooms, vehicles, or mobile facilities for sex work and employee facilities (preferably at 1:100 scale)
Copy of rental agreement, purchase contract, or proof of valid vehicle registration for used buildings or vehicles
Current extract from the Commercial Register for registered businesses, or articles of association/bylaws for legal entities in formation
processingTime: Approximately 3 months

bookingInfo.office: The application must be submitted to the administrative office (Ordnungsamt) responsible for the business location.

name: Registration Certificate for Prostitution/Sex Work (Anmeldebescheinigung)
description: A registration certificate required for individuals aged 18 and older who wish to legally work in prostitution or sex work in Berlin, provided they have completed mandatory health counseling and meet residency requirements.
eligibility: Must be at least 18 years old at the time of registration. Registration certificate cannot be issued if the applicant is pregnant and in the final six weeks before delivery. Personal appearance is required. Applicants must have completed health counseling at the Berlin Center for Health Counseling (Berliner Zentrum für gesundheitliche Beratung) according to §10 ProstSchG and received a certificate of completion.
requiredDocuments: Valid personal identification document (Personalausweis, passport, passport substitute, or identification substitute with photograph). If you are a foreign national without freedom of movement rights, you must provide proof of German residence permit showing permission to work or pursue self-employment in Germany.
Certificate of health counseling according to §10 ProstSchG: proof of participation in health counseling conducted within the previous three months in Berlin.

Current registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung/Meldebestätigung) showing your residence or primary residence; alternatively, if you have no fixed residence in Germany, proof of a delivery address with written authorization from the person receiving mail at that address (form available).
Recent passport photograph: 45 millimeters high and 35 millimeters wide for the registration certificate.
processingTime: Typically issued immediately; otherwise within 5 working days, provided all required documents are complete.

bookingInfo.office: The District Office of Tempelhof-Schöneberg (Bezirksamt Tempelhof-Schöneberg) is responsible for issuing registration certificates for prostitution throughout Berlin.

name: Sex Work Registration Certificate Extension
description: This service allows adult sex workers in Berlin to extend their mandatory registration certificate, provided they have completed required health consultations and meet all eligibility requirements.
eligibility: You must be at least 18 years old. You cannot be in the last six weeks of pregnancy. You must appear in person. You must have completed a health consultation at the Berlin Center for Health Counseling according to §10 ProstSchG and have received a certificate documenting this.
requiredDocuments: Valid personal ID document (Personalausweis, passport, passport substitute, or ID substitute with photo)
German residence permit if you are a foreign national without freedom of movement

Proof of uninterrupted health consultations according to §10 ProstSchG (for persons 21 and over: proof of at least annual consultations; for persons under 21: proof of consultations at least every six months)

Current registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung) or confirmation of residence at main address, or if you have no fixed residence in Germany, proof of an alternative delivery address (with written authorization from the person receiving mail at that address)
Recent passport-style photo (45mm high and 35mm wide)
processingTime: Usually immediate

bookingInfo.office: For registration certificate extensions, the responsible office citywide is the registration authority Probea Berlin of the Tempelhof-Schöneberg district office (Bezirksamt Tempelhof-Schöneberg).

name: Sex Work/Prostitution – Health Counseling for Sex Workers
description: Health counseling service for sex workers in Berlin provided by the Tempelhof-Schöneberg Health Department.
eligibility: Must be 18 years of age or older at the time of registration.
requiredDocuments: Identity document (Personalausweis, passport, passport substitute, or ID card substitute with photo)
processingTime: Immediate

bookingInfo.office: Gesundheitliche Beratung für Prostituierte in Berlin (Health Counseling for Sex Workers in Berlin) – BeZeGeBePro (Berliner Zentrum für gesundheitliche Beratung nach §10 ProstSchG), operated by the Tempelhof-Schöneberg Health Department (Gesundheitsamt Tempelhof-Schöneberg)

name: Prostitution Event - Notification of Organization or Conduct
description: A notification service for operators with valid prostitution business permits to register the organization or conduct of prostitution events at designated venues.
eligibility: Valid permit for prostitution business operation required; the notifying person must hold a valid permit to operate a prostitution business. Suitability of venue required; the event venue and operating hours must meet statutory requirements for the protection of all involved parties. Age requirement; the notifying person and any representative must be at least 18 years old.
requiredDocuments: Notification of prostitution event (submitted online or using the official form, must include: full name of event operator, exact location and time of event, full name of property owner responsible for buildings, rooms, or other fixed or mobile facilities used)
processingTime: approximately 4 weeks

bookingInfo.office: The notification must be submitted to the responsible regulatory authority (Ordnungsamt) for the event location.

name: Apply for Legal Aid (Prozess- und Verfahrenskostenhilfe)
description: Financial assistance from the court to cover legal proceedings and court costs for eligible residents who cannot afford them.
eligibility: You must demonstrate a reasonable prospect of success in your legal claim; you cannot have alternative legal protection such as legal insurance or support from another party; you must not have someone else obligated by law to pay (such as a spouse or parents); your personal and financial circumstances must justify the assistance, and you must use your own income and assets first; the proceedings must not already be concluded; and your legal action must not be pursued frivolously.
requiredDocuments: Application for Legal Aid (Prozess- und Verfahrenskostenhilfe) — submitted in writing and substantiated by you or your authorized attorney
Declaration of Personal and Economic Circumstances — completed in full, dated, and signed by hand in German
Supporting documents and evidence of your personal and economic situation (copies) — specific required documents vary by case; refer to the information sheets and completion instructions provided
fees: No fees for the legal aid application proceeding itself; attorney costs depend on the individual case.
processingTime: Not stated on the page — check the official page for details.

bookingInfo.office: The court responsible for the legal aid application is the court where the proceedings are to be filed or are already pending.

name: Fire Safety Engineer - Establish Secondary Office
description: A service for recognized fire safety engineers in Berlin to establish a secondary office location in another German state.
eligibility: Must be recognized as a fire safety engineer (Prüfingenieur/in für Brandschutz) in the state of Berlin.
requiredDocuments: Informal application stating the address of the secondary office
Evidence of independent responsibility and autonomy at the secondary office; a copy of the partnership agreement or equivalent document
Information on the number and qualifications of staff participating in inspection activities
Information on the distance between the main office and secondary office or place of residence
Details on the time allocation of inspection activities between head office and secondary office
Explanation of measures to ensure proper building supervision
Consent declaration from the recognition authority of the state where the secondary office will be established (this will be arranged by the Berlin recognition authority)
processingTime: Processing depends on the consent declaration from the recognition authority of the other state and typically takes no longer than 8 weeks.
