name: Apply for Research Stipendium in Visual Arts
description: This is a research stipendium for visual artists and curators in Berlin who professionally exhibit their work and meet specific eligibility criteria.
eligibility: Applications are accepted from 26 January 2026 to 20 March 2026, with a deadline of 11:00 on 20 March 2026. Only one application per person is permitted, though applications are possible annually and previous applicants (e.g., for the 2024 stipendium) may reapply. You must live and work in Berlin. You must have completed artistic training and/or demonstrate several years of professional artistic or curatorial activity in visual arts. Only visual artists and curators who professionally present their work at visual arts venues (museums, exhibition spaces, project spaces, etc.) within exhibition contexts are supported. For artists working across multiple disciplines, the primary focus must be visual arts. Applications must be submitted in German (attachments may be in English). You may apply as an individual or as part of a group; newly formed groups are eligible and must confirm their membership with a joint declaration; existing groups require a GbR contract or declaration. For groups, more than 50% of members must have their primary residence registered in Berlin. You cannot be enrolled at a university (including doctoral studies) or employed as a professor at a university at the time of application or during the funding period. Concurrent applications for other stipendia are permitted, but you must disclose if you receive another award to verify compatibility; double funding with other Stiftung Kunstfonds stipendiums in the same funding year is excluded; combinations with project funding are permitted; and the stipendium is freely combinable with other domestic and international stipendiums not named here (verify their conditions separately).
requiredDocuments: Online application form for the Research Stipendium in Visual Arts

Artistic CV with portfolio (maximum 10 MB, PDF file, maximum 10 A4 pages in landscape format preferred) including photos or visual materials of completed works and exhibitions from the last three years; for film/video, include stills and descriptions with accessible links (e.g., Vimeo); for group applications, combine all CVs in one file with a maximum of 10 A4 pages total; no cover page required; application must contain both CV and portfolio sections

Identity document and proof of primary residence in Berlin: either a copy of both sides of your ID card (if it shows your registration address), or a copy of your passport/travel document plus registration certificate from the citizen registration office, or a copy of the registration confirmation from the citizen registration office; for non-EU citizens, also a copy of your residence permit or proof of residence rights (if not in passport)

Group membership declaration (for group applications only): either an existing GbR contract in copy, or a declaration of association signed by all group members confirming their artistic or curatorial collaboration; the declaration must be signed by all participating applicants and include proof of all members' registration addresses
processingTime: 4-5 months

Your intended legal action must not appear frivolous. Your personal and economic circumstances must be such that you cannot afford the necessary costs for legal advice or representation.

name: Travel Document - New Issuance
description: A travel document issued to foreign nationals who cannot reasonably obtain a passport from their country of origin and have lawful residence in Berlin.
eligibility: You must demonstrate that obtaining a passport or travel document from your country of origin is unreasonably difficult or impossible. This particularly applies if you have not been able to request issuance or renewal from your country's authorities despite timely effort and payment of required fees. Refugees recognized under the Geneva Refugee Convention or stateless persons recognized under the Statelessness Convention are generally considered to face insurmountable barriers to passport acquisition. You must have lawful residence status in Berlin (either already holding a residence title or obtaining it together with the travel document). You must have Berlin as your primary residence. You must attend an in-person appointment — request one at least 10 weeks before your current travel document expires by contacting the responsible department at LEA via the contact form.
requiredDocuments: 1 current biometric passport photo (Note: As of 1 May 2025, biometric photos must generally be created digitally only at government offices or professional photo studios and transmitted via secure electronic means — check the State Immigration Authority website before your appointment for current requirements)
Previous/current travel document

Naturalization confirmation and embassy certification from country of origin (only if you must surrender your national passport as part of a naturalization procedure or cannot obtain a new one for this reason)
Proof of primary residence in Berlin: either a residence registration certificate (Meldebestätigung) or a rental contract plus landlord's move-in confirmation
fees: Travel document issuance is always subject to fees, even for recipients of benefits under SGB II, SGB XII, or the Asylum Seeker Benefits Act. The full fee applies even if the application is rejected. Adults (24 and over): €100.00; Adults (24 and over) who are subsidiarily protected under § 4 Asylum Act or resettlement refugees under § 23(4) Residence Act: €70.00; Under 24 years: €97.00; Under 24 years who are subsidiarily protected under § 4 Asylum Act or resettlement refugees under § 23(4) Residence Act: €38.00.
processingTime: Approximately 4-6 weeks after your in-person appointment until the travel document is ready for collection.
